title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
山東鄉試錄序
萬曆壬午
詔有司復論士時御史黄〔應坤〕按
行山東則念曰齊魯之多士
也自昔記之矣〔應坤〕辱董兹
役其敢不脊簡以稱塞
明詔於是走幣徵〔應龍〕暨教諭郭
===
〔廷翰〕鄒〔浩宗〕葛〔亮渭〕徐〔商〕彭
〔英〕訓導陳〔大烈〕王〔一鵬〕解〔性〕
來典試事簾以外提調屬左
布政使楊〔一魁〕右叅政孫〔鋐〕
監試屬按察使蔡〔叔逵〕僉事
劉〔天秩〕它百執事咸具而御
史譏防矢毖斯往事有加乃
punctuated:
山東鄉試錄序

萬曆壬午，詔有司復論士。時御史黄〔應坤〕按行山東，則念曰：「齊魯之多士也，自昔記之矣。〔應坤〕辱董兹役，其敢不脊簡，以稱塞明詔？」於是走幣徵〔應龍〕，暨教諭郭〔廷翰〕、鄒〔浩宗〕、葛〔亮渭〕、徐〔商〕、彭〔英〕，訓導陳〔大烈〕、王〔一鵬〕、解〔性〕來典試事。簾以外，提調屬左布政使楊〔一魁〕、右叅政孫〔鋐〕，監試屬按察使蔡〔叔逵〕、僉事劉〔天秩〕，它百執事咸具。而御史譏防矢毖，斯往事有加。乃
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shandong Provincial Examination

In the renwu year of the Wanli era [1582], an imperial edict ordered the authorities to once again evaluate the scholars. At that time, Censor Huang Yingkun 黄應坤 was touring Shandong on inspection, and he reflected, saying: "That Qi and Lu abound in scholars has been recorded since antiquity. Having the honor of supervising this undertaking, how could I, Yingkun, dare not make selections with the utmost care [?] so as to fulfill the enlightened edict?" Thereupon, he dispatched gifts by courier to summon me, Yinglong, along with Instructors Guo Tinghan 郭廷翰, Zou Haozong 鄒浩宗, Ge Liangwei 葛亮渭, Xu Shang 徐商, and Peng Ying 彭英, and Assistant Instructors Chen Dalie 陳大烈, Wang Yipeng 王一鵬, and Xie Xing 解性, to come and take charge of the examination affairs. Outside the curtain, the duties of Proctor were assigned to Left Administration Commissioner Yang Yikui 楊一魁 and Right Administration Vice Commissioner Sun Hong 孫鋐; the supervision of the examination was assigned to Surveillance Commissioner Cai Shukui 蔡叔逵 and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Liu Tianzhi 劉天秩; and all the other hundred functionaries were fully in place. Moreover, the Censor guarded against irregularities and swore to exercise the utmost caution, surpassing previous occasions in this regard [?]. Then…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
三試提學副使蹇〔達〕所擇士
俾〔應龍〕等竭宵旦之力謹寧
可者得士七十有五人籍
奏之諸士且偕計吏上公車〔應〕
〔龍〕不佞以一日長諸士乃僭
告之曰自周以來易象春秋
在魯孔子講業洙泗之上齊
===
魯士益多彬彬焉漢興山東
大師竝出各名其家朝廷有
大議至使使就問經法云何
甘露間論石渠者亡慮數十
輩大氏皆齊魯士何其盛也
漢而下詞華浸競經術稍衰
我
punctuated: 三試提學副使蹇〔達〕所擇士，俾〔應龍〕等竭宵旦之力，謹寧可者，得士七十有五人，籍奏之。諸士且偕計吏上公車，〔應龍〕不佞，以一日長諸士，乃僭告之曰：「自周以來，《易象》、《春秋》在魯，孔子講業洙泗之上，齊、魯士益多彬彬焉。漢興，山東大師竝出，各名其家。朝廷有大議，至使使就問經法云何。甘露間，論石渠者亡慮數十輩，大氏皆齊、魯士，何其盛也！漢而下，詞華浸競，經術稍衰。我
translation_en:
… examined in three sessions the scholars selected by Education-intendant Surveillance Vice Commissioner Jian Da 蹇達, and charged Yinglong 應龍 and his colleagues to exhaust their strength night and day in carefully selecting those who met the standard [? 寧可], obtaining seventy-five scholars, whose roster was submitted to the throne.

As these scholars are about to accompany the fiscal-reporting officials in boarding the public carriages to the capital, I, Yinglong, though unworthy, by virtue of being slightly their senior, venture to address them, saying: "Since the Zhou dynasty, the Images of the Changes (Yi xiang) and the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) were preserved in Lu, and when Confucius lectured on his teachings along the Zhu and Si rivers, the scholars of Qi and Lu grew ever more refined and accomplished. With the rise of the Han, great masters of Shandong emerged side by side, each establishing his own school of learning. When the court held great deliberations, it even sent envoys to ask them what the canonical precedents prescribed. During the Ganlu era (53–50 BCE), those who debated at the Stone Canal Pavilion (Shiqu ge) numbered roughly several dozen men, and for the most part they were all scholars of Qi and Lu—how flourishing that was! From the Han onward, literary华丽 (floridness) gradually competed for prominence, and classical learning somewhat declined. Our…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
國家興學隆儒軼漢世遠甚聚
士壹本之六藝繇是方領矩
步之倫非墳策不譚而山東
固羣儒故里乃今覽諸士之
文離經析義闡論眇指推其
意且欲比肩游夏何論漢士
應龍以是益信齊魯之嫺於
===
經術所淵源遠矣然諸士亦
聞夫市珠者乎鄭人有市珠
于楚者悅其函珠之櫝而遺
其珠此可謂求櫝矣而非善
求珠者也夫六學者寄道之
匭櫝也是以先聖重之七十
子者流號通六藝彼其人皆
punctuated: 國家興學隆儒，軼漢世遠甚，聚士壹本之六藝。繇是方領矩步之倫，非墳、策不譚，而山東固羣儒故里。乃今覽諸士之文，離經析義，闡論眇指，推其意，且欲比肩游、夏，何論漢士？應龍以是益信齊、魯之嫺於經術，所淵源遠矣。然諸士亦聞夫市珠者乎？鄭人有市珠于楚者，悅其函珠之櫝而遺其珠，此可謂求櫝矣，而非善求珠者也。夫六學者，寄道之匭櫝也，是以先聖重之。七十子者流，號通六藝，彼其人皆
translation_en: … Dynasty has promoted schools and honored Confucian scholars, far surpassing the Han era, and in gathering scholars it bases everything solely on the Six Arts. Because of this, those who wear square-collared robes and walk with measured steps do not speak of anything other than the ancient classics and records, and Shandong is inherently the homeland of the great multitude of Confucian scholars. Now, reading the essays of the various candidates, I see how they dissect the Classics and analyze their meanings, expounding upon subtle principles; extending their aim, they would even wish to stand shoulder to shoulder with Ziyou 子游 and Zixia 子夏—what need is there even to mention the scholars of the Han? From this, I, Yinglong 應龍, am all the more convinced that the mastery of classical learning in Qi 齊 and Lu 魯 has deep and distant origins. Yet have the candidates also heard of the man who bought a pearl? There was a man of Zheng 鄭 who bought a pearl from a man of Chu 楚; delighted by the casket that held the pearl, he left the pearl behind. Such a man may be called a seeker of caskets, but he is not one who knows how to seek pearls. Now, the Six Disciplines of Learning are the caskets and boxes in which the Way is lodged, and for this reason the former sages attached great importance to them. Those of the fellowship of the Seventy Disciples were renowned for mastering the Six Arts, and as men they all…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
被服仁義而檢押節禮�co脅
肩赧色不嘗如臏以故孔氏
之道彌尊而經學滋重於世
漢史稱申公之弟子治官皆
有廉節稱其它諸儒著清名
者甚衆則其窮精畢力拾亡
苴漏以承絕學非苟焉而已
===
而今之藝士類耳剽口襲務
以華言取世資而曰吾姑羔
雉之此亦市櫝遺珠之喻也
嗟乎茲豈先聖之緒業
國家之科指其端若是哉僞浮
榮而忘本實即漢士恥稱之
安在其不詭于孔氏也善乎
punctuated: 被服仁義，而檢押節禮，co脅肩，赧色不嘗如臏，以故孔氏之道彌尊，而經學滋重於世。漢史稱申公之弟子治官皆有廉節稱，其它諸儒著清名者甚衆，則其窮精畢力，拾亡苴漏，以承絕學，非苟焉而已。而今之藝士，類耳剽口襲，務以華言取世資，而曰「吾姑羔雉之」，此亦市櫝遺珠之喻也。嗟乎！茲豈先聖之緒業、國家之科指其端若是哉？僞浮榮而忘本實，即漢士恥稱之，安在其不詭于孔氏也？善乎
translation_en: …clothed themselves in benevolence and righteousness and restrained themselves with moderation and ritual propriety. Toward [fawning with a?] hunched-shoulder demeanor [?], they blushed with shame as if they had suffered the kneecap-removal punishment. For this reason, the Way of Confucius (Kongshi 孔氏) grew ever more revered, and classical learning became increasingly valued in the world. The Han histories state that the disciples of Master Shen (Shengong 申公), in administering their offices, were all praised for their integrity and principle, and that among the other Confucian scholars, those who established pure reputations were very numerous. Thus, their exhausting their mental energy and exerting their utmost strength to gather what was lost and patch what was omitted in order to carry on interrupted learning was no mere perfunctory matter! Yet today's men of letters generally plagiarize by ear and copy by mouth, striving with華麗 flowery words to secure worldly advancement, while saying, "I am merely using this as my ritual gift of lamb or pheasant to gain entry." This, too, is an illustration of buying the casket and leaving behind the pearl. Alas! Could the legacy of the Former Sages and the aim of the dynasty's examination system have such an origin as this? Feigning superficial glory while forgetting fundamental substance—even the scholars of the Han would have been ashamed to speak of it; how then can one claim not to be at odds with Confucius? Well said indeed were…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
嚴太傅之言也凡通經術固
當修行先聖之道柰何追俗
以儌富貴其人至今稱之平
津創業金馬釋疏蹻而取公
卿而阿世苟合爲轅汲二子
所面詆諸士何居焉蓋孔子
周游不遇喟然有狂狷之思
===
夫以其嘐嘐道古介特而寡
與宜若不比于中行而聖人
亟稱之爲吾黨而思之乃若
愿人媚夫至不欲其一闚其
室豯斯以談士之賢不肖何
如也今諸士出聖人之黨言
必引古昔斐然狂簡豈少於
punctuated: 嚴太傅之言也：「凡通經術，固當修行先聖之道，柰何追俗以儌富貴？」其人至今稱之。平津創業金馬，釋疏蹻而取公卿，而阿世苟合，爲轅、汲二子所面詆。諸士何居焉？蓋孔子周游不遇，喟然有狂狷之思。夫以其嘐嘐道古，介特而寡與，宜若不比于中行，而聖人亟稱之爲「吾黨」而思之；乃若愿人媚夫，至不欲其一闚其室。豯斯以談，士之賢不肖何如也？今諸士出聖人之黨，言必引古昔，斐然狂簡，豈少於
translation_en:
… the words of Grand Tutor Yan [Yan Pengzu 嚴彭祖]: "Anyone who masters the classical arts ought certainly to cultivate and practice the Way of the Former Sages; how could one chase after vulgar trends to seek wealth and rank?" As a person, he is praised to this day. The Marquis of Pingjin [Gongsun Hong 公孫弘] began his career at the Golden Horse Gate, casting off coarse cloth and straw sandals to attain the rank of excellency or minister; yet he flattered the age and compromised for easy agreement, and was denounced to his face by the two gentlemen Yuan [Yuan Gu 轅固] and Ji [Ji An 汲黯]. Where do you scholars stand between these two?

Indeed, when Confucius traveled around without meeting a worthy ruler, he sighed and thought fondly of the ardently ambitious and the fastidiously upright. Now, because the ambitious grandiloquently speak of antiquity and the upright are fiercely independent and have few associates, they might seem not to measure up to those who walk the middle way; yet the Sage repeatedly called them "our party" and longed for them. As for the ostensibly honest men and sycophantic fellows [the "village worthies"], he went so far as not to wish them even once to peer into his chamber. Proceeding from this to discuss the matter [reading 豯 as 繇/由?], what does this show about the worthiness or unworthiness of scholars? Today you scholars come forth from the Sage's own home region; in speech you unfailingly cite antiquity, and in accomplished brilliance and ardent ambition, how are you any less than …

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
曩所云有如萬分一渝志隳
節與世湛浮甘自悖所聞而
猥託之乎中行不亦畔聖訓
甚吾黨之士乎嗟乎士貴重
地非以地重簪紳之裔容禮
有章衆不謂賢而一越檢軌
輒蒙世姍笑隤其家聲何則
===
其求之者備也今海內之重
諸士惟齊魯而其求多于諸
士亦惟齊魯諸士慎念之哉
第不愧齊魯士則不佞之責
塞矣是舉也兵部尚書凌〔雲〕
〔翼〕以總督漕運右副都御史
揚〔俊民〕以巡撫山東監察御
punctuated:
曩所云？有如萬分一渝志隳節，與世湛浮，甘自悖所聞，而猥託之乎中行，不亦畔聖訓、甚吾黨之士乎？嗟乎！士貴重地，非以地重。簪紳之裔，容禮有章，衆不謂賢；而一越檢軌，輒蒙世姍笑，隤其家聲。何則？其求之者備也。今海內之重諸士惟齊、魯，而其求多于諸士亦惟齊、魯，諸士慎念之哉！第不愧齊、魯士，則不佞之責塞矣。

是舉也，兵部尚書凌〔雲翼〕以總督漕運，右副都御史揚〔俊民〕以巡撫山東，監察御
translation_en:
… those mentioned in the past? If by a one-in-ten-thousand chance someone should alter his resolve and ruin his integrity, sinking or floating along with the age, willingly betraying what he has learned while basely claiming to follow the path of the mean—would this not be rebelling against the Sage's teachings and going even further than the scholars of "our party"? Alas! A scholar is valued because he adds weight to his homeland, not because he derives weight from his homeland. When the descendants of official families comport themselves with proper decorum and ritual, the multitude does not call them worthy; yet the moment they overstep the bounds of restraint, they immediately incur the ridicule of the world and ruin their family's reputation. Why is this? Because what is demanded of them is perfection. Today, within the seas, it is precisely as scholars of Qi and Lu that you gentlemen are held in high esteem, and it is likewise precisely as scholars of Qi and Lu that so much is demanded of you. May you gentlemen reflect on this with care! So long as you bring no shame to the name of scholars of Qi and Lu, my own responsibility shall have been fulfilled.

On the occasion of this examination, Minister of War Ling Yunyi 凌雲翼, serving as Supreme Commander of Grain Transport; Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Yang Junmin 揚俊民 [楊俊民], serving as Grand Coordinator of Shandong; Investigating Censor[s] …

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
史曹〔一夔〕林〔休徵〕以先後巡
鹽王〔國楫〕以印馬楊〔杜〕以巡漕
戶部主事李〔一鳳〕王〔宗伊〕程〔上〕
陳〔簡謙〕吳〔謹〕刑部郎中程〔元沐〕
工部郎中屠〔伯淵〕員外郎
劉〔玉麟〕主事馬〔棐〕皆有事
茲土布政司左參政王〔棐〕右
===
參政馬〔顧澤〕左參議成〔繼〕蘇
副使丘〔民牧〕右參議茹〔宗舜〕按察司
副使丘〔浙〕僉事吳〔之彥〕劉〔弘〕
都司署都指揮僉事任〔道自〕
嚴〔强〕郭〔慄〕董〔曉承祺〕皆有勞
于外右布政使翟〔繡裳〕副使
劉〔渾成〕署都指揮同知陳〔國〕
punctuated: 史曹〔一夔〕、林〔休徵〕以先後巡鹽，王〔國楫〕以印馬，楊〔杜〕以巡漕，戶部主事李〔一鳳〕、王〔宗伊〕、程〔上〕、陳〔簡謙〕、吳〔謹〕，刑部郎中程〔元沐〕，工部郎中屠〔伯淵〕、員外郎劉〔玉麟〕、主事馬〔棐〕，皆有事茲土；布政司左參政王〔棐〕、右參政馬〔顧澤〕、左參議成〔繼〕、蘇副使丘〔民牧〕、右參議茹〔宗舜〕，按察司副使丘〔浙〕、僉事吳〔之彥〕、劉〔弘〕，都司署都指揮僉事任〔道自〕、嚴〔强〕、郭〔慄〕、董〔曉承祺〕，皆有勞于外；右布政使翟〔繡裳〕、副使劉〔渾成〕、署都指揮同知陳〔國〕
translation_en: …[Investigating] Censors Cao Yikui 曹一夔 and Lin Xiuzheng 林休徵, successively serving as Salt-Control Censors; Wang Guoji 王國楫, serving as Horse-Branding Inspector; and Yang Du 楊杜, serving as Canal-Inspecting Censor; as well as Ministry of Revenue Secretaries Li Yifeng 李一鳳, Wang Zongyi 王宗伊, Cheng Shang 程上 [?], Chen Jianqian 陳簡謙 [?], and Wu Jin 吳謹; Ministry of Justice Director Cheng Yuanmu 程元沐 [?]; and Ministry of Works Director Tu Boyuan 屠伯淵, Vice Director Liu Yulin 劉玉麟, and Secretary Ma Fei 馬棐, were all on official duty in this region. Provincial Administration Commission Left Administration Vice Commissioner Wang Fei 王棐, Right Administration Vice Commissioner Ma Guze 馬顧澤, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Cheng Ji 成繼, Su [?] Vice Commissioner [?] Qiu Minmu 丘民牧 [?], and Right Assistant Administration Commissioner Ru Zongshun 茹宗舜; Surveillance Commission Vice Commissioner Qiu Zhe 丘浙, and Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Wu Zhiyan 吳之彥 and Liu Hong 劉弘 [?]; and Regional Military Commission Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Ren Daozi 任道自 [?], Yan Qiang 嚴强, Guo Li 郭慄, and Dong Xiaochengqi 董曉承祺 [?], all rendered service on the outside. Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Zhai Xiushang 翟繡裳, Vice Surveillance Commissioner Liu Huncheng 劉渾成, and Acting Vice Regional Military Commissioner Chen Guo… [Chen Guosi 陳國俟]…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
〔俟〕以齊
賀行都指揮僉事陸〔應元〕署都
指揮僉事檀〔武臣〕米〔萬春〕以
領班行左叅政徐〔元太〕按察
使李〔汝〕副使賈〔仁元〕王〔庭詩〕
僉事李〔淶〕署都指揮僉事梁
〔大任〕以遷秩行副使徐〔成位〕
===
以調任行布叅政蕭〔遹〕張〔崇〕
〔功〕曹〔于登〕雷〔以仁〕叅議岳〔汴〕
按察使李〔松〕周〔于德〕副使張
〔崇謙〕唐〔錬〕劉〔魯〕僉事靖〔四方〕
則各事于一方法得竝書云
河南河南府嵩縣儒學教諭
林〔應龍〕謹序
punctuated:
〔俟〕，以齊賀行；都指揮僉事陸〔應元〕、署都指揮僉事檀〔武臣〕、米〔萬春〕，以領班行；左叅政徐〔元太〕、按察使李〔汝〕、副使賈〔仁元〕、王〔庭詩〕、僉事李〔淶〕、署都指揮僉事梁〔大任〕，以遷秩行；副使徐〔成位〕，以調任行；布叅政蕭〔遹〕、張〔崇〕〔功〕、曹〔于登〕、雷〔以仁〕、叅議岳〔汴〕、按察使李〔松〕、周〔于德〕、副使張〔崇謙〕、唐〔錬〕、劉〔魯〕、僉事靖〔四方〕，則各事于一方，法得竝書云。
河南河南府嵩縣儒學教諭林〔應龍〕謹序。
translation_en:
… [Chen Guo]si 陳國俟 departed to present congratulations; Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Lu Yingyuan 陸應元 and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Tan Wuchen 檀武臣 and Mi Wanchun 米萬春 departed to lead the rotation troops; Left Administration Vice Commissioner Xu Yuantai 徐元太, Surveillance Commissioner Li Ru 李汝, Surveillance Vice Commissioners Jia Renyuan 賈仁元 and Wang Tingshi 王庭詩, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Li Lai 李淶, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Liang Daren 梁大任 departed upon promotion to new ranks; Surveillance Vice Commissioner Xu Chengwei 徐成位 departed upon transfer to another post; while Administration Vice Commissioners [?布叅政] Xiao Yu 蕭遹, Zhang Chonggong 張崇功, Cao Yudeng 曹于登, and Lei Yiren 雷以仁, Assistant Administration Commissioner Yue Bian 岳汴, Surveillance Commissioners Li Song 李松 and Zhou Yude 周于德, Surveillance Vice Commissioners Zhang Chongqian 張崇謙, Tang Lian 唐錬, and Liu Lu 劉魯, and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Jing Sifang 靖四方 were each engaged in duties in their respective localities; by precedent, all are entitled to be recorded together here.
Respectfully prefaced by Lin Yinglong 林應龍, Instructor in the Confucian School of Song County, Henan Prefecture, Henan.

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
定公問一言而可以興邦有諸孔子對曰
言不可以若是其幾也人之言曰爲君
難爲臣不易如知爲君之難也不幾乎
一言而興邦乎
子曰道不遠人人之爲道而遠人不可以
爲道
養心莫善於寡欲其爲人也寡欲雖有不
存焉者寡矣
===
易
六四至臨无咎象曰至臨无咎位當也六
五知臨大君之宜吉象曰大君之宜行
中之謂也
大壯利貞大者正也
子曰知變化之道者其知神之所爲乎
昔者聖人之作易也將以順性命之理是
以立天之道曰陰與陽立地之道曰柔
punctuated:
第壹場

四書：
定公問：「一言而可以興邦，有諸？」孔子對曰：「言不可以若是其幾也。人之言曰：『爲君難，爲臣不易。』如知爲君之難也，不幾乎一言而興邦乎？」
子曰：「道不遠人。人之爲道而遠人，不可以爲道。」
養心莫善於寡欲。其爲人也寡欲，雖有不存焉者，寡矣。

易：
六四：至臨，无咎。象曰：「至臨无咎」，位當也。六五：知臨，大君之宜，吉。象曰：「大君之宜」，行中之謂也。
大壯，利貞；大者正也。
子曰：「知變化之道者，其知神之所爲乎！」
昔者聖人之作《易》也，將以順性命之理。是以立天之道曰陰與陽，立地之道曰柔…
translation_en:
First Session

The Four Books (Sishu):
Duke Ding asked, "A single word that can make a state prosper—is there such a thing?" Confucius replied, "Words cannot have so near an effect as that. Yet there is a saying among people: 'To be a ruler is difficult; to be a minister is not easy.' If one understands the difficulty of being a ruler, does this not come close to a single word that can make a state prosper?" [Analects 13.15]
The Master said, "The Way is not far from human beings. When people pursue a way that distances them from human beings, it cannot be considered the Way." [Doctrine of the Mean 13]
"For nurturing the heart-mind, nothing is better than making desires few. If a person has few desires, although there may be some things in which the heart-mind is not preserved, they will be few." [Mencius 7B.35]

The Classic of Changes (Yi):
Six in the fourth place: "Approaching closely; no blame." The Commentary on the Images (Xiang) says: "'Approaching closely; no blame'—this is because the position is appropriate." Six in the fifth place: "Approaching with wisdom, fitting for a great ruler; auspicious." The Commentary on the Images says: "'Fitting for a great ruler' refers to practicing the mean." [Hexagram 19, Lin (Approach)]
"Great Strength (Dazhuang): it is advantageous to be steadfast and upright. That which is great is upright." [Commentary on the Judgments (Tuan), Hexagram 34, Dazhuang]
The Master said, "One who knows the way of change and transformation—does he not know what is done by the spirit-like power?" [Appended Remarks (Xici) I.9]
In ancient times, when the sages made the Changes (Yi), they intended thereby to accord with the principles of human nature and destiny. Therefore they established the way of Heaven, calling it yin and yang; they established the way of Earth, calling it the yielding… [Discussion of the Trigrams (Shuogua) 2]

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
與剛立人之道曰仁與義兼三才而兩
之故易六畫而成卦分陰分陽迭用柔
剛故易六位而成章
書
益曰吁戒哉儆戒無虞
三百里揆文教二百里奮武衛
籲俊尊上帝迪知忱恂于九德之行
夏暑雨小民惟曰怨咨冬祁寒小民亦惟
曰怨咨厥惟艱哉思其艱以圖其易民

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
問禮享帝享親揆文奮武所從來遠矣其
制至周始備今覩周禮禮經諸書所載
圜方異位祫禘異祭親賢齒貴異教蒐
苗獮狩異名匪直儀典蓋亦有精意焉
可縷指而陳之與漢唐誼主間有慕其
躅而舉之者受釐渭陽立廟郡國辟雝
祖割驪山講武班班簡編可鏡也抑于
古帝王有符合與
二祖初定天下釐正
===
鴻典
天
親介禧文武飭治其度越前代殊甚
皇上臨御祗事
郊
廟
親幸大學已又謁
山陵
閱營兵
punctuated: 問：禮，享帝享親，揆文奮武，所從來遠矣，其制至周始備。今覩《周禮》、《禮經》諸書所載，圜方異位，祫禘異祭，親賢齒貴異教，蒐苗獮狩異名，匪直儀典，蓋亦有精意焉，可縷指而陳之與？漢、唐誼主間有慕其躅而舉之者，受釐渭陽，立廟郡國，辟雝袒割，驪山講武，班班簡編，可鏡也。抑于古帝王有符合與？二祖初定天下，釐正鴻典，天親介禧，文武飭治，其度越前代殊甚。皇上臨御，祗事郊廟，親幸大學，已又謁山陵，閱營兵，
translation_en:
Question: In ritual, making offerings to the Supreme Lord and making offerings to one's ancestors, regulating civil affairs and rousing martial vigor—these practices have a very long history, and their institutional forms first became complete in the Zhou dynasty. Now, looking at what is recorded in the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), the Classic of Rites (Lijing), and other texts: the round mound and the square altar have different sites; the collective sacrifice (xia) and the great imperial sacrifice (di) are different sacrificial rites; honoring relatives, honoring the worthy, respecting age, and respecting noble rank involve different teachings; and the spring, summer, autumn, and winter hunts (sou, miao, xian, shou) go by different names. These are not merely ceremonial canons; rather, there is also subtle meaning in them. Can you point them out in detail and set them forth? Rightly-principled rulers of the Han and Tang dynasties occasionally admired the footsteps of the ancients and carried out such rites: receiving blessings at Weiyang, establishing ancestral temples in the commanderies and kingdoms, baring the arm to slice the sacrificial meats at the Imperial University (Biyong), and holding military reviews at Mount Li. These are clearly recorded in the historical annals and can serve as a mirror. Yet did they truly accord with the ancient emperors and kings?

When Our Two Progenitors [the Hongwu and Yongle Emperors] first pacified the realm, they rectified the great canons: receiving blessings from Heaven and the imperial ancestors, and ordering governance through both the civil and the martial, they surpassed previous dynasties to an extraordinary degree. Since His Majesty ascended the throne, he has reverently served at the suburban altars and the Imperial Ancestral Temple, personally visited the National University, and subsequently visited the imperial mausoleums and reviewed the troops of the capital training divisions, …

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
祖烈克紹
大禮其舉炳炳炳乎登三五軼漢唐矣顧所以
植仁孝之經而崇文武之本者諸士亦
可竊窺而揚厲之與夫敷章易浴精意
難合亦有因繁縟之觀究精微之蘊可
仰裨
丹扆萬一與簪筆而揚
主徽臣子責也諸士其毋隱毋蔓主司願聽焉
問今之襃衣博帶誦法先王者孰不以儒
===
自命哉儒之名安從昉也孔子對魯君
論儒行其說至詳第令士者循軌而趍
即名實不爽矣乃宋儒謂非孔子之言
也奚所指與孫卿著儒效篇謂有俗儒
大儒椎儒之辨可悉數而詳榷之與三
代而下儒莫盛於漢莫醇於宋兩漢書
所列儒林彬彬衆矣由今觀其人咸克
羽翼聖經綿延絕學顧尚論者多有瑕
舉試悉加評隲於孔氏所稱儒行何似
punctuated:
祖烈克紹，大禮其舉，炳炳炳乎登三、五，軼漢、唐矣！顧所以植仁孝之經，而崇文武之本者，諸士亦可竊窺而揚厲之與？夫敷章易浴，精意難合，亦有因繁縟之觀，究精微之蘊，可仰裨丹扆萬一與？簪筆而揚主徽，臣子責也。諸士其毋隱毋蔓，主司願聽焉。
問：今之襃衣博帶、誦法先王者，孰不以儒自命哉？儒之名安從昉也？孔子對魯君論《儒行》，其說至詳。第令士者循軌而趍，即名實不爽矣。乃宋儒謂非孔子之言也，奚所指與？孫卿著《儒效篇》，謂有俗儒、大儒、椎儒之辨，可悉數而詳榷之與？三代而下，儒莫盛於漢，莫醇於宋。《兩漢書》所列《儒林》，彬彬衆矣。由今觀其人，咸克羽翼聖經，綿延絕學，顧尚論者多有瑕舉。試悉加評隲，於孔氏所稱儒行何似？
translation_en:
…thus ably continuing the achievements of His Imperial Ancestors! With the performance of these grand rituals, how brilliantly He ascends to the level of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors and surpasses the Han and Tang dynasties! Yet as for the means by which the constant principles of benevolence and filial piety are established, and the foundations of civil and military governance are exalted, can you gentlemen also venture to glimpse into them and extol them? Now, outward ceremonial display is easy to become accustomed to [?], whereas the subtle essence is difficult to match; is there also a way, by examining the elaborate spectacle, to investigate its profound and subtle inner meaning, so as to respectfully aid the Imperial Throne even one part in ten thousand? To wear the official's brush in one's cap and proclaim the Sovereign's excellence is the duty of a subject. Gentlemen, neither conceal your thoughts nor ramble; the Examiners wish to hear your views.

Question: Among those today who wear broad robes and wide sashes and recite and model themselves upon the Former Kings, who does not style himself a Confucian scholar (ru)? Where did the name "Confucian" (ru) first originate? When Confucius replied to the ruler of Lu discussing the "Conduct of the Confucian" (Ruxing), his explanation was exceedingly detailed. If only scholars were made to follow its tracks and hasten along them, then name and reality would not fail to correspond. Yet the Song-dynasty Confucians claimed that these were not the words of Confucius; to what were they pointing? Sun Qing [Xunzi] wrote the chapter "On the Efficacy of the Confucian" (Ruxiao pian), stating that there is a distinction between the vulgar Confucian (suru), the great Confucian (daru), and the unrefined [for 雅 'refined'?] Confucian (zhuiru); can you enumerate them all and discuss them in detail? From the Three Dynasties onward, Confucians were never more flourishing than in the Han, and never more pure than in the Song. Those arrayed in the "Biographies of Confucian Scholars" (Rulin) in the two Books of Han (Liang Han shu) are an impressively refined multitude. Viewing these men from the present day, all were able to serve as wings to the sage's classics and perpetuate lost learning; yet those who evaluate figures of the past often point out their flaws. Try to thoroughly appraise them: how do they compare to the "conduct of the Confucian" spoken of by Confucius?

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
至宋史又以儒林道學各自爲傳夫舍
道學則安所名儒也將後世之言儒者
類失其實與即兩漢之儒亦尚有卓然
可稱者而史氏顧别爲著傳其又奚以
也漢宋諸儒未易軒輊說者乃謂漢士
實宋士浮其取舍將無失衷與
今天下儒術盛矣爾多士涵濡
道化又生齊魯之鄉夫求儒於齊魯猶掄駿
於冀北剖玉於崑岡也所爲循名責實
===
無愧前哲者當何如而後可昔人有云
儒貴名也不可以比周爭不可以夸誕
有也願試言之以觀尚友之學
問爲政不患有盜患弭盜難耳山以東非
古齊地哉太史公曰多劫人者大國之
風也蓋自古記之矣漢以弭盜稱者或
購賞捕斬或部衆掩擊或賣刀而馴渤
海或罷兵而平泰山率齊吏也其方略
孰爲得與
punctuated:
至《宋史》，又以《儒林》、《道學》各自爲傳。夫舍道學則安所名儒也？將後世之言儒者類失其實與？即兩漢之儒，亦尚有卓然可稱者，而史氏顧别爲著傳，其又奚以也？漢、宋諸儒未易軒輊，說者乃謂漢士實、宋士浮，其取舍將無失衷與？今天下儒術盛矣。爾多士涵濡道化，又生齊、魯之鄉。夫求儒於齊、魯，猶掄駿於冀北、剖玉於崑岡也。所爲循名責實、無愧前哲者，當何如而後可？昔人有云：「儒，貴名也，不可以比周爭，不可以夸誕有也。」願試言之，以觀尚友之學。
問：爲政不患有盜，患弭盜難耳。山以東非古齊地哉？太史公曰：「多劫人者，大國之風也。」蓋自古記之矣。漢以弭盜稱者，或購賞捕斬，或部衆掩擊，或賣刀而馴渤海，或罷兵而平泰山，率齊吏也。其方略孰爲得與？
translation_en:
As for the History of the Song (Songshi 宋史), it furthermore places the "Forest of Confucians" (Rulin 儒林) and the "Learning of the Way" (Daoxue 道學) into separate collective biographies. Yet if one sets aside the Learning of the Way, on what grounds can anyone be called a Confucian? Is it that those recorded as Confucians in later ages had generally lost the true substance of the name? Even among the Confucians of the Former and Later Han, there were still those of outstanding merit worthy of praise, yet the historians recorded their biographies elsewhere [outside the "Forest of Confucians"]—why was that? The Confucians of the Han and Song are not easily ranked one above the other, yet commentators claim that Han scholars were substantial while Song scholars were superficial; in choosing one over the other, have they not strayed from balanced judgment? Today, Confucian scholarship flourishes across the empire. You gentlemen have been steeped in the transformative influence of the imperial Way, and moreover were born in the land of Qi 齊 and Lu 魯. Seeking Confucians in Qi and Lu is like selecting fine steeds in northern Ji 冀 or cutting jade from Mount Kun 崑岡. If you are to match name with reality and feel no shame before the sages of the past, how must you conduct yourselves to succeed? A writer of old once said: "'Confucian' is a noble title; it cannot be won through factional partisanship, nor possessed through boastful pretense." I wish you to discuss this, so that I may observe your learning in befriending the ancients.

Question: In governance, the worry is not that bandits exist, but that suppressing bandits is difficult. Is not the region east of the mountains the ancient land of Qi? The Grand Historian (Taishigong 太史公, Sima Qian 司馬遷) said: "The prevalence of highway robbery is the custom of a great state." Indeed, this has been recorded since antiquity. In the Han dynasty, those renowned for suppressing bandits—whether by offering rewards to capture and execute them, marshaling troops for surprise attacks, having men sell their swords to tame Bohai 渤海, or disbanding troops to pacify Mount Tai 泰山—were generally officials serving in Qi. Which of their strategies was the most effective?

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
今天下綦隆而東省乃時有盜警當事者亟
申捕令矣輒捕輒竊發竟不衰止議者
大都在嚴保甲覈其法果足恃與孔子
論太叔治盜曰糾之以猛對康子患盜
曰不欲不竊之兩者可試度之
今日否夫山東北衞
帝畿南通漕輓所慮于盜尤亟也諸士有概于
中其著于篇毋諱
問國家薪槱才儁所以亮天工熙帝載其
===
道不誠鉅哉虞夏而上無論已賔興大
比周制可傚也漢設四科復有茂才三
科明經三科辟召四科至唐則為六科
宋復為三科其法果與成周合與世有
升降制由益損顧所得人孰多也
明興以經術取士士不操本業罷不用脫有
姬孔詎越是起家哉而二百年來鴻士
碩卿比肩接轂大都賢科選也其間卓
然名世者可悉數其人與或者顧謂取
punctuated:
今天下綦隆，而東省乃時有盜警。當事者亟申捕令矣，輒捕輒竊發，竟不衰止。議者大都在嚴保甲，覈其法，果足恃與？孔子論太叔治盜曰「糾之以猛」，對康子患盜曰「不欲不竊」。之兩者，可試度之今日否？夫山東北衞帝畿，南通漕輓，所慮于盜尤亟也。諸士有概于中，其著于篇，毋諱。

問：國家薪槱才儁，所以亮天工、熙帝載，其道不誠鉅哉！虞、夏而上，無論已；賔興大比，周制可傚也。漢設四科，復有茂才三科、明經三科、辟召四科；至唐則為六科，宋復為三科。其法果與成周合與？世有升降，制由益損，顧所得人孰多也？明興，以經術取士，士不操本業，罷不用。脫有姬、孔，詎越是起家哉？而二百年來，鴻士碩卿比肩接轂，大都賢科選也。其間卓然名世者，可悉數其人與？或者顧謂取
translation_en:
Today the realm enjoys supreme prosperity, yet the eastern province [Shandong] still experiences frequent alarms over banditry. Although the authorities have repeatedly and urgently issued orders for their capture, no sooner are bandits arrested than new outbreaks secretly arise, never abating or ceasing. Those who deliberate on the matter generally favor strictly enforcing the mutual-security system (baojia); if we examine this method closely, can it truly be relied upon? When Confucius discussed Zitaishu's suppression of bandits, he said, "Correct them with severity"; when replying to Ji Kangzi's worry about bandits, he said, "If you yourself are free of desire, they wouldn't steal even if you paid them." Can these two approaches be weighed and applied to the present day? Now, Shandong guards the Imperial Capital to the north and connects the Grand Canal grain transport to the south, so concern over banditry here is especially pressing. You gentlemen who harbor convictions on this matter in your hearts, set them forth in your essays and hold nothing back.

Question: The state gathers and nurtures men of talent and distinction (like firewood stacked for sacrifice) in order to assist in Heaven's work and make the sovereign's undertakings flourish—is this Way not truly momentous! Of the eras of Yu, Xia, and earlier we need not speak; as for the triennial presentation of local worthies (binxing dabi), the institutions of the Zhou may be emulated. The Han established the Four Categories (sike), and in addition had the Three Categories for Flourishing Talent (maocai), the Three Categories for Understanding the Classics (mingjing), and the Four Categories for Recruitment by Summons (pizhao). By the Tang there were Six Categories, and the Song returned to Three Categories. Did these methods truly accord with those of the flourishing Zhou? As ages rise and fall, institutions are modified by additions and reductions; yet looking back, which of them yielded the greatest number of capable men? Since the rise of the Ming, scholars have been selected on the basis of classical learning; any scholar who does not apply himself to this fundamental pursuit is dismissed and not employed. Even if a Duke of Zhou or a Confucius were to appear, how could he begin his official career except through this path? Over the past two hundred years, great scholars and eminent ministers have stood shoulder to shoulder and their carriage hubs have touched, almost all of them selected through the examination rosters. Among them, can you enumerate in full those who have stood out as illustrious figures of their generation? Yet some critics maintain that selecting…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
人以言如射覆盂爾必復德行舉選之
制而後得眞才而用之其說果足採與
夫上側席以求賢而下懷珍以待舉然
俯仰今昔往往嘆才難者何也茲欲
朝多髦髦而野無遺賢則何脩而可諸士其
試言之不佞將藉手聞于
上
問土田于民生急矣周官遂師遂大夫教
民稼穡而先王巡狩田蕪則讓誠重之
===
也漢唐而降有鎭襄陽而墾田八百餘
頃者有脩召信臣故迹而公私利之者
有爲營田使而起代北墾田三百頃者
有充河北判官而興堰六百里民賴其
利者夫亦可指言之與山東舊號沃土
而邇者地有遺利民寙不耕則何以故
也嘉靖間嘗一議墾矣復民二年越三
年始稅意蒸蒸厚也顧竟無左效何與
議者以爲地額未清所致然與否與今
punctuated:
人以言，如射覆盂爾；必復德行舉選之制，而後得眞才而用之。其說果足採與？夫上側席以求賢，而下懷珍以待舉，然俯仰今昔，往往嘆才難者，何也？茲欲朝多髦髦而野無遺賢，則何脩而可？諸士其試言之，不佞將藉手聞于上。

問：土田于民生急矣。《周官》遂師、遂大夫教民稼穡，而先王巡狩，田蕪則讓，誠重之也。漢、唐而降，有鎭襄陽而墾田八百餘頃者，有脩召信臣故迹而公私利之者，有爲營田使而起代北墾田三百頃者，有充河北判官而興堰六百里、民賴其利者，夫亦可指言之與？山東舊號沃土，而邇者地有遺利，民寙不耕，則何以故也？嘉靖間嘗一議墾矣，復民二年，越三年始稅，意蒸蒸厚也，顧竟無左效，何與？議者以爲地額未清所致，然與否與？今
translation_en:
…men by their words is like guessing what lies beneath an overturned bowl, and that only by restoring the system of selection based on moral conduct can we obtain and employ true talent. Is this view truly worth adopting? Now, the ruler above leaves his mat vacant in eagerness to seek the worthy, while scholars below cherish their precious virtues awaiting recommendation; yet looking back and forth between past and present, why do people so often sigh over the scarcity of talent? If today we wish the court to abound in eminent talents and the countryside to have no worthy left behind, what measures should be cultivated to achieve this? Gentlemen, pray set forth your views, and I, though unworthy, shall avail myself of them to report to His Majesty.

Question: Land and fields are of urgent importance to the people's livelihood. In the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), the Master of the Outlying Districts (Suishi) and the Grand Master of the Outlying Districts (Suidafu) taught the people sowing and reaping, and when the former kings went on tours of inspection, they reprimanded those whose fields had gone to weeds—truly because they attached great weight to this. From the Han and Tang dynasties onward, there was one who garrisoned Xiangyang and reclaimed over eight hundred qing of land; one who restored the old works of Shao Xinchen so that both public and private interests profited from it; one who served as Commissioner for State Farms (Yingtianshi) and initiated the reclamation of three hundred qing of land north of Dai; and one who served as Administrative Assistant (Panguan) of Hebei and built six hundred li of dikes, upon whose benefit the people relied—can you point out and name these men? Shandong was of old famed as fertile soil, yet recently the land has unexploited resources and the people are indolent and do not plow; what is the reason for this? During the Jiajing era (1522–1566), land reclamation was once deliberated upon: the people were exempted from obligations for two years and only taxed starting in the third year. The intention was generously benevolent, yet in the end there was no proven effect—why was that? Commentators held that it was caused by land quotas not having been cleared and clarified; was this so or not? The reigning…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
上軫念民瘼特
令丈地乃首以清頟報者東省也第濵海斥
鹵田卒汙萊則何以墾之當事之臣啟
議輸穀疏得
俞旨民忻忻然應焉夫嘉靖間寬賦于二年之
後而地荒如故今顧輸穀于初墾之年
而民樂從此其故又何以解也率是著
爲
令其于民便否抑其中尚有畫焉可枚舉而
言之與諸生桑梓于茲目擊之熟矣幸
悉心以對我
punctuated: 上軫念民瘼，特令丈地，乃首以清頟報者，東省也。第濵海斥鹵，田卒汙萊，則何以墾之？當事之臣，啟議輸穀，疏得俞旨，民忻忻然應焉。夫嘉靖間寬賦于二年之後，而地荒如故；今顧輸穀于初墾之年，而民樂從，此其故又何以解也？率是著爲令，其于民便否？抑其中尚有畫焉，可枚舉而言之與？諸生桑梓于茲，目擊之熟矣，幸悉心以對我。
translation_en: …His Majesty, sympathetically mindful of the people's hardships, issued a special command to survey the land, and the first to report that its quotas had been cleared up was the eastern province [Shandong]. Yet along the coast the soil is saline and barren, and the fields end up waterlogged and overgrown with weeds—so how are they to be reclaimed? The officials in charge initiated a proposal for the delivery of grain; their memorial received an approving rescript, and the people responded to it with delight. Now, during the Jiajing era (1522–1566), taxes were remitted until after two years had passed, yet the land remained as desolate as before; today, by contrast, grain is delivered in the very first year of reclamation, and the people gladly comply. How is the reason for this to be explained? If we follow this practice and establish it as an ordinance, will it be advantageous to the people or not? Or are there still further plans within this matter that can be enumerated and discussed one by one? You students have your native homes here and have witnessed these things thoroughly with your own eyes; I hope you will devote your whole minds to answering me.

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
定公問一言而可以興邦有諸孔子對曰
言不可以若是其幾也人之言曰爲君
難爲臣不易如知爲君之難也不幾乎
一言而興邦乎
杜華先
同考試官訓導解　批〔發知難興邦歸本君心上極得本旨〕
===
考試官教諭郭　批〔詞醇理到文之有典則者〕
考試官教諭林　批〔精確渾成〕
求治效於一言在圖其難而已矣夫君責至難
也知其難而圖之邦其可興乎且君人者孰不
欲邦之興哉顧其機本於君心心有敬肆而治
忽因之誠不可不知也定公志在興邦而以一
言爲問其望治亦切矣孔子對曰治道多端恐
非一言所能幾也而人之言則亦有可繹思者
其曰爲君難爲臣不易夫君臣並言當交儆矣
punctuated:
第壹塲
四書
「定公問：『一言而可以興邦，有諸？』孔子對曰：『言不可以若是其幾也。人之言曰：「爲君難，爲臣不易。」如知爲君之難也，不幾乎一言而興邦乎？』」
杜華先
同考試官訓導解　批：〔發知難興邦，歸本君心上，極得本旨。〕
考試官教諭郭　批：〔詞醇理到，文之有典則者。〕
考試官教諭林　批：〔精確渾成。〕
求治效於一言，在圖其難而已矣。夫君責至難也，知其難而圖之，邦其可興乎！且君人者孰不欲邦之興哉？顧其機本於君心，心有敬肆，而治忽因之，誠不可不知也。定公志在興邦，而以一言爲問，其望治亦切矣。孔子對曰：治道多端，恐非一言所能幾也；而人之言，則亦有可繹思者。其曰「爲君難，爲臣不易」，夫君臣並言，當交儆矣，
translation_en:
First Session
The Four Books

"Duke Ding asked: 'A single saying that can cause a state to flourish—is there such a thing?' Confucius replied: 'A saying cannot be expected to have such a direct effect as that. Yet there is a saying among people: "To be a ruler is difficult; to be a minister is not easy." If one knows the difficulty of being a ruler, would this not come close to making a state flourish through a single saying?'"

Du Huaxian 杜華先
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Xie 解, comments: [In expounding how knowing the difficulty makes a state flourish, he traces the root back to the ruler's mind, capturing the fundamental purport exceptionally well.]
Examiner, Instructor Guo 郭, comments: [The diction is pure and the reasoning thorough—a piece of writing that possesses classic standards.]
Examiner, Instructor Lin 林, comments: [Precise, accurate, and seamlessly integrated.]

To seek the efficacy of governance in a single saying lies simply in addressing its difficulty. Now, the responsibility of a ruler is supremely difficult; if one knows its difficulty and addresses it, can the state not be made to flourish? Moreover, among those who rule over others, who does not wish for his state to flourish? Yet the pivotal spring of this is rooted in the ruler's mind: the mind may be reverent or lax, and order or neglect follows accordingly—this truly cannot go unknown. Duke Ding set his ambition on making his state flourish and asked about a single saying; his hope for good governance was indeed earnest. Confucius replied: The ways of governance are manifold, and one fears such an effect cannot be expected from a single saying; yet among the sayings of people, there is indeed one worth pondering at length. It goes, "To be a ruler is difficult; to be a minister is not easy." Now, since ruler and minister are spoken of together, they ought to admonish one another…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
而君爲主治責尤重焉特患人君不知其難耳
夫苟知上天之難諶罔敢以逸豫承之叢萬幾
於一日而夙夜兢兢業業皆勑命之永圖也知下民
之難懷靡敢以慢易臨之萃百責於一身而朝
夕慄慄咸恤民之至計也由是君德以戒懼而
成精神之所運用無遠弗周而邦其日登於理
矣王業以憂勤而盛事功之所建立無廢不舉
而邦其永孚於休矣故人君不知其難則多言
而無補誠知其難則一言而有餘然則此一言
也謂不可幾於興邦耶吁繹其言而圖其所以
興在君加之意耳雖然人君之難莫難於用人
定公用孔子而郈費繼墮鄆讙龜陰來歸蓋勃
然興矣惜也女樂受而膰肉不至是公未知其
所以難即有不易之臣安所從效耶魯之不爲
東周也固宜噫可鑒矣
子曰道不遠人人之爲道而遠人不可以
爲道
于若瀛
punctuated:
而君爲主，治責尤重焉，特患人君不知其難耳。夫苟知上天之難諶，罔敢以逸豫承之，叢萬幾於一日，而夙夜兢兢業業，皆勑命之永圖也；知下民之難懷，靡敢以慢易臨之，萃百責於一身，而朝夕慄慄，咸恤民之至計也。由是君德以戒懼而成，精神之所運用，無遠弗周，而邦其日登於理矣；王業以憂勤而盛，事功之所建立，無廢不舉，而邦其永孚於休矣。故人君不知其難，則多言而無補；誠知其難，則一言而有餘。然則此一言也，謂不可幾於興邦耶？吁！繹其言而圖其所以興，在君加之意耳。雖然，人君之難，莫難於用人。定公用孔子，而郈、費繼墮，鄆、讙、龜陰來歸，蓋勃然興矣。惜也！女樂受而膰肉不至，是公未知其所以難，即有不易之臣，安所從效耶？魯之不爲東周也，固宜。噫，可鑒矣！

子曰：「道不遠人。人之爲道而遠人，不可以爲道。」

于若瀛
translation_en:
… Yet since the ruler is the master, his responsibility for governance is especially heavy; the only worry is that a ruler of men does not understand its difficulty. Now if he understands that High Heaven is hard to rely upon, he will not dare to receive its mandate in ease and pleasure; gathering a myriad affairs into a single day, day and night he is cautious and diligent—all of which is a lasting plan for reverently attending to Heaven's charge. If he understands that the common people below are hard to win over, he will not dare to approach them with negligence; concentrating a hundred responsibilities in his own person, morning and evening he is apprehensive—all of which is the ultimate counsel for showing compassion to the people. Through this, the ruler's virtue is perfected through vigilance and fear; wherever his vital spirit operates, there is no distant place it does not reach, and the state will daily ascend toward order. The kingly enterprise flourishes through anxious diligence; in the establishment of achievements and deeds, nothing neglected is left unraised, and the state will forever repose in blessings. Therefore, if a ruler of men does not understand its difficulty, then many words will be of no avail; if he truly understands its difficulty, then a single saying is more than enough. This being so, can it be said that this single saying cannot come close to making a state prosper? Alas! To ponder these words and plan how to bring about prosperity rests simply in the ruler paying heed to them. Even so, among the difficulties of a ruler of men, none is more difficult than employing men. When Duke Ding 魯定公 employed Confucius 孔子, the walls of Hou 郈 and Bi 費 were successively dismantled, and the lands of Yun 鄆, Huan 讙, and Guiyin 龜陰 were returned; the state was indeed vigorously prospering. Alas, what a pity! When the female musicians were accepted and the sacrificial meat did not arrive, this showed that the Duke did not yet understand wherein the difficulty lay; even though he had a minister who knew it was not easy, how could such a minister render his service? That Lu 魯 did not become an Eastern Zhou 東周 was certainly fitting. Alas, this may serve as a mirror!

The Master said: "The Way is not far from man. When men practice the Way and yet distance themselves from man, it cannot be considered the Way."

By Yu Ruoying 于若瀛.

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭葛　批〔以性言道不離倫□□□□□□〕
與乎支異者錄之
考試官教諭郭　批〔純正不浮〕
考試官教諭林　批〔簡潔〕
中庸論道切於人求諸遠者失之也夫道於人
至切也遠人以爲之曾是以爲道乎甞謂道之
不明不行也寧獨不爲者之咎哉卽爲之而或
過焉其爲畔道一也何也道也者命於天而率
於性者也故觀於未始有物之先有此命斯有
===
此人理非由于外鑠觀於既始有物之後有是
人卽具是性機不假于他求道之昭然者夫人
而可知也道之坦然者夫人而可能也夫何遠
之有如使人之爲道者反求諸身而得其所以
爲人則不外乎人而得其所以爲道矣夫茍視
道爲過高既騖于身心性情之外則去道爲益
遠自失其民彝物則之常遠人以爲知而索之
愈焉彼以爲會道之精矣而不知道之昭然示
□者本無所謂隱也非德性之良知也遠人以
punctuated:
同考試官教諭葛　批：〔以性言道，不離倫□□□□□□〕與乎支異者，錄之。
考試官教諭郭　批：〔純正不浮。〕
考試官教諭林　批：〔簡潔。〕

《中庸》論道切於人，求諸遠者失之也。夫道於人至切也，遠人以爲之，曾是以爲道乎？甞謂道之不明不行也，寧獨不爲者之咎哉？卽爲之而或過焉，其爲畔道一也。何也？道也者，命於天而率於性者也。故觀於未始有物之先，有此命斯有此人，理非由于外鑠；觀於既始有物之後，有是人卽具是性，機不假于他求。道之昭然者，夫人而可知也；道之坦然者，夫人而可能也。夫何遠之有？如使人之爲道者，反求諸身而得其所以爲人，則不外乎人而得其所以爲道矣。夫茍視道爲過高，既騖于身心性情之外，則去道爲益遠，自失其民彝物則之常。遠人以爲知，而索之愈焉，彼以爲會道之精矣，而不知道之昭然示□者，本無所謂隱也，非德性之良知也；遠人以
translation_en:
Associate Examiner, Instructor Ge, comments: [Explaining the Way in terms of human nature, never departing from human relationships [...] different from] those that are fragmented and heterodox; let it be recorded for publication.
Examiner, Instructor Guo, comments: [Pure, correct, and free of superficiality.]
Examiner, Instructor Lin, comments: [Concise and clear.]

When the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) discusses how the Way is closely bound to human beings, those who seek it afar lose it. Indeed, the Way is most closely bound to human beings; if one distances oneself from human beings in practicing it, how can that be considered the Way? I have maintained that when the Way is neither understood nor practiced, is the fault solely that of those who do not practice it? Even if one practices it and yet goes to excess, it is equally a departure from the Way. Why is this? The Way is what is decreed by Heaven and followed in accordance with human nature. Therefore, looking at the state before things ever came into being, once there was this decree, there was this human being—its principle was not fused onto us from the outside; looking at the state after things came into being, wherever there is this human being, this nature is endowed—its vital mechanism does not depend on seeking elsewhere. That in which the Way is luminous, everyone can know; that in which the Way is level and easy, everyone can practice. How could it be far off? If those who practice the Way turn within to seek it in themselves and grasp that by which they are human, then without going outside of what is human they will grasp that by which the Way is the Way. If, however, one regards the Way as overly lofty, racing after things outside of body, mind, nature, and feelings, one moves ever further from the Way and naturally loses the constancy of human moral bonds and the principles of things. Distancing oneself from human beings in pursuit of knowledge, and prying ever further into the obscure [?], such a person thinks he has grasped the essence of the Way, not knowing that the Way as luminously revealed to [humanity] fundamentally has nothing hidden about it—this is not the innate knowledge of our moral nature. Distancing oneself from human beings in…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
爲行而求之怪焉彼以爲體道之妙矣而不知
性之坦然示人者本無所謂怪也非德性之良
能也謂之道也可乎蓋求之性分之中則近耶
而自足求之性分之外則愈遠而愈濶爲道者
慎無遠人以爲之哉雖然道以中爲至過與不
及均之不可以爲道也夫子獨以遠人者言之
何哉蓋不及者易見也過焉者難知也自好奇
之士出倡爲異說而天下靡焉從之道斯裂矣
此聖人之所憂也此中庸之所以作也
養心莫善於寡欲其爲人也寡欲雖有不
存焉者寡矣
柳佐
同考試官教諭鄒　批〔欲寡心存即爲善養士子乃各自爲〕
說支離甚矣惟此作得之
考試官教諭郭　批〔切實無一長語〕
考試官教諭林　批〔雅醇〕
大賢論事心之要惟能去其累者得之也甚矣
欲之爲心累也欲寡而心可存矣養心孰善於
punctuated:
爲行，而求之怪焉。彼以爲體道之妙矣，而不知性之坦然示人者，本無所謂怪也，非德性之良能也。謂之道也可乎？蓋求之性分之中，則近耶而自足；求之性分之外，則愈遠而愈濶。爲道者，慎無遠人以爲之哉！雖然，道以中爲至，過與不及，均之不可以爲道也。夫子獨以遠人者言之，何哉？蓋不及者易見也，過焉者難知也。自好奇之士出，倡爲異說，而天下靡焉從之，道斯裂矣。此聖人之所憂也，此《中庸》之所以作也。

養心莫善於寡欲。其爲人也寡欲，雖有不存焉者，寡矣。
柳佐
同考試官教諭鄒　批：〔欲寡心存，即爲善養。士子乃各自爲〕說，支離甚矣，惟此作得之。
考試官教諭郭　批：〔切實，無一長語。〕
考試官教諭林　批：〔雅醇。〕

大賢論事心之要，惟能去其累者得之也。甚矣，欲之爲心累也！欲寡而心可存矣，養心孰善於
translation_en:
… act, and seek what is bizarre. They believe they have embodied the wonders of the Way, yet they do not know that in what nature openly reveals to people, there is originally nothing bizarre—it is not the innate ability of our moral nature. Can this be called the Way? Indeed, if one seeks it within one's innate nature, it is near [?] and self-sufficient; if one seeks it outside one's innate nature, the further one goes, the more detached from reality it becomes. Those who pursue the Way must take care not to distance themselves from humanity in practicing it! Even so, the Way takes the Mean as its ultimate standard; going too far and falling short are equally incapable of being the Way. Why then did the Master speak solely of those who distance themselves from humanity? Because falling short is easy to see, whereas going too far is difficult to recognize. Ever since men fond of novelty emerged to advocate heterodox doctrines, the world hasbeen swept along in following them, and thus the Way has been torn apart. This was what the Sage worried about, and this was why the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) was composed.

"To nourish the mind, there is nothing better than to make the desires few. Here is a man whose desires are few: in some things he may not be able to preserve his mind, but they will be few."
Liu Zuo 柳佐
Associate Examiner, Instructor Zou 鄒 comments: 〔When desires are few and the mind is preserved, that in itself is good nourishment. Yet the candidates each fabricated their own〕 theories, becoming utterly fragmented; only this essay has grasped the point.
Examiner, Instructor Guo 郭 comments: 〔Concrete and substantial, without a single superfluous word.〕
Examiner, Instructor Lin 林 comments: 〔Refined and pure.〕

When the great worthy discussed the essentials of serving the mind, he held that only one who can cast off its burdens grasps it. How great indeed is the burden that desires place upon the mind! When desires are few, the mind can be preserved; in nourishing the mind, what could be better than…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
是且夫心之在人不可一息而不存則人之於
心不可一息而不養養心急矣而孰爲善哉亦
曰寡欲焉耳蓋人心之初本渾然而無欲人心
之欲因有感而後形欲固不能絕之而使無尤
不可縱之而使熾也如使其爲人也道足以御
情而防檢必嚴能制乎欲而不制於欲則私無
以勝理而非幾盡黜自命於心而不命乎心矣
與物接也而欲不使之萌焉人心退聽道心之
所以日著也湛然而虛者庶其常在我乎既與
===
物接也而欲不爲之引焉嗜慾既淺天機之所
以日深也瑩然而靈者庶其常在我乎而謂心
有不存焉者寡矣是何也心不出則入而惟欲
足以馳其心欲不節則流而惟寡足以制夫欲
欲寡而心存乃機之必然者也此所以爲善養
也與抑寡欲云者豈必離物而後可哉心不逐
於物則萬感紛紜而不足爲吾心病欲或潛滋
雖淵居閴寂而已不勝其憧憧之擾矣故聲色
臭味聖人未嘗絕之也而道在焉以其無物之
punctuated: 是？且夫心之在人，不可一息而不存；則人之於心，不可一息而不養。養心急矣，而孰爲善哉？亦曰「寡欲」焉耳。蓋人心之初，本渾然而無欲；人心之欲，因有感而後形。欲固不能絕之而使無，尤不可縱之而使熾也。如使其爲人也，道足以御情，而防檢必嚴，能制乎欲而不制於欲，則私無以勝理，而非幾盡黜，自命於心而不命乎心矣。與物接也，而欲不使之萌焉；人心退聽，道心之所以日著也，湛然而虛者，庶其常在我乎！既與物接也，而欲不爲之引焉；嗜慾既淺，天機之所以日深也，瑩然而靈者，庶其常在我乎！而謂「心有不存焉者，寡矣」。是何也？心不出則入，而惟欲足以馳其心；欲不節則流，而惟寡足以制夫欲。欲寡而心存，乃機之必然者也。此所以爲善養也與！抑寡欲云者，豈必離物而後可哉？心不逐於物，則萬感紛紜，而不足爲吾心病；欲或潛滋，雖淵居閴寂，而已不勝其憧憧之擾矣。故聲色臭味，聖人未嘗絕之也，而道在焉，以其無物之
translation_en:
… this?

Now then, as the mind exists in a person, it cannot fail to be preserved for even a single breath; thus, in a person's relation to the mind, it cannot fail to be nourished for even a single breath. Nourishing the mind is urgent indeed, yet what is the best way to do it? One simply says, "Make the desires few," and that is all. For in the beginning of the human mind, it is originally whole and without desires; the desires of the human mind take form only after it is stirred by things. While desires certainly cannot be completely cut off and reduced to nothing, even less may they be indulged and allowed to blaze up.

Suppose that in a person's conduct, the Way is sufficient to govern the emotions and his self-restraint and vigilance are strictly maintained, so that he is able to control his desires rather than be controlled by them; then selfish impulses have no means to overcome principle, improper tendencies are completely dismissed, and one takes command from the mind rather than letting desires command the mind. When coming into contact with external things, one does not allow desires to sprout therein; the human mind retreats and obeys, which is whereby the mind of the Way becomes daily more manifest. That which is limpid and empty—perhaps it will always abide in me! Having come into contact with external things, one is not lured away by desires therein; as cravings and desires become shallow, that is whereby the heavenly mechanism becomes daily deeper. That which is lustrous and spiritually perceptive—perhaps it will always abide in me! And as for saying, "Though there be some in whom the mind is not preserved, they are few"—why is this? If the mind does not go out, it stays within, and only desires are sufficient to make the mind gallop away; if desires are not moderated, they flow unchecked, and only making them few is sufficient to control desires. That when desires are few the mind is preserved is an inevitable working of the mechanism. Is this not why it is the best way to nourish the mind!

Yet what is meant by "making the desires few"—must one really separate oneself from external things before this is possible? If the mind does not chase after things, then even if ten thousand stimuli arise in profusion, they are not enough to afflict my mind; if desires secretly multiply, then even if one dwells in deep seclusion and quietude, one will already be unable to bear the disturbance of their restless wavering. Therefore, sounds, colors, odors, and flavors—the sage never cut them off, and yet the Way was present in them, because with a mind devoid of attachment to things…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
心而行於有物之中耳彼離形去智正佛氏之
所爲畔道也此又養心者所當知
易
六四至臨无咎象曰至臨无咎位當也六
五知臨大君之宜吉象曰大君之宜行
中之謂也
趙　肆塾
同考試官教諭葛　批〔用賢本於有德士子鮮能言之至說〕
〔出中正之旨僅見此作佳士佳士〕
===
考試官教諭郭　批〔詞不繁而意足可以式矣〕
考試官教諭林　批〔明潔雅重〕
兩觀於臨爻君相用賢之道得矣夫賢人之有
益于治也四之以正五之以中其善於用賢者
乎且夫君臣相與以共成化理者豈無其道哉
用人其要也純心其本也吾於臨爻見之矣何
則大臣所以輔治可以獨任乎誠於求賢者廣
益之心也相道宜爾也六四下應初九以之非
蔽賢而病國者咎何有焉然使本諸身而匪正
punctuated:
心，而行於有物之中耳。彼離形去智，正佛氏之所爲畔道也，此又養心者所當知。

易
「六四，至臨，无咎。象曰：至臨无咎，位當也。六五，知臨，大君之宜，吉。象曰：大君之宜，行中之謂也。」
趙　肆塾
同考試官教諭葛　批：〔用賢本於有德，士子鮮能言之。至說出中正之旨，僅見此作。佳士，佳士！〕
考試官教諭郭　批：〔詞不繁而意足，可以式矣。〕
考試官教諭林　批：〔明潔雅重。〕

兩觀於臨爻，君相用賢之道得矣。夫賢人之有益于治也，四之以正，五之以中，其善於用賢者乎！且夫君臣相與以共成化理者，豈無其道哉？用人其要也，純心其本也，吾於臨爻見之矣。何則？大臣所以輔治，可以獨任乎？誠於求賢者，廣益之心也，相道宜爾也。六四下應初九，以之非蔽賢而病國者，咎何有焉？然使本諸身而匪正，
translation_en:
… mind while acting amidst external things. As for casting off the physical form and discarding knowledge, that is precisely how the Buddhists rebel against the Way; this is also what those who nourish the mind ought to know.

Book of Changes (Yi)
"Six in the fourth place: Personal approach, no blame. The Commentary on the Images (Xiang) says: 'Personal approach, no blame'—this is because the position is appropriate. Six in the fifth place: Wise approach, fitting for a great ruler, auspicious. The Commentary on the Images says: 'Fitting for a great ruler'—this refers to walking the middle path."
Zhao Sishu 趙肆塾
Associate Examiner Instructor Ge 葛 comments: [That employing the worthy is rooted in possessing virtue is something few candidates are able to articulate. As for bringing out the purport of centrality and correctness, it is seen only in this composition. A fine scholar, a fine scholar!]
Examiner Instructor Guo 郭 comments: [The words are not prolix, yet the meaning is complete; it can serve as a model.]
Examiner Instructor Lin 林 comments: [Clear, pure, elegant, and dignified.]

Observing both lines of the hexagram Approach (Lin), the Way for ruler and chief minister to employ the worthy is grasped. Now, as for worthy men being beneficial to governance, the fourth line through correctness and the fifth line through centrality—how skilled they are in employing the worthy! Moreover, when ruler and minister work together to jointly accomplish transformative governance, how could it be without its proper Way? Employing men is its essential point, and a pure mind is its foundation; I see this in the lines of Approach. Why is this so? A grand minister is one who assists in governance; can he take on the burden alone? Being sincere in seeking the worthy reflects a mind that broadens benefit; the Way of a chief minister ought to be thus. Six in the fourth place responds below to Nine in the first place; by doing so, he is not one who obscures the worthy and harms the state—what blame could there be? Yet suppose that what is rooted in his own person is not correct, …

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
則志有未合賢誰與我而不知四有柔正之德
也以正感正是同道相孚非出于有我之意而
同心共濟自篤夫好善之誠此至臨之所以无
咎也觀於四爻而相道其克盡乎大君所以主
治可以獨運乎明於任賢者先務之知也君道
宜爾也六五下用九二以之乃得人而弘化者
吉可必焉然使本諸身而匪中則心有未純賢
誰與我而不知五有柔中之德也以中用中是
心唯虛已不狃于自用之偏而政在取人自行
===
乎下賢之願此大君之所以爲宜也觀於五爻
而君道其克盡乎要之有得正之相聖君益得
以享其逸有行中之君賢相益得以輸其忠上
下相須而致治之盛可深幸也已大抵世有可
用之人而又有用人之人用人之人相也用用
人之人者君也君擇相相擇百執事則天下治
矣易垂憲之意深哉噫成王之任周公周公之
勤吐握蓋得是道矣然則周公之繫爻也其亦
有所感也夫
punctuated: 則志有未合，賢誰與我？而不知四有柔正之德也。以正感正，是同道相孚，非出于有我之意，而同心共濟，自篤夫好善之誠，此至臨之所以无咎也。觀於四爻，而相道其克盡乎！大君所以主治，可以獨運乎？明於任賢者，先務之知也，君道宜爾也。六五下用九二以之，乃得人而弘化者，吉可必焉。然使本諸身而匪中，則心有未純，賢誰與我？而不知五有柔中之德也。以中用中，是心唯虛已，不狃于自用之偏，而政在取人，自行乎下賢之願，此大君之所以爲宜也。觀於五爻，而君道其克盡乎！要之，有得正之相，聖君益得以享其逸；有行中之君，賢相益得以輸其忠。上下相須，而致治之盛可深幸也已。大抵世有可用之人，而又有用人之人。用人之人，相也；用用人之人者，君也。君擇相，相擇百執事，則天下治矣。《易》垂憲之意深哉！噫！成王之任周公，周公之勤吐握，蓋得是道矣。然則周公之繫爻也，其亦有所感也夫！
translation_en:
…then their aspirations would not yet be in harmony, and what worthy would join with me? Yet they fail to realize that the Fourth line possesses the virtue of yielding correctness. Moving the correct through correctness is the mutual trust of those who share the same Way, not arising from selfish intent; and working together with one heart, he naturally deepens his sincerity in loving goodness. This is why "approaching in the highest degree" (zhi lin) entails "no blame." Observing the Fourth line, is not the Way of the chief minister fully realized!

As for the "great ruler" who presides over governance, can he operate all alone? Being clear-sighted in employing worthies is the wisdom of knowing the foremost priority; the Way of the ruler ought to be thus. Six in the Fifth place reaches down to employ Nine in the Second place; thereby obtaining the right man and broadening transformation, good fortune can be assured. Yet if, rooted in his own person, he were not balanced (zhong), then his mind would not yet be pure, and what worthy would join with me? Yet they fail to realize that the Fifth line possesses the virtue of yielding balance. Employing the balanced through balance means that his mind is solely humble and self-effacing, not bound by the bias of relying only on oneself, while his governance lies in selecting men, naturally fulfilling his wish to defer to worthies. This is why it is "fitting for the great ruler." Observing the Fifth line, is not the Way of the ruler fully realized!

In sum, when there is a chief minister who attains correctness, the sage ruler is all the more able to enjoy his ease; when there is a ruler who practices balance, the worthy chief minister is all the more able to pour forth his loyalty. Superior and inferior depend upon one another, and the flourishing of well-ordered governance may indeed be deeply rejoiced in. On the whole, in the world there are men who can be employed, and there are also men who employ men. The man who employs men is the chief minister; the one who employs the man who employs men is the ruler. When the ruler selects the chief minister, and the chief minister selects the hundred executive officials, then All under Heaven is well governed. Profound indeed is the Book of Changes (Yi) in handing down this model! Ah! King Cheng's entrusting of the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Zhou's diligence in spitting out his food and grasping his hair to receive worthies, surely attained this Way. If so, when the Duke of Zhou appended the line statements, was he not also moved by this!

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
子曰知變化之道者其知神之所爲乎
于若瀛
同考試官訓導王　批〔神只是自然作者多未深知子獨闡發明透非深於易者不能〕
考試官教諭郭　批〔理精而詞達〕
考試官教諭林　批〔莊重雄偉〕
聖人贊數法之妙一自然而已夫惟自然者神
也數法之所以妙其以是夫夫子恐人以私智
窺易也故贊之且夫天地大衍之數起于一窮
===
于十若子毋相續而至于成變化行鬼神此變
化之道在天地者也揲蓍求卦之法始於衍終
於扐與天人相符而至於顯道神德行此變化
之道在易書者也淺乎觀易者以爲龍馬雖異
不過物中之一奇蓍卦雖精不過象中之一數
此天地偶然之產而聖人有心之爲也此非知
變化之道者矣知道者其知神之所爲乎蓋天
下惟出於理勢之自然者謂之神變而之化化
而之變事相禪而不已者理有固然也變而不
punctuated:
「子曰：知變化之道者，其知神之所爲乎。」
于若瀛
同考試官訓導王　批：〔神只是自然，作者多未深知，子獨闡發明透，非深於《易》者不能。〕
考試官教諭郭　批：〔理精而詞達。〕
考試官教諭林　批：〔莊重雄偉。〕
聖人贊數法之妙，一自然而已。夫惟自然者，神也；數法之所以妙，其以是夫！夫子恐人以私智窺《易》也，故贊之。且夫天地大衍之數，起于一，窮于十，若子毋相續，而至于成變化、行鬼神，此變化之道在天地者也。揲蓍求卦之法，始於衍，終於扐，與天人相符，而至於顯道、神德行，此變化之道在《易》書者也。淺乎觀《易》者！以爲龍馬雖異，不過物中之一奇；蓍卦雖精，不過象中之一數；此天地偶然之產，而聖人有心之爲也。此非知變化之道者矣。知道者，其知神之所爲乎！蓋天下惟出於理勢之自然者，謂之神。變而之化，化而之變，事相禪而不已者，理有固然也；變而不
translation_en:
"The Master said: 'He who knows the way of change and transformation—does he not know what the numinous does?'"

Yu Ruoying 于若瀛

Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Wang, comments: [The numinous is simply natural spontaneity. Most writers have not deeply understood this; you alone have elucidated it with thorough clarity—something impossible for anyone not deeply versed in the Classic of Changes (Yi).]
Examiner, Instructor Guo, comments: [The reasoning is refined and the expression is lucid.]
Examiner, Instructor Lin, comments: [Dignified and magnificent.]

The Sage praises the subtlety of the numbers and the divination method as nothing other than natural spontaneity. Now, only what is naturally spontaneous is numinous; is it not for this reason that the numbers and the method are so subtle! The Master feared that people would peer into the Classic of Changes with their private cleverness, and therefore he praised it thus.

Moreover, the numbers of Heaven and Earth and of the Great Expansion begin with one and reach their limit at ten, succeeding one another like mother and child [reading 毋 as 母], until they accomplish change and transformation and set in motion the spiritual beings—this is the way of change and transformation as it exists in Heaven and Earth. The method of sorting yarrow stalks to seek the hexagrams begins with the expansion and ends with placing the remainder between the fingers, corresponding with both Heaven and humanity, until it makes manifest the Way and renders spiritual the practice of virtue—this is the way of change and transformation as it exists in the Book of Changes.

How shallow are those who view the Changes superficially! They suppose that although the dragon-horse was extraordinary, it was no more than a single oddity among creatures; and that although the yarrow stalks and hexagrams are refined, they are no more than a single calculation among emblems—that the former was an accidental product of Heaven and Earth, and the latter a deliberate contrivance of the Sages. Such people do not know the way of change and transformation. He who knows this way—does he not know what the numinous does!

For in all the world, only that which arises from the natural spontaneity of principle and tendency is called numinous. Changing and thereby going into transformation, transforming and thereby going into change, affairs yielding to one another without cease—this is because principle is inherently so. Changing and not…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
得不化化而不得不變機相迫而不停者勢有
必至也陰陽五行錯綜經緯其生也孰始之其
成也孰終之蓋天地雖無不能而不能取自然
之數易置于其間神而已矣陰陽老少進退離
合其營也非有思其變也非有為蓋聖人雖無
不能而不能取自然之法損益於其間神而已
矣知此者謂之知道易豈可以淺乎觀之哉于
此而知易以神作雖作猶未作也易以神用雖
用猶未用也吉凶不在卦趨避不在蓍神潜先
===
告而已矣故至人終日言而未嘗言終日為而
未嘗為用此易也人不自神而責易之神豈知
神之所以神者乎
書
三百里揆文教二百里奮武衛
于永清
同考試官訓導解　批〔播詞雅醇而意復歷暢舒之〕
考試官教諭郭　批〔明淨冠冕〕
考試官教諭林　批〔純正〕
punctuated:
得不化，化而不得不變，機相迫而不停者，勢有必至也。陰陽五行，錯綜經緯，其生也孰始之？其成也孰終之？蓋天地雖無不能，而不能取自然之數易置于其間，神而已矣。陰陽老少，進退離合，其營也非有思，其變也非有為。蓋聖人雖無不能，而不能取自然之法損益於其間，神而已矣。知此者謂之知道，易豈可以淺乎觀之哉！于此而知易以神作，雖作猶未作也；易以神用，雖用猶未用也。吉凶不在卦，趨避不在蓍，神潜先告而已矣。故至人終日言而未嘗言，終日為而未嘗為，用此易也。人不自神而責易之神，豈知神之所以神者乎！

書

「三百里揆文教，二百里奮武衛。」
于永清
同考試官訓導解　批〔播詞雅醇，而意復歷暢舒之。〕
考試官教諭郭　批〔明淨冠冕。〕
考試官教諭林　批〔純正。〕
translation_en:
… cannot but transform, and transforming, it cannot but change; the mechanisms urge each other on without stopping because the tendency of things must inevitably reach this point. Yin and yang and the Five Phases interweave as warp and woof—in their generation, who initiates them? In their completion, who brings them to an end? Indeed, although Heaven and Earth are capable of everything, they cannot take the spontaneous numbers of nature and alter their placement therein; it is simply spirit (shen), and nothing more. Yin and yang, old and young, advance and retreat, separate and unite—their operation involves no deliberation, and their alternation involves no deliberate action. Indeed, although the sages are capable of everything, they cannot take the spontaneous methods of nature and add to or subtract from them therein; it is simply spirit, and nothing more. One who knows this is said to know the Way; how then could the Changes (Yi) be viewed shallowly! From this we know that the Changes were created through spirit, so although created, it is as if they were never created; the Changes are put to use through spirit, so although used, it is as if they were never used. Good and bad fortune do not reside in the hexagrams, and what to pursue or avoid does not reside in the yarrow stalks; spirit merely foretells them imperceptibly, and nothing more. Therefore, the supreme person speaks all day long without ever having spoken, and acts all day long without ever having acted—this is how he uses the Changes. If people do not make themselves numinous through spirit, yet demand the numinous power of the Changes from the Changes alone, how could they know that by which spirit is spirit!

Book of Documents (Shu)

"Three hundred li where civil teachings are measured; two hundred li where military defense is roused."
Yu Yongqing 于永清
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor (xundao) Xie 解 comments: [His phrasing is elegant and pure, and the meaning is furthermore articulated smoothly and thoroughly.]
Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Guo 郭 comments: [Clear, clean, and stately.]
Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Lin 林 comments: [Pure and upright.]

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
文武與其施而綏服之制定矣夫揆文以治內
奮武以治外而華夏辨焉聖人所以善綏服之
制者如此且帝王治天下之道文與武而已顧
有不容以槩施者水土平而法制定侯服之外
固別之爲綏服矣而所以制之者能無辨乎
彼綏服以內爲百里者三雖漸遠王畿而密邇
侯甸則所以安之者利用文也故三百里揆文
敎焉立之學校以萃其渙聯之師儒以樂其羣
又敎之禮樂詩書以廣其業蓋因俗尚而規畫
===
之而覲遷之風藹然於三百里中矣此文以治
乎內固以培國家之元氣也而奮武不有其地
耶綏服以外爲百里者二是已遠侯甸而聯屬
要荒則所以安之者利用武也故二百里奮武
衞焉爲之簡其什伍也爲之謹其斥堠也又爲
之嚴其約束訓練也蓋因遐服而保障之而戎
兵之詰赫然於二百里中矣此武以治乎外固
以壯國家之神氣也而揆文不有其助耶要之
揆文而繼之以武則不爲弛奮武而先之以文
punctuated: 文武與其施，而綏服之制定矣。夫揆文以治內，奮武以治外，而華夏辨焉，聖人所以善綏服之制者如此。且帝王治天下之道，文與武而已，顧有不容以槩施者。水土平而法制定，侯服之外，固別之爲綏服矣，而所以制之者，能無辨乎？彼綏服以內，爲百里者三，雖漸遠王畿，而密邇侯甸，則所以安之者，利用文也，故三百里揆文敎焉。立之學校以萃其渙，聯之師儒以樂其羣，又敎之禮樂詩書以廣其業。蓋因俗尚而規畫之，而覲遷之風藹然於三百里中矣。此文以治乎內，固以培國家之元氣也，而奮武不有其地耶？綏服以外，爲百里者二，是已遠侯甸，而聯屬要荒，則所以安之者，利用武也，故二百里奮武衞焉。爲之簡其什伍也，爲之謹其斥堠也，又爲之嚴其約束訓練也。蓋因遐服而保障之，而戎兵之詰赫然於二百里中矣。此武以治乎外，固以壯國家之神氣也，而揆文不有其助耶？要之，揆文而繼之以武，則不爲弛；奮武而先之以文…
translation_en:
When civil and martial means are each accorded their proper application, the institution of the Pacified Zone (suifu) is established. Indeed, measuring out civil teachings to govern the interior and rousing martial defenses to govern the exterior—so that the civilized heartland is distinguished from the periphery—such was how the sage perfected the system of the Pacified Zone.

Moreover, the Way by which emperors and kings govern All-under-Heaven consists of nothing more than the civil and the martial; yet these cannot be applied indiscriminately across the board. Once the waters and lands were pacified and institutional laws established, beyond the Zone of the Regional Rulers (houfu) a separate division was made for the Pacified Zone; yet in how it was regulated, could there be no differentiation?

Within the inner part of that Pacified Zone, spanning three hundred li, although it grows gradually more distant from the Royal Domain (wangji), it remains in close proximity to the Royal and Noble Zones (houdian); thus, the means to pacify it profitably employs the civil. Therefore, across three hundred li, civil teachings are measured out. Schools are established for them to gather what was dispersed; teachers and Confucians are linked together for them to take joy in their fellowship; and they are further instructed in the Rites, Music, Odes, and Documents to broaden their learning. By planning and ordering them in accordance with local customs and preferences, the ethos of emulation and transformation towards the good [?] flourishes harmoniously throughout the three hundred li. This use of the civil to govern the interior indeed nurtures the vital energy of the state; yet is there not also a place for rousing the martial?

In the outer part of the Pacified Zone, spanning two hundred li, this is already far from the Royal and Noble Zones and adjoins theZones of Restraint and the Wilds (yaohuang); thus, the means to pacify it profitably employs the martial. Therefore, across two hundred li, martial defenses are roused. Their squads of five and ten are inspected and selected for them; their watchtowers and beacons are maintained with vigilance for them; and their discipline and training are made strict for them. By providing a bulwark in accordance with the remoteness of the zone, the preparedness of military arms stands awe-inspiring throughout the two hundred li. This use of the martial to govern the exterior indeed strengthens the spirited vigor of the state; yet does not the measuring out of civil teachings thereby gain its support?

In sum, when measuring out civil teachings is followed by the martial, it does not become lax; when rousing the martial is preceded by the civil…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
而不偏顯文武不偏廢而內外酌其施舜禹之
世內順治而外威嚴固有自哉雖然文武並用
誠久安長治之術而聖人之心則右文事而武
非所急也益贊於禹曰惟德動天帝乃誕敷文
德干羽兩階而逆命如苗竟以來格矣是可以
窺聖人耀德不觀兵之心
夏暑雨小民惟曰怨咨冬祁寒小民亦惟
曰怨咨厥惟艱哉思其艱以圖其易民
乃寧
杜華先
同考試官訓導解　批〔體認思艱圖易意甚切而發以雅健之詞經義之佳者可式多士〕
考試官教諭郭　批〔意明詞達〕
考試官教諭林　批〔簡潔〕
===
賢王兩指民艱而望大臣以寧之也夫暑雨祁
寒民艱亦甚矣能圖其易庶幾其寧矣乎穆王
命君牙以爲自昔聖世而民無不寧者非能耕
而食之織而衣之也凡以圖之者預耳爾爲司
punctuated:
而不偏顯。文武不偏廢，而內外酌其施，舜、禹之世，內順治而外威嚴，固有自哉！雖然，文武並用，誠久安長治之術，而聖人之心，則右文事而武非所急也。益贊於禹曰：「惟德動天。」帝乃誕敷文德，干羽兩階，而逆命如苗，竟以來格矣。是可以窺聖人耀德不觀兵之心。

夏暑雨，小民惟曰怨咨；冬祁寒，小民亦惟曰怨咨。厥惟艱哉！思其艱以圖其易，民乃寧。
杜華先
同考試官訓導解　批〔體認思艱圖易，意甚切，而發以雅健之詞，經義之佳者，可式多士。〕
考試官教諭郭　批〔意明詞達。〕
考試官教諭林　批〔簡潔。〕

賢王兩指民艱，而望大臣以寧之也。夫暑雨祁寒，民艱亦甚矣，能圖其易，庶幾其寧矣乎！穆王命君牙，以爲自昔聖世而民無不寧者，非能耕而食之、織而衣之也，凡以圖之者預耳。爾爲司
translation_en:
… and so it does not become one-sidedly harsh. Neither civil nor military administration is neglected in favor of the other, and their application is weighed according to what is internal and what is external. That in the age of Shun and Yu all within was harmoniously ordered and all without was held in awe—surely this had its source! Even so, while the joint employment of civil and military means is indeed the art of enduring peace and lasting order, in the mind of the sage civil affairs take precedence and military force is not what he considers urgent. Yi, in offering counsel to Yu, said: "It is virtue alone that moves Heaven." The Sovereign thereupon broadly diffused his civil virtue, with shields and feathers danced between the two staircases, and even those as defiant of his mandate as the Miao ultimately came in submission. From this one may glimpse the sage's intention of displaying virtue rather than making a show of arms.

"In the summer, when there is sultry rain, the common people murmur and sigh; in the winter, when there isbitter cold, the common people likewise murmur and sigh. How hard their lot is! Think on their hardships in order to plan for their ease, and the people will then be tranquil."
Du Huaxian 杜華先
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Xie 解, comments: [He grasps the meaning of "thinking on their hardships to plan for their ease" most incisively, and expresses it in refined and vigorous language. It is a fine piece of classical exegesis that can serve as a model for the many scholars.]
Examiner, Instructor Guo 郭, comments: [The thought is clear and the expression fluent.]
Examiner, Instructor Lin 林, comments: [Concise and clean.]

The worthy king twice points out the hardships of the people, and looks to his great minister to bring them tranquility. Indeed, amid sultry rains and bitter cold, the hardships of the people are extreme; if one can plan for their ease, may they not perhaps find tranquility? When King Mu 穆王 charged Jun Ya 君牙, he held that the reason there had been no people left unpacified in the sage eras of the past was not that the ruler could plow to feed them himself or weave to clothe them himself, but simply that planning for them was done beforehand. title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
徒欲固不可緩矣而養尤在所先乎今夫人情
一日不再食則饑至於夏其饑爲甚矣故覩暑
雨而小民之怨咨形於聲焉終歲不製衣則寒
至於冬其寒爲甚矣故當祁寒而小民之怨咨
亦不免焉夫暑雨而怨則養生未贍夏何以寧
豈不艱哉必思其艱以圖其食之易凡可以爲
足食計者無不用也祁寒而怨則卒歲無資冬
何以寧豈不艱哉必思其艱以圖其衣之易凡
可以爲足衣計者無不周也允若茲則爾之憂
===
民已切民之蒙惠自深向固艱於食自易其食
而阻饑之民得安於粒食之休向固艱於衣自
易其衣而號寒之民得享夫煖衣之慶民乃寧
矣即暑雨祁寒豈復有怨咨者耶由是民生厚
而正德之教可舉矣向使忽民瘼而不之思弃
民事而不之圖則民之怨咨無已時也而何以
興教耶嗟夫穆王嗣周業以養民命君牙誠有
味哉其言之也豈不稱賢乃其竟也財匱民勞
又制爲贖刑以詰四方視君牙之命不可同日
punctuated: 徒，欲固不可緩矣，而養尤在所先乎！今夫人情，一日不再食則饑，至於夏，其饑爲甚矣，故覩暑雨而小民之怨咨形於聲焉；終歲不製衣則寒，至於冬，其寒爲甚矣，故當祁寒而小民之怨咨亦不免焉。夫暑雨而怨，則養生未贍，夏何以寧？豈不艱哉！必思其艱以圖其食之易，凡可以爲足食計者，無不用也。祁寒而怨，則卒歲無資，冬何以寧？豈不艱哉！必思其艱以圖其衣之易，凡可以爲足衣計者，無不周也。允若茲，則爾之憂民已切，民之蒙惠自深。向固艱於食，自易其食，而阻饑之民得安於粒食之休；向固艱於衣，自易其衣，而號寒之民得享夫煖衣之慶。民乃寧矣，即暑雨祁寒，豈復有怨咨者耶？由是民生厚，而正德之教可舉矣。向使忽民瘼而不之思，弃民事而不之圖，則民之怨咨無已時也，而何以興教耶？嗟夫！穆王嗣周業，以養民命君牙，誠有味哉其言之也，豈不稱賢？乃其竟也，財匱民勞，又制爲贖刑以詰四方，視君牙之命不可同日
translation_en: … [Minister of] Education, [teaching] indeed cannot be delayed [reading 欲 as 教?], yet nourishing [the people] must especially come first! Now, in the nature of human circumstances, if one does not eat twice in a single day, one goes hungry, and by summer that hunger is at its worst; therefore, upon seeing the summer rains, the resentments and sighs of the common folk are voiced aloud. If throughout the whole year one makes no clothes, one goes cold, and by winter that cold is at its worst; therefore, when facing the bitter cold, the resentments and sighs of the common folk are likewise unavoidable. Now, if they complain during the summer rains, then the means to nourish life are insufficient—how can they find peace in summer? Is this not hardship! You must reflect on their hardship in order to plan for the ease of their food, leaving unused no measure that might serve as a plan for sufficient food. If they complain during the bitter cold, then they lack the resources to finish out the year—how can they find peace in winter? Is this not hardship! You must reflect on their hardship in order to plan for the ease of their clothing, leaving incomplete no measure that might serve as a plan for sufficient clothing. Truly, if you act like this, then your concern for the people is already earnest, and the favor the people receive will naturally be profound. Where formerly they struggled for food, their food will naturally become easy to obtain, and people suffering from famine will be able to rest secure in the blessing of grain to eat; where formerly they struggled for clothing, their clothing will naturally become easy to obtain, and people crying out from the cold will be able to enjoy the felicity of warm garments. Then the people will be at peace! Even amid summer rains and bitter cold, how could there still be any who complain and sigh? From this, the people's livelihood will be abundant, and instruction in rectifying virtue can be carried out. Suppose instead that one were to neglect the people's distress and give it no thought, or cast aside the people's affairs and make no plans for them—then the people's resentments and sighs would never cease, and how could instruction be promoted? Alas! When King Mu succeeded to the patrimony of Zhou and charged Jun Ya with nourishing the people, how truly meaningful were the words he spoke! Could he not be called worthy? Yet in the end, when wealth was exhausted and the people were worn out with toil, he further instituted redemption punishments to regulate the four quarters; compared with the Charge to Jun Ya, they cannot be spoken of on the same day…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
語矣詎虔其始而未能厚其終非耶君天下者
可以思矣
詩
南有樛木葛藟纍之樂只君子福履綏之
王夢經
同考試官教諭徐　批〔詞旨溫厚得詩人稱願意結以序濟〕
如充之有發明是善說詩者
考試官教諭郭　批〔文典雅而氣和平〕
考試官教諭林　批〔莊重得體〕
===
詩人與后妃德盛而天休附焉甚矣惟德動天
也后妃有可樂之德而福履之綏固其所哉衆
妾稱願之意蓋曰天人之勢相懸而感應之機
不爽吾玆觀德於君子而幸願深矣彼南山之
木惟樛然其下垂葛藟之生斯依之而上附物
固有所藉以爲安也况我君子嗣京室之音而
志在進賢同乎人而無我溥宮闈之愛而恩周
逮下顯其比而忘私其德如此洵可樂矣由是
羣情之所繫屬而和氣流通一德之所感乎而
punctuated:
語矣。詎虔其始而未能厚其終，非耶？君天下者可以思矣。

《詩》
「南有樛木，葛藟纍之。樂只君子，福履綏之。」
王夢經
同考試官教諭徐　批〔詞旨溫厚，得詩人稱願意，結以序濟〕如充之，有發明，是善說《詩》者。
考試官教諭郭　批〔文典雅而氣和平〕
考試官教諭林　批〔莊重得體〕

詩人與后妃德盛而天休附焉。甚矣，惟德動天也！后妃有可樂之德，而福履之綏，固其所哉！衆妾稱願之意，蓋曰：天人之勢相懸，而感應之機不爽。吾玆觀德於君子，而幸願深矣。彼南山之木，惟樛然其下垂，葛藟之生，斯依之而上附，物固有所藉以爲安也。况我君子嗣京室之音，而志在進賢，同乎人而無我；溥宮闈之愛，而恩周逮下，顯其比而忘私。其德如此，洵可樂矣！由是羣情之所繫屬，而和氣流通；一德之所感孚，而
translation_en:
…spoken of in the same breath! Is it not that he was reverent at the beginning, yet failed to be generous to the end? Those who rule the world may well reflect upon this.

Classic of Poetry (Shi)
"In the south are trees with drooping branches, the kudzu and wild grape vines twine around them. Joyous be our lordly lady, may felicity and dignity comfort her."
By Wang Mengjing 王夢經.
Associate Examiner Instructor Xu comments: [The diction and purport are warm and generous, capturing the well-wishing intent of the poet; the conclusion draws on the Preface to aid [?]] and expands upon it with real insight—this is one who excels at explaining the Poetry.
Examiner Instructor Guo comments: [The prose is classical and elegant, and its vital breath harmonious and calm.]
Examiner Instructor Lin comments: [Dignified and fitting.]

The poet praises the Queen Consort for the abundance of her virtue and the heavenly blessings that attach to her. Profound indeed is the truth that only virtue moves Heaven! Since the Queen Consort possesses a virtue worthy of joy, is it not only natural that felicity and dignity should comfort her? The meaning behind the myriad concubines' praise and good wishes is broadly this: Though the positions of Heaven and humanity are far apart, the mechanism of stimulus and response never errs. Seeing now the virtue in our lordly lady, our joy and good wishes run deep indeed. Those trees on the southern mountain, simply because their branches droop downward, allow the growing kudzu and wild grape vines to rely on them and cling upward; things inherently have that upon which they depend in order to find peace. How much more so our lordly lady, who succeeds to the fine reputation of the royal house of Zhou, and whose aspiration lies in advancing the worthy, identifying with others without ego; who extends love throughout the palace quarters, her grace reaching all below, manifesting open solidarity while forgetting private interest! Her virtue being such as this, she is truly worthy of joy! Consequently, where the sentiments of the multitude are bound together, harmonious vital breath circulates; where pure virtue moves and inspires trust [reading 乎 as 孚], …

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
大休協應綏之以福而元吉旋焉正位中宮有
優游而無揺扤也綏之以祿而庶徵備焉母儀
下國有逸豫而無阽危也蓋天監周京久矣仁
厚之脉君子式與培之則天心之眷佑自不容
於不隆耳吾人何幸而獲藉其休乎帝懷明德
素矣豈弟之度君子式克相之則帝命之寵綏
自不容於不篤耳吾人何幸而獲蒙其庇乎要
之有是德斯有是福機非偶也得乎人自得乎
天理不誣也后妃之賢文王之化均可想見矣
===
抑家人睽始於婦人則乘寵以爲階然非遠驕
嫚之難而無禮以定其位之患關雎正始取義
有別則禮之序明焉耳樛木之感豈徒沾沾然
利用恩乎艷妻煽處而宗周危斁其序也閑有
家者宜鑒於茲
穫之挃挃積之栗栗其崇如墉其比如櫛
以開百室百室盈止婦子寧止
李毓奇
同考試官教諭鄒　批〔形容豐年之象宛然在目而詞更華〕
punctuated:
大休協應。綏之以福，而元吉旋焉，正位中宮，有優游而無揺扤也；綏之以祿，而庶徵備焉，母儀下國，有逸豫而無阽危也。蓋天監周京久矣，仁厚之脉，君子式與培之，則天心之眷佑，自不容於不隆耳，吾人何幸而獲藉其休乎！帝懷明德素矣，豈弟之度，君子式克相之，則帝命之寵綏，自不容於不篤耳，吾人何幸而獲蒙其庇乎！要之，有是德斯有是福，機非偶也；得乎人自得乎天，理不誣也。后妃之賢、文王之化，均可想見矣。抑《家人》、《睽》始於婦人，則乘寵以爲階，然非遠驕嫚之難，而無禮以定其位之患。《關雎》正始，取義有別，則禮之序明焉耳。《樛木》之感，豈徒沾沾然利用恩乎？艷妻煽處而宗周危，斁其序也，閑有家者宜鑒於茲。

穫之挃挃，積之栗栗，其崇如墉，其比如櫛，以開百室。百室盈止，婦子寧止。
李毓奇
同考試官教諭鄒　批〔形容豐年之象，宛然在目，而詞更華…〕
translation_en:
…and great blessings respond in harmony. Comforting her with good fortune, supreme auspiciousness returns to her: occupying her rightful position in the central palace, she enjoys leisurely ease without precariousness. Comforting her with felicity, all the auspicious signs are complete: serving as a maternal model for the realm below, she enjoys peaceful delight without peril. Indeed, Heaven has long watched over the Zhou capital; since our lady helps to cultivate its pulse of benevolent thickness, the favored protection of Heaven's heart naturally cannot fail to be abundant. How fortunate we are to rely upon her blessings! The Sovereign on High has ever cherished bright virtue; since our lady is able to assist with her magnanimous and easygoing bearing, the favored comfort of the Sovereign's mandate naturally cannot fail to be generous. How fortunate we are to receive her shelter! In sum, where there is this virtue, there is this blessing—the mechanism is no coincidence; winning over humanity naturally wins over Heaven—the principle does not deceive. Both the worthiness of the Queen Consort and the transforming influence of King Wen can well be envisioned here. Yet in the hexagrams Family (Jiaren) and Opposition (Kui), disorder begins with women, who use favor as a stepping-stone; however, the difficulty lies not in keeping arrogance and disrespect at a distance, but in the danger of lacking ritual propriety to fix their proper positions. When "Ospreys" (Guanju) rectifies the beginning by taking its meaning from proper distinction, the order of ritual propriety is made clear. How could the moving influence seen in "Drooping Branches" (Jiumu) consist merely in a self-satisfied dispensing of favor? When the seductive wife fanned her influence within and ancestral Zhou fell into peril, it was because that proper order was ruined. Those who regulate a household ought to take warning from this.

"They reap it, rustling; they stack it, dense and solid; it is high as a wall, close-set as the teeth of a comb, so that the hundred storehouses are opened. The hundred storehouses are full, and the wives and children are at peace."
By Li Yuqi 李毓奇.
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Zou: [It depicts the scene of a bountiful year vividly before one's eyes, while its diction is all the more ornate…]

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
欽宜錄以式
考試官教諭郭　批〔體裁整飭當是作家〕
考試官教諭林　批〔溫文閑雅〕
周人頌豐年利之所入者富慶之所及者弘蓋
農事以有成爲慶也收入之富而婦子賴以寧
焉其利亦何溥哉良耜所以答神貺也意謂吾
人之力田也耕而播播而耘其用力勤矣閔閔
焉望歲之情敢冀其厚穫乎幸也上帝溥降康
之祥而穀皆熟矣從而穫之此疆爾界挃挃焉
===
銍艾之相聞也西成啓築場之候而稼既同矣
從而積之墉崇櫛比栗栗然豐登之有象也惟
此多稼非但一倉箱之儲也千耦其耘向嘗舉
百室以于田矣今則通其力者均其利比屋之
藏皆充然其有餘蓄也百室不既盈乎然此美
利又非但一手足之烈也或來瞻女向嘗偕婦
子而從事矣今則任其勞者享其逸數口之家
皆晏然其獲我所矣婦子不既寧乎至是則豐
亨之慶徧于閭閻而天休普被樂利之澤綏厥
punctuated:
欽，宜錄以式。〕
考試官教諭郭　批〔體裁整飭，當是作家。〕
考試官教諭林　批〔溫文閑雅。〕

周人頌豐年，利之所入者富，慶之所及者弘。蓋農事以有成爲慶也，收入之富，而婦子賴以寧焉，其利亦何溥哉！《良耜》所以答神貺也，意謂吾人之力田也，耕而播，播而耘，其用力勤矣。閔閔焉望歲之情，敢冀其厚穫乎？幸也，上帝溥降康之祥，而穀皆熟矣。從而穫之，此疆爾界，挃挃焉銍艾之相聞也；西成啓築場之候，而稼既同矣，從而積之，墉崇櫛比，栗栗然豐登之有象也。惟此多稼，非但一倉箱之儲也。千耦其耘，向嘗舉百室以于田矣；今則通其力者均其利，比屋之藏，皆充然其有餘蓄也，百室不既盈乎？然此美利，又非但一手足之烈也。或來瞻女，向嘗偕婦子而從事矣；今則任其勞者享其逸，數口之家，皆晏然其獲我所矣，婦子不既寧乎？至是，則豐亨之慶徧于閭閻，而天休普被；樂利之澤綏厥
translation_en:
…and grave; it should be recorded as a model.
Examiner and Confucian School Instructor Guo comments: The form and structure are neat and disciplined; this must be the work of a skilled writer.
Examiner and Confucian School Instructor Lin comments: Gentle in style and refined in grace.

The people of Zhou praised the year of abundance: the profit brought in was rich, and the celebration that extended from it was vast. Indeed, in agricultural labor, having a successful harvest is the cause for celebration; when the income is rich, wives and children rely upon it for peace and security—how widespread too is that benefit! The ode "Good Plowshares" (Liang si) was written to give thanks for the blessings of the spirits. Its meaning is that when our people toil in the fields, plowing and then sowing, sowing and then weeding, the effort they expend is diligent indeed. With anxious longing as they hope for a good year, how could they dare expect an abundant harvest? Fortunately, the Lord on High universally sends down the auspicious blessing of prosperity, and the grains all ripen. Thereupon they reap them: across these borders and those boundaries, crunching and rustling, the sounds of sickles mowing are heard answering one another. The autumn completion opens the season for pounding the threshing floors, and the harvested grain is gathered together; thereupon they stack it up, high as a city wall and close-set as the teeth of a comb, standing in solid, dense array as the visible sign of a bountiful harvest. Now this multitude of grain is not merely the store of a single granary or bin. When a thousand pairs weeded together, earlier all the hundred households went out to the fields; now those who pooled their strength share equally in the profit, and the stores of the adjoining houses are all full to overflowing with surplus savings—are not the hundred households filled? Yet this fine profit is also not merely the achievement of a single pair of hands and feet. Coming to visit and see to them, earlier the wives and children had joined in the work; now those who bore the toil enjoy the ease, and families of several mouths all dwell in tranquility, each having found its proper place—are not the wives and children at peace? By this point, the celebration of abundance and prosperity extends throughout the village lanes, and the blessings of Heaven universally cover all; the bounty of joy and profit gives comfort to the…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
士女而靈貺昭垂神之所以福我者誠甚厚矣
報其容已哉抑聞唐虞之民飲食于耕鑿而忘
帝力曰何有于我周民則循知脩報于神焉然
生養休息出于君上之所賜固亦皡皡而莫知
爲之矣及讀鴻鴈桑柔之詩民有嘆劬勞憂卒
痒者然後知豐年之樂民受上恩德之深也故
曰王者如天
春秋
夏六月邢遷于夷儀〔僖公元年〕
張四聰
同考試官教諭彭　批〔讓齊桓忘義處令桓無以自解是旨〕
===
暢而調古蓋深於春秋者
考試官教諭郭　批〔得謹嚴體〕
考試官教諭林　批〔有斷制〕
春秋紀小國避患而深譏伯義之怠焉夫義莫
急於恤小而邢之遷也桓實貽之中國其奚賴
哉吾觀簡書之畏責在宗盟纓冠之情切於同
室脈可泄泄然圖之者桓自北杏創伯既以安
punctuated:
士女，而靈貺昭垂。神之所以福我者，誠甚厚矣，報其容已哉？抑聞唐虞之民，飲食于耕鑿，而忘帝力，曰：「何有于我？」周民則循知脩報于神焉，然生養休息出于君上之所賜，固亦皡皡而莫知爲之矣。及讀《鴻鴈》、《桑柔》之詩，民有嘆劬勞、憂卒痒者，然後知《豐年》之樂，民受上恩德之深也。故曰：「王者如天。」
春秋
夏六月，邢遷于夷儀。〔僖公元年〕
張四聰
同考試官教諭彭　批：〔讓齊桓忘義處，令桓無以自解。是旨〕暢而調古，蓋深於《春秋》者。
考試官教諭郭　批：〔得謹嚴體。〕
考試官教諭林　批：〔有斷制。〕
《春秋》紀小國避患，而深譏伯義之怠焉。夫義莫急於恤小，而邢之遷也，桓實貽之，中國其奚賴哉？吾觀簡書之畏，責在宗盟；纓冠之情，切於同室，脈可泄泄然圖之者？桓自北杏創伯，既以安
translation_en:
