… men and women, and divine blessings are brightly bestowed. That whereby the spirits bless us is truly generous indeed; how could our recompense ever cease? Yet I have heard that the people of the reigns of Yao and Shun ate and drank from their plowing and well-digging, forgetting the Emperor's power and saying, "What is that to us?" The people of Zhou, on the other hand, knew to follow custom and offer recompense to the spirits; yet as for the livelihood, nourishment, and rest granted by the sovereign above, they too were content and self-satisfied, not knowing who brought it about. Only when one reads the odes "Hongyan" (Wild Geese) and "Sangrou" (Tender Mulberry), in which the people sigh over painful toil and grieve in exhaustion and sickness, does one realize that in the joy of the ode "Fengnian" (Abundant Year), the people received the profound grace and virtue of their superiors. Therefore it is said: "The true king is like Heaven."

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)
"In summer, in the sixth month, Xing moved to Yiyi." [First year of Duke Xi]
By Zhang Sicong 張四聰
Associate Examiner and Instructor Peng 彭 comments: [Where it reproaches Duke Huan of Qi for forgetting righteousness, it leaves Huan with no way to excuse himself. The meaning is] fluent and the tone ancient—surely one who is deeply versed in the Spring and Autumn Annals.
Examiner and Instructor Guo 郭 comments: [It achieves a rigorous and strict style.]
Examiner and Instructor Lin 林 comments: [It possesses decisive judgment.]

The Spring and Autumn Annals records a small state fleeing disaster, and deeply criticizes thehegemon's negligence of righteousness. Now, in righteousness nothing is more urgent than relieving the small; yet as for the relocation of Xing, it was truly Duke Huan who brought it upon them—on what, then, could the Central States rely? Looking at the awe inspired by allied dispatches, the responsibility lies with the covenant of the ruling clan; as for the urgency of tying on one's cap strings in haste to rescue others, the feeling is as acute as a quarrel within the same household—how could one plan for it in such a leisurely manner [? 脈]? Ever since Duke Huan initiated his hegemony at Beixing, he had already taken pacifying …

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
擴爲已任矣方邢之有狄患也朝夕引領東望
豈不曰糾合仗義之齊庶幾克庇我乎顧臨淄
振旅徒張恤患之聲聶北駐師坐失事機之會
斯時也以伯叔則靡同危亡之憂其無日矣用
是遷其朝市爰爲苟免之謀以大邦則靡控倒
懸之勢殆弗支矣用是徙其人民少紓一時之
難斯豈邢之得已哉豈桓之力不足以及之哉
安安酖毒之言猶在於耳而徒欲養亂以爲功
豺狼莫厭之戒猶惕於懷而阻於爲義之不勇
===
即具厥器用邢遷如歸桓非終弃乎邢者然城
諸旣遷之餘孰與拯諸未遷之始存之於垂亡
之際孰與圖之於未事之先義士以桓爲薄德
良有由哉經書邢遷夷儀若曰夷儀之遷聶北
之次使之也齊桓之責深矣抑嘗觀徐之取舒
江黃之犄角皆協謀安攘有功於桓者然且見
敗見滅而不之恤以素所戮力共事之國一旦
弃之如遺也又何有於邢也彼伯者之經營直
爲一已功利匪有意匡天下者也故曰仲尼之
punctuated: 擴爲已任矣。方邢之有狄患也，朝夕引領東望，豈不曰：「糾合仗義之齊，庶幾克庇我乎？」顧臨淄振旅，徒張恤患之聲；聶北駐師，坐失事機之會。斯時也，以伯叔則靡同，危亡之憂其無日矣，用是遷其朝市，爰爲苟免之謀；以大邦則靡控，倒懸之勢殆弗支矣，用是徙其人民，少紓一時之難。斯豈邢之得已哉？豈桓之力不足以及之哉？「安安酖毒」之言猶在於耳，而徒欲養亂以爲功；「豺狼莫厭」之戒猶惕於懷，而阻於爲義之不勇。即具厥器用，邢遷如歸，桓非終弃乎邢者。然城諸旣遷之餘，孰與拯諸未遷之始？存之於垂亡之際，孰與圖之於未事之先？義士以桓爲薄德，良有由哉！經書「邢遷夷儀」，若曰：夷儀之遷，聶北之次使之也。齊桓之責深矣。抑嘗觀徐之取舒、江黃之犄角，皆協謀安攘、有功於桓者，然且見敗見滅而不之恤。以素所戮力共事之國，一旦弃之如遺也，又何有於邢也？彼伯者之經營，直爲一已功利，匪有意匡天下者也。故曰：仲尼之
translation_en: …and repelling [the barbarian tribes] as his own personal responsibility. When Xing was suffering from the Di threat, day and night they craned their necks looking eastward, surely saying to themselves, "Will not Qi, which rallies the states and upholds righteousness, perhaps be able to shelter us?" Yet although troops were marshaled at Linzi, it merely broadcast the empty reputation of relieving distress; and by halting the army at Niebei, he idly lost the opportune moment for action. At that time, since among the fraternal states [of the royal house] none shared their plight, the dread of peril and ruin left them almost no time; therefore they moved their court and marketplaces, devising a plan merely to escape for the moment. And since among the great states there was none to appeal to, their desperate situation—like hanging upside down—could scarcely be sustained; therefore they relocated their populace, slightly easing the crisis of the hour. How could this have been what Xing wanted to do? And how could it be that Duke Huan's strength was insufficient to reach them? The words that "Indulging in ease is a deadly poison" were still ringing in his ears, yet he merely wished to let the disorder fester so as to claim greater merit; the warning that "Jackals and wolves cannot be satisfied" still alarmed his heart, yet he was held back by a lack of courage to act righteously. Even though he furnished their implements and supplies so that "Xing moved as if returning home"—showing that Duke Huan did not ultimately abandon Xing—still, how does walling their city after they had already moved compare to rescuing them at the outset before they had to move? How does preserving them on the brink of ruin compare to planning for them before trouble even began? That righteous men consider Duke Huan to be of meager virtue is truly with good reason! When the Classic records, "Xing moved to Yiyi," it is as if to say: the move to Yiyi was brought about by the encamping at Niebei. The reproach against Duke Huan of Qi is profound indeed. Moreover, if we observe how Xu captured Shu, and how Jiang and Huang acted as supporting horns—all of whom joined in counsels to pacify and repel, rendering meritorious service to Duke Huan—yet when they were defeated or destroyed, he showed them no concern. If states that had habitually united their strength and worked together with him could one day be cast aside like something forgotten, what then did Xing matter to him? The enterprises of those hegemons were simply for their own personal merit and profit; they had no genuine intention of rectifying the world. Therefore it is said: Among the disciples of Confucius…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
徒無道桓文之事者
晉人執季孫意如以歸〔昭公十有三年〕春
意如至自晉〔昭公十有四年〕
李有實
同考試官教諭彭　批〔意如專魯虐鄰罪本可討諸作畢略〕
此意獨予發揮明確宜錄以式
考試官教諭郭　批〔格嚴詞整〕
考試官教諭林　批〔古健〕
伯國操縱由於利無以宗諸侯矣夫大國制義
===
以爲盟主者也晉之視利爲操縱何惑乎諸侯
之解體耶且晉自文襄以來主盟中夏其威焉
足畏惠焉足懷者以義命故也胡至昭之世而
反之是故始而耀邾南之旆則執魯意如焉夫
意如內專魯國外虐鄰邦即聲厥罪而致之辟
其誰曰不可乃晉之心則豈爲是哉徒謂邾莒
不共魯故之以是魯之不利於我也吾治之而
已矣既而因穆子之請則歸意如焉夫晉也不
能救蔡爲夷執親即悔過而徼之惠夫孰曰不
punctuated:
徒無道桓、文之事者。

晉人執季孫意如以歸。〔昭公十有三年〕春，意如至自晉。〔昭公十有四年〕
李有實
同考試官教諭彭　批〔意如專魯虐鄰，罪本可討，諸作畢略此意，獨予發揮明確，宜錄以式。〕
考試官教諭郭　批〔格嚴詞整。〕
考試官教諭林　批〔古健。〕

伯國操縱由於利，無以宗諸侯矣。夫大國制義以爲盟主者也，晉之視利爲操縱，何惑乎諸侯之解體耶？且晉自文、襄以來，主盟中夏，其威焉足畏、惠焉足懷者，以義命故也，胡至昭之世而反之？是故始而耀邾南之旆，則執魯意如焉。夫意如內專魯國，外虐鄰邦，即聲厥罪而致之辟，其誰曰不可？乃晉之心，則豈爲是哉？徒謂邾、莒不共，魯故之以，是魯之不利於我也，吾治之而已矣。既而因穆子之請，則歸意如焉。夫晉也不能救蔡，爲夷執親，即悔過而徼之惠，夫孰曰不
translation_en:
… disciples of Confucius spoke of the affairs of Duke Huan and Duke Wen.

"The people of Jin seized Jisun Yiru and took him back with them." [Thirteenth Year of Duke Zhao] "In spring, Yiru arrived from Jin." [Fourteenth Year of Duke Zhao]
By Li Youshi 李有實.
Associate Examiner Instructor Peng 彭 comments: [Yiru monopolized power in Lu and oppressed neighboring states; his crimes inherently warranted punishment. Other essays all passed over this point, whereas mine alone expounds it clearly and accurately; it is fitting to record it as a model.]
Examiner Instructor Guo 郭 comments: [Strict in structure and neat in diction.]
Examiner Instructor Lin 林 comments: [Archaic and vigorous.]

When a hegemonic state's coercion and leniency stem from profit, it has no means to command the allegiance of the feudal lords. Now, a great state establishes righteousness in order to serve as lord of covenants. When Jin looked to profit in exercising coercion and leniency, what wonder is it that the feudal lords fell away? Moreover, since the time of Dukes Wen and Xiang, Jin had presided over covenants in the central states; the reason its majesty sufficed to inspire awe and its kindness sufficed to win devotion was that its commands were rooted in righteousness. Why, then, by the reign of Duke Zhao, did it reverse this course? Therefore, at first, displaying its banners south of Zhu, it seized Yiru of Lu. Now, Yiru monopolized the state of Lu within and oppressed neighboring countries without; even had Jin proclaimed his crimes and put him to death, who would have said it was wrong? Yet as for Jin's true intention, how could it have been for this reason? It merely held that because Zhu and Ju failed to supply tribute on account of Lu, Lu was unprofitable to Jin: "We shall simply punish it, and that is all." Before long, because of Muzi's request, Jin sent Yiru back. Now, Jin had been unable to rescue Cai and had seized a kinsman on behalf of barbarians; even if it repented of its fault and sought to win favor through kindness, who would have said it was…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
宜乃晉之心則豈爲是哉徒謂土地猶大所命
能具是魯尚有利於我也吾綏之而已矣其怒
也以利則雖震疊以示威而人心不知所懲其
喜也以利則雖懷柔以示德而人心不知所勸
蓋晉之加於魯者即羊舌鮒求貨之心而魯之
中乎晉者亦猶司鐸射懷錦之智耳彼伯者之
於義雖云假之亦奚至棄利棄義如晉昭者哉
此春秋所深惡也雖然晉亦何利之有夫擇利
於己雖當安受其害者上下交征國鮮不危矣
===
卒之荀寅求貨而諸侯叛於外衛晉首難而大
夫叛於內晉幾無以爲國已利果安在也是故
夫子罕言利所以防亂源者其慮深哉
禮記
大樂與天地同和大禮與天地同節和故
百物不失節故祀天祭地明則有禮樂
幽則有鬼神如此則四海之內合敬同
愛矣
趙任
punctuated:
宜？乃晉之心則豈爲是哉？徒謂土地猶大，所命能具，是魯尚有利於我也，吾綏之而已矣。其怒也以利，則雖震疊以示威，而人心不知所懲；其喜也以利，則雖懷柔以示德，而人心不知所勸。蓋晉之加於魯者，即羊舌鮒求貨之心；而魯之中乎晉者，亦猶司鐸射懷錦之智耳。彼伯者之於義，雖云假之，亦奚至棄利棄義如晉昭者哉？此《春秋》所深惡也。雖然，晉亦何利之有？夫擇利於己，雖當，安受其害者？上下交征，國鮮不危矣。卒之荀寅求貨而諸侯叛於外，衛晉首難而大夫叛於內，晉幾無以爲國已，利果安在也？是故夫子罕言利，所以防亂源者，其慮深哉！

禮記
「大樂與天地同和，大禮與天地同節。和，故百物不失；節，故祀天祭地。明則有禮樂，幽則有鬼神。如此，則四海之內，合敬同愛矣。」
趙任
translation_en:
…proper? Yet how could Jin's intention have been for this reason? It merely reasoned that [Lu's] territory was still large and it could supply what was demanded; thus Lu was still profitable to us, so we shall simply pacify it and nothing more. When its anger was driven by profit, even though it struck terror to display its might, people's hearts did not know what to be warned against; when its pleasure was driven by profit, even though it showed leniency to display its kindness, people's hearts did not know what to be encouraged by. Indeed, what Jin imposed upon Lu was nothing other than Yangshe Fu's 羊舌鮒 mind of demanding bribes, and how Lu hit the mark with Jin was likewise merely the cleverness of Siduo She 司鐸射 concealing brocade in his bosom. Even though those hegemons were said to merely borrow righteousness, how could they go so far as to cast aside [righteousness for] profit, abandoning righteousness like Duke Zhao of Jin 晉昭? This is what the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) deeply abhors. Even so, what profit did Jin actually gain? When one chooses profit for oneself, even if it succeeds, who will quietly accept the harm? When superiors and inferiors mutually vie for profit, a state is rarely not endangered. In the end, Xun Yin 荀寅 demanded bribes and the feudal lords rebelled on the outside; Wei and Jin [at Jinyang] initiated the conflict [?] and the grandees rebelled on the inside. Jin was almost unable to survive as a state—where, indeed, was the profit? Therefore, the Master rarely spoke of profit; his consideration in preventing the source of disorder was profound indeed!

Record of Rites (Liji)
"Great music shares the harmony of Heaven and Earth; great rites share the regularity of Heaven and Earth. Through harmony, the myriad things do not lose their nature; through regularity, sacrifices are offered to Heaven and Earth. In the bright realm there are rites and music; in the dark realm there are ghosts and spirits. When it is like this, within the four seas all will unite in reverence and join in affection."
Zhao Ren 趙任

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導陳　批〔發禮樂通於天地人心意明透可錄〕
考試官教諭郭　批〔簡淨融貫題旨躍然〕
考試官教諭林　批〔精深〕
禮樂合造化而人心不能外焉夫禮樂之用大
矣成功所合即天地且不違而况於人乎嘗謂
禮樂未興道涵天地禮樂既備道洽生民盡自
其成功之合觀之彼玩天地之和而作者大樂
也樂之大者音律不足以囿之而與天地同其
和焉處天地之節而制者大禮也禮之大者經
===
曲不足以泥之而與天地同其節焉惟同和則
以和召和而覆天載地百物其咸若矣惟同節
則以序召序而祀天祭地萬物其各正矣是可
見禮樂天地一而已特明而聖人制作名曰禮
樂即鬼神之洩其精也幽而天地功用名曰鬼
神即禮樂之合其祕也禮樂之大如此而天下
人心夫孰能外之吾知四海之內無非天地之
民四海之民無非禮樂之用禮達而分定是故
作民敬焉蓋敬非一人而實敬以天下矣敬之
punctuated:
同考試官訓導陳　批〔發禮樂通於天地人心，意明透，可錄。〕
考試官教諭郭　批〔簡淨融貫，題旨躍然。〕
考試官教諭林　批〔精深。〕

禮樂合造化，而人心不能外焉。夫禮樂之用大矣，成功所合，即天地且不違，而况於人乎？嘗謂禮樂未興，道涵天地；禮樂既備，道洽生民。盡自其成功之合觀之：彼玩天地之和而作者，大樂也。樂之大者，音律不足以囿之，而與天地同其和焉。處天地之節而制者，大禮也。禮之大者，經曲不足以泥之，而與天地同其節焉。惟同和，則以和召和，而覆天載地，百物其咸若矣；惟同節，則以序召序，而祀天祭地，萬物其各正矣。是可見禮樂、天地一而已。特明而聖人制作，名曰禮樂，即鬼神之洩其精也；幽而天地功用，名曰鬼神，即禮樂之合其祕也。禮樂之大如此，而天下人心，夫孰能外之？吾知四海之內，無非天地之民；四海之民，無非禮樂之用。禮達而分定，是故作民敬焉，蓋敬非一人，而實敬以天下矣。敬之
translation_en:
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Chen's comment: [He brings out how rites and music communicate with Heaven, Earth, and the human mind; the ideas are clear and penetrating, worthy of recording.]
Examiner and Instructor Guo's comment: [Concise, pure, and thoroughly integrated; the purport of the theme leaps vividly to life.]
Examiner and Instructor Lin's comment: [Refined and profound.]

Rites and music accord with the creative transformations of nature, and the human mind cannot stand outside them. Great indeed is the function of rites and music! In the convergence of their perfected achievements, even Heaven and Earth do not deviate from them—how much less so human beings! It has been said that before rites and music arose, the Way was contained within Heaven and Earth; once rites and music were fully provided, the Way suffused the living people. Let us observe this entirely from the convergence of their perfected achievements: That which was created by contemplating the harmony of Heaven and Earth is great music. What is great in music cannot be confined merely to pitches and pipes, for it shares in the harmony of Heaven and Earth. That which was instituted by dwelling in the due measure of Heaven and Earth is great ritual. What is great in ritual cannot be bogged down merely in major principles and minor rules, for it shares in the due measure of Heaven and Earth. Because it shares in their harmony, harmony summons forth harmony, and between covering Heaven and supporting Earth, the hundred things all flourish in accord; because it shares in their due measure, order summons forth order, and in the sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, the myriad things each find their proper place. From this it can be seen that rites and music and Heaven and Earth are simply one. Only, in the realm of the manifest, what the sages have instituted are called rites and music, which are none other than ghosts and spirits revealing their essence; in the realm of the unseen, the functional operations of Heaven and Earth are called ghosts and spirits, which are none other than rites and music uniting with their mystery. Since the greatness of rites and music is such as this, among the minds of all people under Heaven, who could stand outside them? I know that within the four seas, there are none who are not the people of Heaven and Earth, and among the people of the four seas, there are none who are outside the function of rites and music. When ritual reaches everywhere, distinctions are settled, and thus it inspires reverence among the people; indeed, this reverence is not that of a single person, but is truly a reverence shared by all under Heaven. The uniting of reverence…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
合者其節之同者爲之乎樂行而向方是故作
民愛焉蓋愛非一人而實愛以天下矣愛之同
者其和之同者爲之乎先王之道禮樂可謂盛
矣猶未也天地之大也人猶有所憾卒神從天
而鬼從地斡玄工而濟海內禮樂同之禮樂者
聖人所以參三才贊化育之道也世無禮樂天
地能有全功乎是故禮樂之功于斯爲大
上必明正道以道民民道之而有功然後
取其什一故上用足而下不匱也
張和中
===
同考試官訓導陳　批〔此題博而無上下頗多頭緒不則陳〕
略是作獨渾融無迹而詞更精纖故取之
考試官教諭郭　批〔講不虛取節明盡〕
考試官教諭林　批〔可當〕
人君以道取民則上下兼利矣夫上用不能無
取於下也以正道之而惟正取焉此其所以兼
利歟見於燕義者若曰人知人君財用仰給於
天下不知其先天下而制之者有道也曷言乎
punctuated:
合者，其節之同者爲之乎？樂行而向方，是故作民愛焉。蓋愛非一人，而實愛以天下矣。愛之同者，其和之同者爲之乎？「先王之道，禮樂可謂盛矣。」猶未也。天地之大也，人猶有所憾，卒神從天而鬼從地，斡玄工而濟海內，禮樂同之。禮樂者，聖人所以參三才、贊化育之道也。世無禮樂，天地能有全功乎？是故禮樂之功，于斯爲大。

上必明正道以道民，民道之而有功，然後取其什一，故上用足而下不匱也。
張和中
同考試官訓導陳　批〔此題博而無上下，頗多頭緒，不則陳〕略。是作獨渾融無迹，而詞更精纖，故取之。
考試官教諭郭　批〔講不虛取，節明盡。〕
考試官教諭林　批〔可當。〕

人君以道取民，則上下兼利矣。夫上用不能無取於下也，以正道之而惟正取焉，此其所以兼利歟！見於《燕義》者若曰：人知人君財用仰給於天下，不知其先天下而制之者有道也。曷言乎？
translation_en:
… united is brought about by this shared restraint, is it not? When music prevails and the people turn toward what is right, it thereby stirs affection among the people. Indeed, such affection is not that of a single person, but is truly affection felt throughout the entire realm. That this affection is shared is brought about by this shared harmony, is it not? "In the Way of the Former Kings, rites and music may well be called flourishing." Yet that is not all. Great as heaven and earth are, men still find things to regret in them; ultimately, that the celestial spirits follow heaven and the terrestrial spirits follow earth, pivoting the mysterious work of creation and bringing aid to all within the seas—rites and music share in this. Rites and music are the Way by which the sage forms a triad with heaven and earth and assists in the transforming and nourishing processes of nature. If the world had no rites and music, could heaven and earth achieve their complete work? Therefore, the achievement of rites and music is in this respect the greatest.

"The ruler must first clarify the correct Way in order to guide the people; after the people follow this guidance and achieve results, he then takes one-tenth from them. Therefore the ruler's expenditure is sufficient and those below do not suffer want."
By Zhang Hezhong 張和中
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Chen, comments: [This topic is broad and lacks preceding and following context, having quite a few loose threads; otherwise it becomes either stale] or sketchy. This essay alone is seamlessly integrated without trace of artifice, and its diction is even more refined and delicate; therefore I selected it.
Examiner, Instructor Guo, comments: [It explains the meaning of "not taking in vain," with clear and thorough articulation of the sections.]
Examiner, Instructor Lin, comments: [Fitting and well-matched.]

When a ruler takes from the people according to the Way, both those above and those below benefit together. Now, for his expenditures, the one above cannot avoid taking from those below; yet if he guides them with correctness and takes only what is regular and proper, is this not why both benefit together? What is seen in the "Meaning of the District Symposium" (Yan yi 燕義) is as if to say: People know that the ruler's financial resources depend upon the realm for supply, without knowing that he first regulates things for the realm according to a Way. How may this be explained? …

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
上焉者以民生不能以自遂而制之田里驅之
耕焉粒食之原自我開之也以民事不可以緩
圖而教之樹畜率以勤焉小民之依自我貽之
也及夫男有餘粟女有餘布民率育矣而道之
者有成功然後粟米之征布縷之征十取一焉
而賦之者有定制將見一常在民一常在官既足以待邦
家之用而九常在民亦可以贍俯仰之資量入
以爲出上無乏用矣益於上者未始損於下王
人之導利上下其均被也已有財此有用國用
===
恒足矣盈於國者十一出於民什一之中制公
私其各足也已要之以上臨下卽取民孰敢不
從乃必道之於先其勞心勸民爲何如也道民
有功卽多取未爲不可乃必取之以制其約已
裕民爲何如也此其所以不虐取於下乎大抵
上下之際其分甚嚴所藉以通上下之情者莫
如禮禮乃其道之所繇者何噫言之矣不曰賢
君恭儉禮下取於民有制乎惟禮下故臣視之
如腹心取民有制故民戴之如父母此丁濟光
punctuated: 上焉者，以民生不能以自遂，而制之田里，驅之耕焉，粒食之原，自我開之也；以民事不可以緩圖，而教之樹畜，率以勤焉，小民之依，自我貽之也。及夫男有餘粟，女有餘布，民率育矣，而道之者有成功；然後粟米之征，布縷之征，十取一焉，而賦之者有定制。將見一常在民，一常在官，既足以待邦家之用，而九常在民，亦可以贍俯仰之資。量入以爲出，上無乏用矣；益於上者，未始損於下，王人之導利，上下其均被也已。有財此有用，國用恒足矣；盈於國者十一，出於民，什一之中制，公私其各足也已。要之，以上臨下，卽取民孰敢不從？乃必道之於先，其勞心勸民爲何如也！道民有功，卽多取未爲不可，乃必取之以制，其約已裕民爲何如也！此其所以不虐取於下乎？大抵上下之際，其分甚嚴，所藉以通上下之情者，莫如禮，禮乃其道之所繇者。何噫言之矣，不曰「賢君恭儉禮下，取於民有制」乎？惟禮下，故臣視之如腹心；取民有制，故民戴之如父母。此丁濟光
translation_en: …Those above recognize that the people's livelihood cannot be fulfilled on its own, and so they regulate their fields and homesteads and urge them to plow; thus the source of their grain food is opened up by us. Recognizing that the people's affairs cannot be planned for with delay, they teach them arboriculture and animal husbandry and lead them with diligence; thus the reliance of the common people is bequeathed by us. When it comes to the point that men have surplus grain and women have surplus cloth, the people are all nourished, and the effort of guiding them has achieved success. Only then is there the levy of grain and the levy of cloth and silk, taking one part in ten, so that the taxation has a fixed regulation. One will see that while [nine parts are?] selalu with the people [text reads: one part is always with the people] and one part is always with the officials, it is already sufficient to meet the expenditures of the state, while the nine parts remaining always with the people are likewise enough to supply the resources for supporting parents and family. By measuring revenues to determine expenditures, the ruler above has no shortage of supplies; what benefits those above never diminishes those below, and through the king's channeling of benefits, both superior and inferior share in them equally. Having wealth, there is thus resources for use, and the state's supplies are constantly sufficient; what fills the state is the one-tenth drawn from the people, and through the moderate regulation of the tithe, both public and private needs are each satisfied. In sum, when those above oversee those below, even if they simply took from the people, who would dare not obey? Yet they must first guide them—how great is their painstaking care in encouraging the people! When guiding the people has achieved success, even taking more would not be impossible; yet they must take from them according to fixed regulation—how great is their restraint of self and generosity toward the people! Is this not why they do not tyrannically extract from those below? Generally speaking, in the relationship between superior and inferior, the distinction of rank is very strict, and what is relied upon to communicate the feelings of superior and inferior is nothing better than ritual propriety, for ritual propriety is that from which the Way proceeds. He Yi [?; likely garbled for 賈誼 Jia Yi] spoke of this: did he not say, "A worthy ruler is respectful and frugal, treats his subordinates with ritual propriety, and takes from the people according to fixed regulation"? Because he treats his subordinates with ritual propriety, his ministers regard him as their heart and vitals; because he takes from the people according to fixed regulation, the people look up to him as their father and mother. This is the [meaning of the radiant] way of downward succor [garbled: 丁濟 for 下濟]…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
明之義容保無疆之治也君天下者其尚諸
第貳場
論
臣事君以忠
杜華先
同考試官訓導解　批〔發揮事君以忠義精深透徹而格調〕
更斟酌而京閣中舖作者宜式
考試官教諭郭　批〔理遂而調古〕
考試官教諭林　批〔高古不羣〕
===
事君以自顯者人臣也臣道之難非其遇之難
也又非其材之難能辨其職之難也又非其敢
犯顏強諫能不懾於威之難也反之已而盡其
所以事君者難也故已者人臣之所輸也不可
私也已在於建功則不建其功者弗爲矣已在
於立名則不立其名者弗爲矣已在於潔身則
不潔其身者弗爲矣之數者於忠似也而其實
非也故忠也者以盡其已也已而能盡斯謂之
忠臣矣非必捐身死難顯主而揚名也於已而
punctuated:
明之義，容保無疆之治也。君天下者，其尚諸！

第貳場

論

臣事君以忠

杜華先

同考試官訓導解　批〔發揮事君以忠，義精深透徹，而格調〕更斟酌，而京閣中舖作者宜式。
考試官教諭郭　批〔理遂而調古。〕
考試官教諭林　批〔高古不羣。〕

事君以自顯者，人臣也。臣道之難，非其遇之難也；又非其材之難，能辨其職之難也；又非其敢犯顏強諫，能不懾於威之難也；反之已而盡其所以事君者難也。故已者，人臣之所輸也，不可私也。已在於建功，則不建其功者弗爲矣；已在於立名，則不立其名者弗爲矣；已在於潔身，則不潔其身者弗爲矣。之數者，於忠似也，而其實非也。故忠也者，以盡其已也。已而能盡，斯謂之忠臣矣，非必捐身死難、顯主而揚名也；於已而
translation_en:
… meaning of "Mutual Promotion and Illumination" (下濟光明), and the governance of accommodating and protecting without bound. May he who rules the world esteem this!

Second Session

Discourse

"A minister serves his prince with loyalty" (臣事君以忠)

Du Huaxian 杜華先

Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Xie 解 comments: 〔He develops the theme of serving one's prince with loyalty with profound and penetrating meaning, while the style〕 is even more measured; writers in the examination halls who lay out their essays should take this as a model [?].
Examiner Instructor Guo 郭 comments: 〔The reasoning is thorough and the tone is antique.〕
Examiner Instructor Lin 林 comments: 〔Lofty, antique, and standing apart from the crowd.〕

One who serves a prince in order to distinguish himself is a minister. What is difficult in the way of a minister is not the difficulty of finding a favorable encounter; nor is it the difficulty of having talent and being able to manage one's duties; nor is it the difficulty of daring to brave the sovereign's countenance with forceful remonstrance and remaining unafraid of his majesty. Rather, what is difficult is to turn back upon oneself and exhaust all where-with one serves the prince. Therefore, the self is what a minister offers up; it must not be kept for private ends. If the self is set upon establishing merit, then whatever does not establish one's merit one will refuse to do. If the self is set upon establishing a reputation, then whatever does not establish one's reputation one will refuse to do. If the self is set upon keeping one's person pure, then whatever does not keep one's person pure one will refuse to do. These several attitudes resemble loyalty, yet in reality they are not. Therefore, loyalty means exhausting one's self. When the self can be exhausted, this is what is called a loyal minister—it is not necessarily a matter of sacrificing one's life and dying in a crisis to bring glory to one's ruler and spread one's own name. When in regard to oneself…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
不盡斯謂之私臣矣非必尸位固寵植黨而行
私也臣人者不可不察也且君臣之所以合者
何由也義也上不能自爲而任人以分其治下
不能自顯而待上以行其術其厚之爵祿而非
以市之也其効之死力而非以要之也故臣之
於君也猶手足之於心也心運於內而手足聽
於外所欲則爲之求所患則爲之捍非有冀而
徇之有較而趨之也故曰爲人臣者無以有已
有所冀者有已也有所較者有已也未有已之
===
不忘而能忠者也且夫職難共而可循也心易
勉而不可襲也經國利人非材弗能也圖事建
功非智弗能也然而能行之者忠也故夫臣之
爲道所就亦各有等也上之而樹鴻猷駿烈揚
明主無窮之名次之而奉法循理以無忘職業
外之而胃風雨衝矢石有斬將搴旗之功內之
而補過拾遺著伉直之節此其建立豈闒茸者
之能爲而苟合者之能辦哉然功因勢成名以
時立使其行之不本於忠而徒出於遇合之心
punctuated: 不盡，斯謂之私臣矣，非必尸位固寵、植黨而行私也。臣人者不可不察也。且君臣之所以合者何由也？義也。上不能自爲，而任人以分其治；下不能自顯，而待上以行其術。其厚之爵祿，而非以市之也；其効之死力，而非以要之也。故臣之於君也，猶手足之於心也。心運於內，而手足聽於外；所欲則爲之求，所患則爲之捍，非有冀而徇之、有較而趨之也。故曰：「爲人臣者無以有已。」有所冀者，有已也；有所較者，有已也。未有已之不忘而能忠者也。且夫職難共而可循也，心易勉而不可襲也。經國利人，非材弗能也；圖事建功，非智弗能也；然而能行之者，忠也。故夫臣之爲道，所就亦各有等也：上之而樹鴻猷駿烈，揚明主無窮之名；次之而奉法循理，以無忘職業；外之而胃風雨、衝矢石，有斬將搴旗之功；內之而補過拾遺，著伉直之節。此其建立，豈闒茸者之能爲，而苟合者之能辦哉？然功因勢成，名以時立，使其行之不本於忠，而徒出於遇合之心，
translation_en: …does not devote himself completely, he is called a self-interested minister; it is not necessarily that he merely holds a sinecure, clings to favor, forms factions, and pursues private ends. Those who serve as ministers cannot fail to examine this. Moreover, by what means are ruler and minister joined together? By righteousness. The superior cannot do everything himself, and so he employs others to share in his governance; the subordinate cannot distinguish himself on his own, and so he awaits the superior to put his arts into practice. When the ruler bestows generous ranks and emoluments upon him, it is not to buy him; when the minister exerts his utmost strength unto death for him, it is not to make demands of him. Therefore, the minister's relation to the ruler is like that of the hands and feet to the mind. The mind operates within, and the hands and feet obey without; what it desires, they seek for it, and what it fears, they ward off for it—not following it out of some hope for reward, nor hurrying toward it out of some calculation. Thus it is said: "One who serves as a minister must not possess a self." One who has hopes of gain possesses a self; one who makes calculations possesses a self. There has never been anyone who could not forget himself and yet was able to be loyal. Furthermore, official duties are difficult to fulfill yet can be followed by routine; the mind is easy to urge on yet cannot be feigned. Ordering the state and benefiting the people cannot be done without talent; planning affairs and establishing merit cannot be done without wisdom; yet that by which one is able to carry them out is loyalty. Therefore, in the Way of the minister, what each accomplishes also has its respective grade: at the highest, establishing grand plans and illustrious achievements, exalting the boundless fame of an enlightened ruler; next, upholding the laws and following principle, so as not to neglect one's official duties; in external service, braving wind and rain and charging through arrows and stones, achieving the merit of slaying enemy generals and capturing their banners; in internal service, remedying faults and supplying omissions, manifesting the integrity of forthrightness. Could such accomplishments be achieved by base and mediocre men, or managed by those who merely curry favor? Yet merit is accomplished through circumstance, and fame is established through timing; if one's actions are not rooted in loyalty, but issue merely from a mind set on opportunistic favor,…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
則求其名而不責其實得其一而不顧其二所
謂材智者將不爲君謀而所謂功名者徒矜竹
帛之光矣人主將何賴於此勳名競盛而精白
弗殫也所表樹展錯者由於自爲也嗟夫世之
爲忠臣者何鮮焉較尺寸於功利之途而爭錙
銖於毀譽之口以得失爲低昂計利害爲進退
操術者曰我能爲君經國家治官府闢地廣賦
圖一切可就之功而患之後發者弗慮矣善兵
者曰我能爲君禦強敵揚威萬里近靜四疆之
===
塵遠雪往年之恥而民之暴骨者弗軫矣負勇
者曰我能守死亡家不顧捐生不恤婞直者曰
我能直諫鈇鉞弗懼竄荒弗悔夫人君果何取
其功死觸禍哉而世猶稱之曰利非彼莫興患
非彼莫解義非彼莫明節非彼莫振是亦不察
之過也是故急談管商之功誇詡孫吳之略高
慕夷讓之風期延茅焦之譽偉節異行爚然光
明而不顧上下之一體寮友之一家此人臣之
利也非天下之長策也嗚呼吾嘗求古聖之
punctuated: 則求其名而不責其實，得其一而不顧其二。所謂材智者，將不爲君謀；而所謂功名者，徒矜竹帛之光矣。人主將何賴於此？勳名競盛而精白弗殫也，所表樹展錯者由於自爲也。嗟夫！世之爲忠臣者，何鮮焉！較尺寸於功利之途，而爭錙銖於毀譽之口，以得失爲低昂，計利害爲進退。操術者曰：「我能爲君經國家、治官府、闢地廣賦，圖一切可就之功。」而患之後發者，弗慮矣。善兵者曰：「我能爲君禦強敵、揚威萬里，近靜四疆之塵，遠雪往年之恥。」而民之暴骨者，弗軫矣。負勇者曰：「我能守死，亡家不顧，捐生不恤。」婞直者曰：「我能直諫，鈇鉞弗懼，竄荒弗悔。」夫人君果何取其功死觸禍哉？而世猶稱之曰：「利非彼莫興，患非彼莫解，義非彼莫明，節非彼莫振。」是亦不察之過也。是故急談管、商之功，誇詡孫、吳之略，高慕夷、讓之風，期延茅、焦之譽，偉節異行，爚然光明，而不顧上下之一體、寮友之一家，此人臣之利也，非天下之長策也。嗚呼！吾嘗求古聖之
translation_en: …then they will seek the reputation without demanding the reality, and grasp one aspect without regard for another. Those who are called men of talent and wisdom will not plan on behalf of their ruler, and what they call achievement and fame will merely be for boasting of their glory in the historical records on bamboo and silk. How can a ruler rely on this? When meritorious fame is competitively pursued, pure and unblemished devotion is not exhausted; what they establish, display, and put into practice arises from acting for themselves. Alas, how rare are those in the world who are truly loyal ministers! They haggle over inches and feet on the path of utility and profit, and contend over grains and ounces in the mouths of praise and blame; they rise and fall according to gain and loss, and advance or retreat by calculating advantage and harm. Those who wield statecraft techniques say, "I can manage the state, govern the official bureaus, open up territory, and expand revenues for the ruler, planning all manner of achievable successes"—yet they give no thought to the calamities that will erupt later. Those skilled in warfare say, "I can fend off powerful enemies for the ruler and project his majesty ten thousand li, settling the dust on the four borders nearby and wiping away the shame of past years afar"—yet they feel no sorrow for the people whose bones are left bleaching in the sun. Those who pride themselves on bravery say, "I can hold fast to death, without regard for the ruin of my family and without pity for the sacrifice of my life." Those who are obstinately forthright say, "I can remonstrate bluntly, unafraid of the executioner's axe and unrepentant if banished to the wilds." Yet what use, after all, does a ruler have for their seeking achievement through death or courting disaster? Still, the world praises them, saying, "Without them, profit cannot be promoted; without them, calamity cannot be resolved; without them, righteousness cannot be made clear; without them, integrity cannot be aroused." This, too, is the fault of failing to examine the matter closely. Therefore, eagerly discussing the achievements of Guan Zhong and Shang Yang, boasting of the military strategies of Sun Wu and Wu Qi, loftily admiring the demeanor of Boyi and Yu Rang, and hoping to extend the fame of Mao Jiao—with grand integrity and extraordinary conduct shining brightly, yet without regard for the ruler and those below being a single body, or colleagues in office being a single family—this is to the advantage of the minister, not a long-term policy for the Empire. Alas! I have sought out how the ancient sages…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
爲人臣矣乘元凱誅大族而不自以爲嫌躬胼
胝平水土而不自以爲勞攻鳴條迎桐宮而不
自以爲專輔台德揚休命而不自以爲諛欲止
君之過則寧成桐葉之戲笲彰君之美則寧爲
嘉禾之獻憚畢成之竭則寧後園成之克避去
國之名則寧受爲肉之謗其心何心也忠也利
其君不計其私務其實不徇其迹也故曰勇者
不必死節怯夫慕義何處不勉焉則惟以其心
諒之也是以原思疏食不厭魯人稱其介公孫
===
弘布被粟飯而汲黯斥其詐非布衣之節易成
而卿相之名難立也又非以汲黯之直苛於責
當世之臣也情以自潔著則鄉人可信貧士行
以釣名立則直臣不滿鉏公此忠與不忠之別
也雖然臣之自靖其盡忠亦可傾矣設君不信
之則如之何曰是未明君臣之義也君人也厚
禮以招士高爵以待賢公之庶職而望之治此
豈有意於過責其臣哉信而見疑忠而被謗則
邪臣導之也人但知平公之不見孟軻而不
punctuated: 爲人臣矣：乘元凱，誅大族，而不自以爲嫌；躬胼胝，平水土，而不自以爲勞；攻鳴條，迎桐宮，而不自以爲專；輔台德，揚休命，而不自以爲諛。欲止君之過，則寧成桐葉之戲；笲彰君之美，則寧爲嘉禾之獻；憚畢成之竭，則寧後園成之克；避去國之名，則寧受爲肉之謗。其心何心也？忠也。利其君，不計其私；務其實，不徇其迹也。故曰：「勇者不必死節，怯夫慕義，何處不勉焉。」則惟以其心諒之也。是以原思疏食不厭，魯人稱其介；公孫弘布被粟飯，而汲黯斥其詐。非布衣之節易成，而卿相之名難立也，又非以汲黯之直苛於責當世之臣也。情以自潔著，則鄉人可信貧士；行以釣名立，則直臣不滿鉏公。此忠與不忠之別也。雖然，臣之自靖，其盡忠亦可傾矣，設君不信之，則如之何？曰：是未明君臣之義也。君人也，厚禮以招士，高爵以待賢，公之庶職而望之治，此豈有意於過責其臣哉？信而見疑，忠而被謗，則邪臣導之也。人但知平公之不見孟軻，而不
translation_en: …serving as a minister! They promoted the Eight Worthies and Eight Talents (Yuankai 元凱) and executed the Four Great Clans without considering themselves open to suspicion; they personally calloused their hands and feet to pacify the waters and lands without considering themselves overworked; they attacked at Mingtiao 鳴條 and welcomed the king back from the Tong Palace (Tonggong 桐宮) without considering themselves domineering; they assisted the royal virtue and proclaimed the gracious mandate without considering themselves sycophantic. When wishing to stop their sovereign's error, they would rather fulfill the playful investiture with a paulownia leaf; when wishing [?] to manifest their sovereign's goodness, they would rather present the auspicious grain; fearing the exhaustion of a complete victory [?], they would rather defer the conquest [?]; avoiding the reputation of leaving the state over a principle, they would rather bear the slander of leaving over a share of sacrificial meat. What sort of mind was theirs? It was loyalty. They benefited their sovereign without calculating their own private interests; they attended to the substance without clinging to outward traces. Therefore it is said: "A brave man need not die for a principle; when a timid man admires righteousness, where will he not exert himself?" It is simply a matter of judging them by their intentions. Thus Yuan Si 原思 was content with coarse food, and the people of Lu 魯 praised his integrity; Gongsun Hong 公孫弘 used a cloth quilt and ate unhulled millet, yet Ji An 汲黯 denounced his deceit. This was not because the integrity of a commoner is easy to achieve while the reputation of a chief minister is hard to establish, nor was it because Ji An in his bluntness was overly harsh in reproaching the ministers of his day. When one's disposition is made manifest through genuine self-purification, fellow villagers can trust an impoverished scholar; when one's conduct is established by fishing for fame, an upright minister will be dissatisfied with a venerable lord [?]. This is the distinction between loyalty and disloyalty. Even so, when a minister composes himself in devotion, his utmost loyalty may well be poured forth [?]; suppose his sovereign does not trust him, then what is to be done? I say: this comes from not understanding the righteous bond between sovereign and minister. One who rules over men uses generous courtesies to summon scholars, high ranks to await the worthy, shares with them the myriad offices, and hopes for good governance from them—how could he have any intention of excessively finding fault with his ministers? When a trustworthy minister is suspected and a loyal minister is slandered, it is because wicked ministers have led the sovereign astray. People only know that Duke Ping (Pinggong 平公) failed to see Meng Ke 孟軻 (Mencius), and do not…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
知沮之者臧倉也知頊襄之放流屈原而不□
讒之者上官大夫也知文帝之疎賈誼而不知
短之者絳灌之屬也忠臣之道豈獨在于與諸
賢而不可責之變人之流哉傳曰一齊人傅之
衆楚人咻之故一人之忠人可自勉也衆臣之
忠人不可共期也噫安得舉世皆忠臣而共佐
大明君也哉
表
擬
===
上以
南郊齋宮
親製
大報歌示輔臣等奉
詔恭和成
進呈表〔嘉靖十三年〕
同考試官教諭葛　批〔揄揚〕
盛美意甚悉而調更典重似宋人體錄之
于若瀛
punctuated:
知沮之者臧倉也；知頊襄之放流屈原，而不□讒之者上官大夫也；知文帝之疎賈誼，而不知短之者絳、灌之屬也。忠臣之道，豈獨在于與諸賢，而不可責之變人之流哉？《傳》曰：「一齊人傅之，衆楚人咻之。」故一人之忠，人可自勉也；衆臣之忠，人不可共期也。噫！安得舉世皆忠臣，而共佐大明君也哉！

表

擬上以南郊齋宮親製《大報歌》示輔臣等，奉詔恭和成，進呈表〔嘉靖十三年〕

同考試官教諭葛　批〔揄揚盛美，意甚悉，而調更典重，似宋人體，錄之。〕
于若瀛
translation_en:
…know that the one who thwarted it was Zang Cang 臧倉; they know that King Qingxiang 頃襄王 [transcription reads Xuxiang 頊襄] banished Qu Yuan 屈原, without [knowing] that the one who slandered him was the Grand Master Shangguan 上官大夫; they know that Emperor Wen 文帝 distanced himself from Jia Yi 賈誼, without knowing that those who disparaged him were the likes of the Marquis of Jiang 絳侯 [Zhou Bo 周勃] and Guan Ying 灌嬰. How could the Way of the loyal minister lie solely with myself and the various worthies, and not be demanded of the likes of favored courtiers [reading 變人 as 嬖人]? The commentary [Mencius] says: "One man of Qi tutors him, while a multitude of men of Chu clamor around him." Therefore, the loyalty of a single person is something one can strive for oneself, whereas the loyalty of the multitude of ministers is something one cannot expect from all alike. Alas! How can we bring it about that the whole world consists of loyal ministers who together assist our great and enlightened ruler!

Memorial (Biao 表)

A composition imitating a memorial presented upon the Emperor showing the Grand Secretaries and others the "Song of the Great Sacrifice of Thanksgiving" (Dabao ge 大報歌), personally composed in the Palace of Fasting at the Southern Suburb, and their respectfully harmonizing with it in verses in obedience to the imperial edict (13th year of the Jiajing 嘉靖 reign [1534]).

Associate Examiner and Confucian Instructor Ge 葛 comments: [It extols the grand splendor with very thorough meaning, and its tone is moreover classical and weighty, resembling the style of the Song dynasty; we record it for publication.]
Yu Ruoying 于若瀛

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭郭　批〔表有典則非直以四六工者〕
考試官教諭林　批〔莊重無一剩語〕
嘉靖十三年十一月某日臣某等伏遇
南郊禮成蒙
皇上頒示
齋官
御製
大報歌
命臣等和恭撰成
===
進呈者伏以
帝德靈承禮特隆于禋祀
聖心昭假歌益勑于時幾
睿藻布雲漢之章臣謨資
天工之代服膺交儆拜手載賡竊聞䜺禱堯堂
欽昊詠神人之暢齋居武臚祀天銘敬義
之書后稷述功于生民成王誦德于基命
嘆魯郊非禮徒祝閟宮慨秦畤不經空碑
岱石白麟赤鴈紛員夸漢武之歌玉露金
punctuated:
考試官教諭郭　批〔表有典則，非直以四六工者。〕
考試官教諭林　批〔莊重，無一剩語。〕
嘉靖十三年十一月某日，臣某等伏遇南郊禮成，蒙皇上頒示齋官御製《大報歌》，命臣等和，恭撰成進呈者。伏以帝德靈承，禮特隆于禋祀；聖心昭假，歌益勑于時幾。睿藻布雲漢之章，臣謨資天工之代。服膺交儆，拜手載賡。竊聞䜺禱堯堂，欽昊詠神人之暢；齋居武臚，祀天銘敬義之書。后稷述功于《生民》，成王誦德于基命。嘆魯郊非禮，徒祝《閟宮》；慨秦畤不經，空碑岱石。白麟赤鴈，紛員夸漢武之歌；玉露金
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Guo commented: 〔This memorial adheres to classic standards; it is not merely skillful in four-six parallel prose.〕
Examiner and Instructor Lin commented: 〔Solemn and dignified, without a single superfluous word.〕
On a certain day in the eleventh month of the thirteenth year of the Jiajing reign [1534], your servants so-and-so and others, humbly encountering the completion of the rites at the Southern Suburb, were favored with His Majesty's promulgation of the "Song of the Great Requital" (Dabao ge), Imperially composed in the Hall of Fasting [reading 齋宮 for 齋官], and were commanded to write verses in harmony with it, which we have reverently composed to present to the throne:
We humbly consider that the Imperial virtue efficaciously receives Heaven's mandate, and its rites are especially grand in the pure sacrifice; the Sacred mind brightly reaches on high, and its song further admonishes attention to timely governing. The Imperial literary grace spreads forth chapters like the Milky Way, while the counsels of your servants assist in acting on behalf of Heaven's work. Clasping this to our breasts in mutual admonition, we bow our heads to the hands and continue the song.
We have humbly heard that in offering prayers in the hall of Yao, reverencing vast Heaven, one sang of the harmony between spirits and men; in dwelling in abstinence in the chamber of King Wu [?], sacrificing to Heaven, one inscribed writings on reverence and righteousness. Hou Ji's merits were recounted in "The Birth of Our People" (Shengmin), and King Cheng's virtue was chanted in receiving the Mandate. One sighs that the suburban sacrifice of Lu was contrary to ritual, merely offering prayers in the "Solemn Temple" (Bigong); one laments that the altars of Qin were uncanonical, vainly erecting steles of Mount Dai stone. White unicorns and red wild geese were boastfully lauded in profusion in the songs of Emperor Wu of Han; jade dew and golden…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
卑江濊俊簡文之頌誣坤元之芳美賈玷
唐典裕冬序之晏溫惟工宋制蓋縟儀之
馨香之德艷曲布嚴誨之辭精意罔達于
彼蒼昌言爲咨于汝爾信
聖人爲能饗
帝非
天子則不考文玆蓋伏遇
皇帝陛下
乾始統天
===
玄元配極
篤昭事之敬翼翼彌小于文心
重嚴禋之儀尊尊益備于周道
圜丘一復方國咸寧實寵荷于
蕃釐諭懋昭夫
明德勤欽
天之戒永祇受于露零動謌
帝之思每肅將于景至玆當
靈壇四啓
punctuated: 卑江濊俊簡文之頌，誣坤元之芳美，賈玷唐典；裕冬序之晏溫，惟工宋制。蓋縟儀之馨香之德，艷曲布嚴誨之辭，精意罔達于彼蒼，昌言爲咨于汝爾。信聖人爲能饗帝，非天子則不考文。玆蓋伏遇皇帝陛下：乾始統天，玄元配極。篤昭事之敬，翼翼彌小于文心；重嚴禋之儀，尊尊益備于周道。圜丘一復，方國咸寧，實寵荷于蕃釐，諭懋昭夫明德。勤欽天之戒，永祇受于露零；動謌帝之思，每肅將于景至。玆當靈壇四啓，
translation_en:
…and [golden] cups and brimming streams [?] showed off the eulogies of Emperor Jianwen; fabricating the fragrant beauties of the Earthly Origin, Jia [Zeng?] blemished the canons of the Tang; and celebrating the mild warmth of the winter season, they were merely skilled in the institutions of the Song. For with elaborate rites [lacking?] the virtue of fragrant offerings, and ornate songs spreading words of solemn admonition [?], their sincere intent failed to reach the Azure Heaven, and how could glorious words be consulted with you? Truly, only the Sage is able to make offerings to the Lord on High, and none but the Son of Heaven examines the cultural institutions.

Now we humbly encounter Your Majesty the Emperor: with the Creative Beginning governing Heaven, and the Profound Origin matching the Supreme Ultimate. Deepening the reverence of bright service, Your cautious devotion is ever more humble than the mind of King Wen; attaching importance to the rites of solemn sacrifice, Your honoring of the honorable is ever more complete than the Way of Zhou. Once the Round Mound was restored, the regions and states all enjoyed peace; truly favored with abundant blessings, You issued instructions to strenuously manifest bright virtue. Diligent in the admonition to revere Heaven, You forever respectfully receive the falling dew; stirred by thoughts of singing praises to the Lord on High, You always solemnly perform the rites at the arrival of the winter solstice. Now, when the Numinous Altar is opened on all four sides,…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
仙蹕重臨
法駕佺于甘泉鉤陳衛于太乙肆
陵龍以入閶闔迴
静默而居蜵蜎洌穆希夷想監觀之有赫高
明亭毒睠覆幬之無私
大報之德聿懷
永言之歌賡作既而柴燔紫焰瓚祼黃流垓
陛秩于三登笙鏞調于九奏
洪歆式就介福攸歸迴日馭于
===
天扉返霓旌乎
帝闕華夷胥慶允
熙事之備成言起交脩遂
宸章之敷錫勒穠而標甲午
御姬曆之十三年八日以紀新冬
乘乾陽之初九象隆恩洪眷善則稱
天菲質綿材過惟歸己欲康民以圖報稱慭無
學以出治源夙夜慕周后之緝熙曰予始
終惕厲朝夕望殷臣之啓沃諮爾左右弼
punctuated: 仙蹕重臨。法駕佺于甘泉，鉤陳衛于太乙。肆陵龍以入閶闔，迴静默而居蜵蜎。洌穆希夷，想監觀之有赫；高明亭毒，睠覆幬之無私。大報之德聿懷，永言之歌賡作。既而柴燔紫焰，瓚祼黃流；垓陛秩于三登，笙鏞調于九奏。洪歆式就，介福攸歸。迴日馭于天扉，返霓旌乎帝闕。華夷胥慶，允熙事之備成；言起交脩，遂宸章之敷錫。勒穠而標甲午，御姬曆之十三年；八日以紀新冬，乘乾陽之初九。象隆恩洪眷，善則稱天；菲質綿材，過惟歸己。欲康民以圖報稱，慭無學以出治源。夙夜慕周后之緝熙，曰：「予始終惕厲」；朝夕望殷臣之啓沃，諮：「爾左右弼…
translation_en: …and the immortal cortège visits once again. The Imperial Carriage halts in reverence [?] at the Ganquan Palace, while the Gouchen constellation guards the Taiyi altar. Thus, ascending with dragon steeds to enter the gates of heaven, His Majesty withdraws into quietude and dwells in deep, coiled stillness [?]. In pure solemnity and subtle silence, He contemplates the radiant majesty of Heaven's watchful gaze; before its lofty brilliance and nurturing power, He reflects on the impartiality of its overarching canopy. Cherishing the virtue of the Great Recompense, He composes anew songs of enduring praise. Thereafter, the sacrificial pyre blazes with purple flames, and the jade libation ladle pours forth the golden wine; the terraced steps are ascended in regular order three times, and the reed organs and great bells harmonize through nine performances of music. The grand offering is thus accomplished, and great blessings descend upon Him. He turns back the sun-chariot from the portals of Heaven and returns the rainbow banners to the Imperial Palace. Chinese and non-Chinese alike rejoice together, recognizing the complete fulfillment of this glorious rite; words arise urging mutual cultivation, and thereupon His Imperial composition is graciously bestowed. Engraved in rich splendor [?] and dated to the jiawu year, when His Majesty reigns in the thirteenth year of the Zhou calendar; on the eighth day marking the new winter, riding the nascent yang of the first nine line of the Qian hexagram. Depicting the exalted grace and vast favor, He attributes all goodness to Heaven; speaking of modest substance and slender talent, He takes all faults solely upon Himself. Desiring to bring peace to the people so as to repay Heaven's grace, He laments lacking the learning from which the source of governance flows. Morning and night He emulates the radiant, continuous敬 of the Zhou sovereign, saying: "From beginning to end, I remain vigilant and cautious"; day and night He hopes for the enlightening counsel of the Yin ministers, consulting them: "You, my left and right, assist…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
丞期躋世道于雍雍用答
皇禧之盻蠁詞不繁而旨已遠實愈大而衷益
虔更僭
綸綍之宜爰藉鹽梅之和周詩之丐言莫落何
以加焉虞歌之元首股肱爲可繼也竊念
臣等對越無秉文之德侍從非獻賦之才
幸風馬光際于
靈斿娩雲龍聲應于
聖作黃鍾協響豈庸瓦釜之鳴蒼璧聯輝曷克
===
瓊瑤之報忠欲傾于葵藿曲聊和夫里巴
希元和聖德之詩不嫌淺薄謝宣室鬼神
之對無取幽深彌性遂歌惟效卷阿之梧
鳳敬天申誡庶酬小毖之桃蟲伏願
有密單心
幾康永命卬盛登豆深惟肇祀之規我享牛
羊祇服畏威之訓
滋百神之貺以霑海寓
萃萬國之驩以格
punctuated: 丞，期躋世道于雍雍，用答皇禧之盻蠁。詞不繁而旨已遠，實愈大而衷益虔。更僭綸綍之宜，爰藉鹽梅之和。周詩之「丐言莫落」，何以加焉；虞歌之「元首股肱」，爲可繼也。竊念臣等對越無秉文之德，侍從非獻賦之才。幸風馬光際于靈斿，娩雲龍聲應于聖作。黃鍾協響，豈庸瓦釜之鳴；蒼璧聯輝，曷克瓊瑤之報。忠欲傾于葵藿，曲聊和夫里巴。希《元和聖德》之詩，不嫌淺薄；謝宣室鬼神之對，無取幽深。彌性遂歌，惟效《卷阿》之梧鳳；敬天申誡，庶酬《小毖》之桃蟲。伏願有密單心，幾康永命。卬盛登豆，深惟肇祀之規；我享牛羊，祇服畏威之訓。滋百神之貺以霑海寓，萃萬國之驩以格
translation_en:
…aides, hoping to elevate the way of the world to harmonious peace, and thereby answer the abundant blessings of Imperial felicity. The words are not prolix, yet their purport is already far-reaching; the reality is all the greater, and the inner heart all the more reverent. Moreover, presuming upon the appropriateness of Your silken rescripts, You rely on the harmonious seasoning of salt and plum. What could surpass the “seeking of words on setting out plans” [访落] in the Odes of Zhou? And the song of Yu on “the head and the limbs” can indeed be continued!

We humbly reflect that, in standing before theAugust Presence, Your servants lack the virtue of upholding King Wen’s pattern, and in attending Your retinue, we do not possess the talent for presenting rhapsodies. Fortunately, like wind-borne steeds, we have gloriously encountered Your numinous standards; ashamed, like clouds following the dragon, we echo in response to Your sacred composition. When the Yellow Bell chimes in harmony, what use is the clanging of an earthen pot? When azure bi-jades join their splendor, how could we manage a repayment of precious jades? Yet our loyalty wishes to incline like the sunflower and bean leaf toward the sun, so in our rustic tunes we tentatively harmonize like the songs of the village and Ba. Aspiring to the Poem on the Sacred Virtue of the Yuanhe Era, we do not shrink from our own shallowness; declining the reply on ghosts and spirits in the Xuan Chamber, we make no claim to dark profundity. Fulfilling our natures and singing forth, we merely imitate the phoenix on the parasol tree in “Curving Slope” (Juan’e); revering Heaven and reiterating admonition, we hope to answer the allegory of the wren in “A Small Precaution” (Xiaobi).

We humbly pray that You will apply Your whole heart in quietude, and perpetuate the Mandate through vigilance and peace. As we fill the platters and vessels, may You deeply ponder the regulations of the founding sacrifices; as we offer the oxen and sheep, may You reverently submit to the precept of fearing Heaven’s majesty. Increase the gifts of the hundred spirits so as to moisten all within the seas; gather the joy of the myriad states so as to reach…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
穹旻靈集山川甘雨繩皇皇之祝光騰日月卿
雲續旦旦之歌臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹以所和詩隨
表上
進以
聞
第叄場
策
===
第一問　柳佐
同考試官教諭徐　批〔我〕
皇上本精意以爭泰為典子能鋪張而揚厲之而末段尤見忠悃宜錄以爲
當宁獻
考試官教諭郭　批〔帝王精微蘊奧揚厲無遺錄之〕
考試官教諭林　批〔揄揚〕
盡與而終之以規此忠愛無已之士亟錄
帝王之纘述祖烈肇舉鴻典也直區區區縟
punctuated:
穹旻。靈集山川，甘雨繩皇皇之祝；光騰日月，卿雲續旦旦之歌。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹以所和詩隨表上進以聞。

第叄場
策

第一問　柳佐
同考試官教諭徐　批：〔我〕皇上本精意以爭泰為典，子能鋪張而揚厲之，而末段尤見忠悃，宜錄以爲當宁獻。
考試官教諭郭　批：〔帝王精微蘊奧，揚厲無遺，錄之。〕
考試官教諭林　批：〔揄揚〕盡與，而終之以規，此忠愛無已之士，亟錄。

帝王之纘述祖烈、肇舉鴻典也，直區區區縟
translation_en:
… the vault of Heaven. May numinous blessings gather upon the mountains and rivers, as sweet rains continue the resplendent prayers; may radiance soar from the sun and moon, as auspicious clouds prolong the song of dawn after dawn. Your servants, overcome with the utmost awe and ardent devotion in gazing up toward Heaven and looking up to Your Sacred Majesty, reverently present the matching poems we have composed, submitted along with this memorial for Your Majesty's hearing.

Third Session
Policy Essays

Question 1: Liu Zuo 柳佐
Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Xu 徐, comments: "[Our] August Emperor takes pure sincerity as his foundation in enacting the grand rites [? 爭泰為典; likely 舉泰鴻典 or 舉大禮典]. You are able to elaborate and extol them, and the final section especially reveals your loyal sincerity. It is fitting to record this to present to the Throne."
Examiner, Instructor Guo 郭, comments: "[The subtle and profound essence of emperors and kings is extolled without omission. Record it.]"
Examiner, Instructor Lin 林, comments: "[He praises and extols] thoroughly [? 盡與], and concludes with remonstrance. This is a scholar of boundless loyalty and devotion; record it at once."

When emperors and kings carry forward the illustrious achievements of their ancestors and initiate great state ceremonies, is this merely a matter of petty, elaborate [? 區區區縟; likely 區區彌縟] …

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
觀哉父天母地壇壝之所自來也而德馨
先之矣尊祖敬宗祼獻之所從起也而精
神貫之矣勸學興禮見謂揆文而所以磨
世礪俗者固自有在也治兵詰戎見謂奮
武而所以建威銷萌者固自有在也人主
不務植仁孝之經崇文武之本而徒日取
詰后之故事而試之其于治道何益夫惟
明主游神粹白之次而超覽興衰之塗秉
昭假之實心則何神不格何釐不迓飭精
明之實政則何文不蔚何武不張不下階
===
序不越俎豆而登于上理率是道也傳曰
仁人爲能饗帝孝子爲能饗親又曰一張
一弛文武之道蓋自古記之矣觀其制肇
于虞夏而大備于成周其說詳于周禮而
雜見于大戴禮諸書何言乎其享帝享親
也圜丘祀天用圜鍾舞雲門禮蒼璧方澤
祭地祇用函鍾舞咸池禮黃琮則郊祀之
說也三年合羣廟之主有祫五年祭始出
punctuated:
觀哉？父天母地，壇壝之所自來也，而德馨先之矣；尊祖敬宗，祼獻之所從起也，而精神貫之矣。勸學興禮，見謂揆文，而所以磨世礪俗者固自有在也；治兵詰戎，見謂奮武，而所以建威銷萌者固自有在也。人主不務植仁孝之經、崇文武之本，而徒日取詰后之故事而試之，其于治道何益？夫惟明主游神粹白之次，而超覽興衰之塗。秉昭假之實心，則何神不格？何釐不迓？飭精明之實政，則何文不蔚？何武不張？不下階序、不越俎豆，而登于上理，率是道也。《傳》曰：「仁人爲能饗帝，孝子爲能饗親。」又曰：「一張一弛，文武之道。」蓋自古記之矣。

觀其制，肇于虞、夏，而大備于成周；其說詳于《周禮》，而雜見于《大戴禮》諸書。何言乎其享帝、享親也？圜丘祀天，用圜鍾，舞《雲門》，禮蒼璧；方澤祭地祇，用函鍾，舞《咸池》，禮黃琮，則郊祀之說也。三年合羣廟之主有祫，五年祭始出
translation_en:
… display? Serving Heaven as father and Earth as mother is the origin of altars and sacred precincts, yet the fragrance of virtue comes first; honoring ancestors and revering lineage founders is the source of libations and offerings, yet one's spiritual devotion pervades them. Encouraging learning and promoting ritual are seen as the management of civil culture, yet that by which the world is polished and customs are whetted inherently lies deeper; drilling troops and inspecting weaponry are seen as the exertion of military might, yet that by which prestige is established and incipient rebellions are dispelled inherently lies deeper. If a ruler does not strive to implant the constant norms of benevolence and filial piety and exalt the foundations of civil and military governance, but merely takes up day by day the precedents of wise [?] sovereigns of the past and tries them out, of what benefit is that to the way of governance? Only an enlightened ruler lets his spirit roam in the realm of pure clarity and gazes transcendently upon the paths of rise and decline. If he holds fast to a sincere heart of luminous communion, what spirit will not be reached, and what blessing will not be welcomed? If he orders well the substantive governance of incisive clarity, what civil culture will not flourish, and what military might will not be extended? Without descending the steps of the hall or stepping beyond the ritual vessels, to ascend to supreme order is to follow this very Way. The Tradition says: "Only the benevolent man can make offerings to the Supreme Ancestor; only the filial son can make offerings to his parents." It also says: "One tension and one relaxation—such is the Way of Kings Wen and Wu." Indeed, this has been recorded since antiquity.

Observing these institutions, they began in the Yu and Xia dynasties and reached complete perfection in the flourishing Zhou; their explanations are detailed in the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) and appear variously in the Elder Dai's Record of Rites (Da Dai Li) and other books. What is meant by making offerings to the Supreme Ancestor and making offerings to one's parents? At the Round Mound, sacrificing to Heaven, one uses the Huanzhong pitch-standard, performs the "Cloud Gate" (Yunmen) dance, and offers ritual homage with the azure bi-disc; at the Square Pool, sacrificing to the deities of Earth, one uses the Hanzhong pitch-standard, performs the "All-Embracing Pool" (Xianchi) dance, and offers ritual homage with the yellow cong-tube—such is the explanation of the suburban sacrifices. Every three years, uniting the spirit tablets of the various ancestral temples is the collective sacrifice (xia); every five years, sacrificing to the first ancestor from whom the founder issued…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
之帝有禘則廟祀之說也微獨是異也燔
瘞不異享乎禴祀蒸嘗不異名乎而聖人
者非徒彌文為也畏天之威于時保之則
不祝史而肅允文允武靡有不孝則不黍
稷而馨視於無形聽於無聲則不吉蠲而
信茲所以潛通沖漠而仰答靈祉也何言
乎其揆文奮武也帝入東學尚親貴仁帝
入西學尚賢貴德帝入南學尚齒貴信帝
入北學尚貴尊爵帝入太學承師問道則
===
視學之說也中春教振旅蒐田中夏教茇
舍苗田中秋教治兵獮田中冬教大閱狩
田則閱武之說也微獨是異也釋奠養老
習樂舞不異禮乎三年五年不異節乎而
聖人者非徒壯觀為也教之以六德六藝
六行則何行不立程之以六步七步六伐
七伐則何藝不成董之以五刑則何惰不
激茲所以文教蔚隆而武功丕赫也漢唐
而來此義漸寖間有舉者明德未馨胡資
punctuated: 之帝有禘，則廟祀之說也。微獨是異也，燔瘞不異享乎？禴祀蒸嘗不異名乎？而聖人者，非徒彌文為也。畏天之威，于時保之，則不祝史而肅；允文允武，靡有不孝，則不黍稷而馨；視於無形，聽於無聲，則不吉蠲而信。茲所以潛通沖漠，而仰答靈祉也。何言乎其揆文奮武也？帝入東學，尚親貴仁；帝入西學，尚賢貴德；帝入南學，尚齒貴信；帝入北學，尚貴尊爵；帝入太學，承師問道，則視學之說也。中春教振旅，蒐田；中夏教茇舍，苗田；中秋教治兵，獮田；中冬教大閱，狩田，則閱武之說也。微獨是異也，釋奠、養老、習樂舞，不異禮乎？三年、五年，不異節乎？而聖人者，非徒壯觀為也。教之以六德、六藝、六行，則何行不立？程之以六步、七步、六伐、七伐，則何藝不成？董之以五刑，則何惰不激？茲所以文教蔚隆，而武功丕赫也。漢、唐而來，此義漸寖。間有舉者，明德未馨，胡資
translation_en: … [ancestor from whom the founder] descended, there is the great quinquennial sacrifice (di); such is the doctrine of ancestral temple sacrifices. Not only are these distinct: do not the burnt offerings (fan) and buried offerings (yi) differ in how they are presented? Do not the spring, summer, autumn, and winter sacrifices (yue, si, zheng, chang) differ in name? Yet the sages did not do these things merely as elaborate formalities. Revering the majesty of Heaven and thereby preserving its mandate, one is solemn without need of invocators and scribes; truly civil and truly martial, lacking nothing in filial piety, one offers fragrant virtue without need of millet and grain; seeing where there is no form and hearing where there is no sound, one is sincere without need of auspicious purification. This is how they silently communicated with the unfathomable void and looked up in response to spiritual blessings. What is meant by their regulating civil culture and rousing martial vigor? When the sovereign enters the Eastern Academy, he honors kinship and values benevolence; when the sovereign enters the Western Academy, he honors the worthy and values virtue; when the sovereign enters the Southern Academy, he honors seniority and values trustworthiness; when the sovereign enters the Northern Academy, he honors rank and respects nobility; when the sovereign enters the Grand Academy, he attends upon his masters and asks about the Way—such is the doctrine of inspecting the academies. In mid-spring, he instructs the troops in marching in formation and conducts the spring hunt (sou); in mid-summer, he instructs them in making camp and conducts the summer hunt (miao); in mid-autumn, he instructs them in drilling arms and conducts the autumn hunt (xian); in mid-winter, he instructs them in the grand review and conducts the winter hunt (shou)—such is the doctrine of reviewing the military. Not only are these distinct: do not the libation ritual to former teachers (shidian), the nourishing of the aged, and the practicing of music and dance differ in ceremonial form? Do not the triennial and quinquennial intervals differ in timing? Yet the sages did not do these things merely to create a grand spectacle. Instructing them in the Six Virtues, Six Arts, and Six Conducts, what conduct would not be established? Measuring them by six paces and seven paces, six strikes and seven strikes, what martial skill would not be perfected? Supervising them with the Five Punishments, what indolence would not be roused into action? This is why civil education flourished richly and martial achievements shone brilliantly. From the Han and Tang dynasties onward, this meaning gradually faded. Among those who occasionally performed these rites, if their illustrious virtue was not yet fragrant, how could they rely on…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
對越寔意未飭奚取儀章漢文帝郊見五
畤立廟渭陽祠衣色尚赤則方家之秤說
也漢高帝令郡國立太上皇廟終漢世因
之議罷議復如築舍然則儇臣之諛肯也
明帝祖劉辟雖尊養更老而漢治竟以不
古爲觀焉耳矣唐明皇躬擐戎服講武驪
山而不能弭夘胡之禍爲耀焉耳矣豈所
以步姚姒之武而方姬王之駕哉
明興
===
高皇帝稽古定制建
圜丘於鍾山之陽建方丘於鍾山之陰以祀
天
地已而合祀建
廟
闕左以饗
德
懿
熙
punctuated:
對越？寔意未飭，奚取儀章？漢文帝郊見五畤，立廟渭陽，祠衣色尚赤，則方家之秤說也；漢高帝令郡國立太上皇廟，終漢世因之，議罷議復，如築舍然，則儇臣之諛肯也；明帝袒割辟雖，尊養更老，而漢治竟以不古，爲觀焉耳矣；唐明皇躬擐戎服，講武驪山，而不能弭夘胡之禍，爲耀焉耳矣。豈所以步姚姒之武，而方姬王之駕哉！
明興，高皇帝稽古定制，建圜丘於鍾山之陽，建方丘於鍾山之陰，以祀天地，已而合祀；建廟闕左，以饗德、懿、熙、
translation_en:
…respond in communion with the spirits? When sincere intent is not cultivated, what value is there in ritual forms and emblems? When Emperor Wen of Han (Han Wendi) performed the suburban sacrifice at the Five Altars, erected the temple on the north bank of the Wei River (Weiyang), and favored red for sacrificial vestments, this was merely the dubious talk [?] of masters of esoterica. When Emperor Gao of Han (Han Gaodi) ordered the commanderies and kingdoms to establish temples to the Grand Supreme Emperor—a practice perpetuated throughout the Han era, with endless debates over abolishing and restoring them like building a house by the roadside—this was merely the flattering assent [?] of sycophantic ministers. When Emperor Ming (Mingdi) bared his arm and sliced the meat [?] at the Circular Moat (Biyong), honoring and nourishing the Three Aged and Five Experienced (Genglao), yet Han governance ultimately failed to match antiquity, it was done merely for spectacle! When Emperor Ming of Tang (Tang Minghuang) personally donned military attire and reviewed the troops at Mount Li (Lishan), yet could not avert the calamity of the rebel barbarians [?], it was done merely for ostentation! How could such acts be the way to walk in the footsteps of Yao and Yu (Yao and Si) or drive abreast with the carriages of the Zhou kings (the kings of Ji)?

When the Ming arose, the High Emperor (Gao Huangdi, i.e., Emperor Taizu) examined antiquity and established the institutions. He built the Round Mound (Huanqiu) on the south slope of Mount Zhong (Zhongshan) and built the Square Mound (Fangqiu) on the north slope of Mount Zhong in order to sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, and later combined the sacrifices. He built the Ancestral Temple to the left of the palace gates to present offerings to Dezu (De), Yizu (Yi), Xizu (Xi), …

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
仁四靚而習師江淮釋奠太學其經始皇業芳
躅可稽也
文皇帝繼統合祀
天
地以
太祖配建
廟北平以饗
列祖
太祖而一視太學再閱京師其潤色太平彝軌
===
可鏡也仰惟
二祖所以駿奔
郊
廟者禋祀則星緯呈輝卿雲耀彩祫享則赤刀
在序玉几如存是左右之孚而君蒿之感
也〔疇非實心〕
二祖所以經緯文武者揆文則敦敘五倫表章
六籍奮武則再造區夏三犁虜庭是咏勺
之化而秉鉞之威也〔疇非實政軼前代裕〕
punctuated: 仁四靚，而習師江淮，釋奠太學，其經始皇業，芳躅可稽也。文皇帝繼統，合祀天地，以太祖配；建廟北平，以饗列祖、太祖；而一視太學，再閱京師。其潤色太平，彝軌可鏡也。仰惟二祖所以駿奔郊、廟者：禋祀則星緯呈輝、卿雲耀彩；祫享則赤刀在序、玉几如存。是左右之孚，而君蒿之感也〔疇非實心〕。二祖所以經緯文武者：揆文則敦敘五倫、表章六籍；奮武則再造區夏、三犁虜庭。是咏《勺》之化，而秉鉞之威也〔疇非實政，軼前代、裕〕
translation_en:
…and Ren, the four ancestors [四靚 for 四親], while drilling the troops along the Yangzi and Huai rivers and performing the libation sacrifices at the Directorate of Education (Taixue); thus, in his founding of the imperial enterprise, his fragrant footsteps can be examined.

When the Cultured Emperor (Emperor Chengzu) succeeded to the throne, he jointly sacrificed to Heaven and Earth, associating the Grand Progenitor (Taizu) with them; he built the Ancestral Temple in Beiping to make sacrificial offerings to the successive ancestors and to the Grand Progenitor; and he once visited the Directorate of Education and twice reviewed the troops in the capital. In his burnishing of the Great Peace, his constant norms can serve as a mirror.

Looking up in contemplation of how the Two Progenitors hastened in service at the suburban altars and the Ancestral Temple: when they offered pure sacrifices, the stars and planets displayed their brilliance and auspicious clouds shone with splendor; when they performed the collective ancestral sacrifice (xia), the red-handled knife was in its place in the side chambers and the jade stool seemed as if the departed were present. This was the spiritual communion on the left and right, and the moving response to the rising vapors of the offerings [comment: Which of these was not from a sincere heart?].

As for how the Two Progenitors wove the warp and woof of the civil and the martial: in measuring out civil administration, they earnestly ordered the Five Relationships and gave prominence to the Six Classics; in displaying martial might, they recreated the Chinese realm and thrice plowed up the courts of the northern caitiffs. This was the transforming influence celebrated in the ode "Shao" and the awe of wielding the battle-axe [comment: Which of these was not substantive governance? Surpassing former dynasties and enriching]…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
後此大都具是矣我
皇上躬
上聖之資履下武之運肯祇事
郊
廟矣已又謁
山陵矣柴望瘞折頊彝也昭穆般薦崇孝也
嘉俞元宰繪圖成冊鉅程也愉奉
兩宮並上
園寢隆敬也愚以爲我將之篇清廟之咏不是
===
過也以故雲流五色占璇宇之長清瑞應
三靈見金甌之如故所謂植仁孝之經者
視太學矣九年
非耶四年
大閱京營矣皮弁釋奠曠典也韎韐視師雄略
也師儒坐講橋門竦觀覃恩也魚麗鵞鸛
肅隊嚴行大法也愚以爲有聲之詩車攻
之雅不是過也以故丹書在朝木鐸在野
而比屋習于絃歌兵休于舍將止于垣而
punctuated: 後此，大都具是矣。我皇上躬上聖之資，履下武之運，肯祇事郊廟矣，已又謁山陵矣。柴望瘞折，頊彝也；昭穆般薦，崇孝也。嘉俞元宰，繪圖成冊，鉅程也；愉奉兩宮，並上園寢，隆敬也。愚以爲《我將》之篇、《清廟》之咏不是過也。以故雲流五色，占璇宇之長清；瑞應三靈，見金甌之如故。所謂植仁孝之經者，視太學矣；九年非耶？四年大閱京營矣。皮弁釋奠，曠典也；韎韐視師，雄略也。師儒坐講，橋門竦觀，覃恩也；魚麗鵞鸛，肅隊嚴行，大法也。愚以爲《有聲》之詩、《車攻》之雅不是過也。以故丹書在朝，木鐸在野，而比屋習于絃歌；兵休于舍，將止于垣，而
translation_en: … posterity, in general, is all contained in this. Our August Emperor personally possesses the endowments of a supreme sage and treads the fortune of succeeding to the martial accomplishments of his ancestors; he has willingly and reverently served at the suburban altars and ancestral temple, and thereafter has also paid homage at the imperial mausoleums. Burning firewood for distant sacrifices and burying victims at the earth altar are his reverent adherence to constant norms [?]; offering abundant sacrifices to the ancestral tablets in the zhao and mu order is his exaltation of filial piety. Graciously approving the Prime Minister's request to paint illustrations and compile them into an album is a grand standard; cheerfully serving the Two Empresses Dowager and ascending together to the imperial tombs is utmost敬 (reverence). I humbly consider that the ode "Wo jiang" (I Bring My Offerings) and the hymn "Qing miao" (The Hallowed Temple) do not surpass this. Therefore, clouds flow in five colors, divining the enduring clarity of the jade-like heavens; auspicious signs respond from the three spiritual realms, showing the golden goblet of the empire intact as of old. Is this not what is called establishing the standard of benevolence and filial piety? [Note: columns transposed in original print: In the fourth year,] he inspected the Imperial University; in the ninth year, he held a grand review of the Capital Training Divisions. Wearing the deerskin cap to perform the libation ceremony to Confucius was an extraordinary rite; wearing red knee-covers to inspect the army was a heroic strategy. Master scholars sitting to lecture while spectators crowded the bridged gates in reverent awe was an extension of imperial grace; deploying the fish-scale and goose-and-stork formations in solemn ranks and strict order was a grand method. I humbly consider that the poem "You sheng" (Wen Wang Has Fame) and the dynastic ode "Che gong" (Our Chariots Were Strong) do not surpass this. Therefore, the cinnabar admonitions are at court, the wooden-tongued bell is in the countryside, and every household side by side practices string music and song; soldiers rest in their quarters, generals remain within their walls, and…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
絶微寧于奏凱所謂崇文武之本者非耶
顧執事猶謂舊典易沿精意難合而冀諸
生有可裨
丹扆萬一者則愚也竊緦緦計之矣
皇上篤明察之義以事天地即配之分合勿論
也齋居能龍見乎淵默能雷聲乎昭事上
帝能翼翼乎先天天弗違後天奉天時乎
有未至焉雖蒼玉在列其精誠猶與天地
爲二也反本始之思以事
===
祖禰即堂之同異勿論也覩亏覆能僾然愾
沐乎瞻堂搆能凜然懼艱難乎儀而刑之
靖四方乎陟降上下能克紹乎有未至焉
雖大祝陳詞其意氣猶與
祖禰爲二也經久遠之圖以飭文武即制之沿
革勿論也遐不作人如棫樸乎疑丞師保
如周官乎式怒蛙乎拊而循之如挾纊乎
有未至焉雖躬臨辟雝親履行陣其于實
致蔑如也故不郊而郊食息起居皆天也
punctuated:
絶微寧于奏凱。所謂崇文武之本者，非耶？顧執事猶謂舊典易沿，精意難合，而冀諸生有可裨丹扆萬一者，則愚也竊緦緦計之矣。

皇上篤明察之義以事天地，即配之分合勿論也，齋居能龍見乎？淵默能雷聲乎？昭事上帝能翼翼乎？先天天弗違，後天奉天時乎？有未至焉，雖蒼玉在列，其精誠猶與天地爲二也。反本始之思以事祖禰，即堂之同異勿論也，覩亏覆能僾然愾沐乎？瞻堂搆能凜然懼艱難乎？儀而刑之靖四方乎？陟降上下能克紹乎？有未至焉，雖大祝陳詞，其意氣猶與祖禰爲二也。經久遠之圖以飭文武，即制之沿革勿論也，遐不作人如《棫樸》乎？疑丞師保如《周官》乎？式怒蛙乎？拊而循之如挾纊乎？有未至焉，雖躬臨辟雝、親履行陣，其于實致蔑如也。故不郊而郊，食息起居皆天也，
translation_en:
…and the farthest frontiers are pacified through the playing of victory hymns. Is this not what is meant by exalting the foundations of civil and military governance? Yet Your Honor still maintains that ancient institutions are easy to follow mechanically while their subtle essence is difficult to match, and hopes that the candidates may have something to contribute, even if only one part in ten thousand, to the imperial throne. On this, I, in my ignorance, have privately given anxious thought.

When His Majesty devotes himself to the principle of luminous discernment in serving Heaven and Earth—leaving aside the question of whether their sacrificial worship is separated or combined—in his fasted seclusion can he manifest like the dragon? In his abyssal silence can he resound like thunder? In brightly serving the Lord on High can he be reverently cautious? Preceding Heaven, does Heaven not act contrary to him, and succeeding Heaven, does he respect Heaven's timing? If anything here falls short, then even though the dark-green jades are arrayed in order, his pure sincerity remains divided from Heaven and Earth as two.

When he turns his thoughts back to his root and origin in serving his distant and immediate imperial ancestors—leaving aside the question of whether their ancestral halls are shared or separate—upon beholding their drinking vessels and coverings [? 亏覆], can he faintly see them with sighing and reverence [? 愾沐]? Upon gazing at the halls and structures they built, can he tremble in awe of their hardships? Can he take them as his model and pattern so as to pacify the four quarters? In their ascending and descending above and below, can he truly carry on their work? If anything here falls short, then even though the Grand Invocator presents his liturgies, his spirit and disposition remain divided from his ancestors as two.

When he plans far-reaching designs to order civil and military affairs—leaving aside the question of institutional continuity and change—does he not rouse and cultivate men of talent as in the ode "Bushy Oak-Trees" (Yupu)? Does he maintain the four辅弼 advisers—Doubt-Resolver, Assistant, Preceptor, and Guardian—as in the "Officers of Zhou" (Zhouguan)? Does he bow from his carriage bar even to an angry frog? Does he soothe and comfort the troops so that they feel as warm as if wrapped in floss silk? If anything here falls short, then even though he personally visits the Imperial University (Biyong) and personally treads the battle ranks, as for actual attainment it counts for nothing.

Therefore, performing the suburban sacrifice without an external suburban altar means that in eating, resting, rising, and dwelling, all is Heaven—…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
所謂陟降厥士日監在茲者也則事天可
知矣不廟而廟羹牆尸牖皆祖也所謂世
德作求求不言配命者也則事親可知矣視
學文之經也然亦有不藉膠校而化捷于
桴鼓者則懿德之敷求也茲不言之教也
視師武之緯也然亦有不藉韜鈐而折衝
于俎豆者則猶之允塞也茲不戰之兵
也是以竊爲今
上望之也矧星象示警雨暘不時饑圻之沴氣
===
爲畿郡國之望竊尤亟
帝貺可常恃乎方隅多警玩愒成風典章忽于
郅隆瑕纇生于泰極
祖釐可常保乎
上嗜學好古虎觀諸儒日濡毫而待
詔士精六書及丹青之業類續食集金門項且
以勞博冠服矣愚以爲
上富于春秋宜游心大業佗以方技進者可一
切報罷也遼左上首功
punctuated: 所謂「陟降厥士，日監在茲」者也，則事天可知矣；不廟而廟，羹牆、尸牖皆祖也，所謂「世德作求」、「求不言配命」者也，則事親可知矣。視學，文之經也，然亦有不藉膠校而化捷于桴鼓者，則「懿德之敷求」也，茲不言之教也；視師，武之緯也，然亦有不藉韜鈐而折衝于俎豆者，則「猶之允塞」也，茲不戰之兵也。是以竊爲今上望之也。矧星象示警，雨暘不時，饑圻之沴氣爲畿，郡國之望竊尤亟，帝貺可常恃乎？方隅多警，玩愒成風，典章忽于郅隆，瑕纇生于泰極，祖釐可常保乎？上嗜學好古，虎觀諸儒日濡毫而待詔；士精六書及丹青之業，類續食集金門，項且以勞博冠服矣。愚以爲上富于春秋，宜游心大業，佗以方技進者，可一切報罷也。遼左上首功，
translation_en:
… This is what is meant by "ascending and descending are His affairs; daily He inspects us here"—from this, how to serve Heaven can be known. Sacrificing in the ancestral temple without being at the temple, in one's soup and on the walls, by the doors and windows, everywhere are the ancestors. This is what is meant by "for generations they cultivated their virtue, seeking to emulate it" and "forever seeking to be in accord with the Mandate" [?]—from this, how to serve one's parents can be known. Inspecting the Imperial Academy is the warp of civil governance; yet there is also that which transforms more swiftly than drumstick and drum without relying on schools, namely "spreading and seeking fine virtue"—this is teaching without words. Inspecting the army is the weft of military affairs; yet there is also that which repels the enemy amidst ritual vessels without relying on military manuals and strategy, namely "plans that are truly sincere and substantial"—this is an army that does not fight. For this reason I humbly hope for this from His Present Majesty.

Moreover, the celestial phenomena show warnings, rain and sunshine are unseasonable, the noxious qi of famine-stricken borders besets the capital [?], and the prefectures and principalities face an even more urgent threat of banditry [?]. Can the favor of the Supreme Lord always be relied upon? The border regions have many alarms, laxity and procrastination have become the custom, statutory institutions are neglected at the height of prosperity, and flaws and blemishes arise at the extreme of peace. Can the blessings of the Ancestors always be preserved?

His Majesty loves learning and delights in antiquity, and the scholars of the White Tiger Hall daily moisten their brushes and await imperial decrees. Yet men skilled in the six principles of script and the art of painting generally receive continuous rations and gather at the Golden Horse Gate, and recently [?] they even obtain caps and robes of office through their toil. In my humble opinion, since His Majesty is rich in years and in the prime of youth, He ought to let His mind roam in the great enterprise of governance, and all others who advance by means of minor arts and skills may be entirely dismissed. Recently Liaodong presented a report of first-rank military merit, …

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
上不靳通侯之賞予世券若曰庶幾得熊羆不
二心之臣爲
國家效尺寸耳少年貪半通之銅或謂乙一
典屬國可生縛左賢王以歸則封狼居胥
之事非渺也愚以爲
上英鋭第無廣侈其雄心邊可息肩也如是而
天
親不益闓懌文武不益懋脩者愚不信也夫宣
揚
===
主徽執事事也黼藻
聖質大臣者之責也愚生何與知焉
第二問
杜華先
同考試官訓導解　批〔辨華實以討諸儒而楮夷不爽足占〕
〔子之所養矣宜直博洽已也宜錄〕
考試官教諭郭　批〔藻鑑精明詞調古雅〕
考試官教諭林　批〔名論制有學識必以儒行自勵者〕
儒之道豈易言哉而何世之言儒者小之
punctuated:
上不靳通侯之賞，予世券，若曰：「庶幾得熊羆不二心之臣，爲國家效尺寸耳。」少年貪半通之銅，或謂乙一典屬國，可生縛左賢王以歸，則封狼居胥之事非渺也。愚以爲上英鋭，第無廣侈其雄心，邊可息肩也。如是而天親不益闓懌、文武不益懋脩者，愚不信也。夫宣揚主徽，執事事也；黼藻聖質，大臣者之責也。愚生何與知焉？
第二問
杜華先
同考試官訓導解　批〔辨華實以討諸儒，而楮夷不爽，足占子之所養矣。宜直博洽已也？宜錄。〕
考試官教諭郭　批〔藻鑑精明，詞調古雅。〕
考試官教諭林　批〔名論制有學識，必以儒行自勵者。〕
儒之道豈易言哉？而何世之言儒者小之
translation_en:
… His Majesty did not begrudge the reward of a marquisate, granting an iron tally of hereditary succession, as if to say: "Perhaps We may obtain fierce, single-hearted subjects like bears and grizzlies to render some small service to the State." Yet hot-blooded youths greedy for even a half-size bronze seal of office might claim that by begging [?] the post of Director of Dependent States, one could bind the Wise King of the Left alive and bring him back—so that performing a sacrifice at Mount Langjuxu is no remote prospect! In my humble opinion, since His Majesty is heroic and keen-spirited, if only we do not further inflate His ambitious heart, the frontiers will be able to rest their shoulders. If this is done, and yet Heaven and His Imperial Parents are not all the more delighted, or civil and military affairs are not all the more diligently cultivated, I would not believe it. Now, to proclaim the sovereign's excellence is the business of you, the examiners; to adorn the sage qualities of the Emperor is the responsibility of the grand ministers. What can a humble student know of such matters?

Second Policy Question
By Du Huaxian 杜華先
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Xie 解, comments: [He distinguishes between outward flourish and inner substance in evaluating the various Confucian scholars, and his brushwork and tenor [?] never miss the mark—enough to gauge what you have cultivated in yourself. Could it be merely broad learning and nothing more [?]? Worthy of recording.]
Examiner, Instructor Guo 郭, comments: [Discerning judgment and clear insight; diction and cadence antique and refined.]
Examiner, Instructor Lin 林, comments: [Famous discourses crafted [?] with scholarly insight; surely one who spurs himself on with Confucian conduct.]

Is the Way of the Confucian scholar easy to speak of? Why then do those in the world who speak of Confucians belittle …

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
也夫誦法先王兼總六籍此儒之華也砥
礪行誼醞釀道德此儒之實也古之爲儒
者華與實稱後世之爲儒者華與實離本
根旣撥支葉滋蕃士始騖於訓詁之學非
獨爲之華藻又從而黼其鞶帨讖者所深
慨也乃論者不探其本而遂并之乎言儒
華實之間庸可以弗辨乎哉夫儒之名何
昉乎周官太宰以九兩繫邦國之民其目
曰儒以道得民而貫於九兩之中蓋道亦
大矣原於眞宰繇於帝王堯舜文武君天
下伊尹周公相天下皆儒道也至孔子以
道設教斤斤洙泗之間而後世稱之曰魯
國之儒一人今之服方領習矩步呻呫畢
孰致身廊廟者誰非動稱孔氏以儒自標
===
哉家語大戴禮所載儒行蓋粲然詳由今
誦其書繹其義間若與儒行相乖剌者夫
上不事天子下不事諸侯是狷士也爵祿
相先患難相死過失可微辨而不可面數
punctuated: 也！夫誦法先王，兼總六籍，此儒之華也；砥礪行誼，醞釀道德，此儒之實也。古之爲儒者，華與實稱；後世之爲儒者，華與實離。本根旣撥，支葉滋蕃，士始騖於訓詁之學，非獨爲之華藻，又從而黼其鞶帨，讖者所深慨也。乃論者不探其本，而遂并之乎言儒，華實之間，庸可以弗辨乎哉？夫儒之名何昉乎？《周官》太宰以九兩繫邦國之民，其目曰：「儒以道得民」，而貫於九兩之中，蓋道亦大矣。原於眞宰，繇於帝王。堯、舜、文、武君天下，伊尹、周公相天下，皆儒道也。至孔子以道設教，斤斤洙、泗之間，而後世稱之曰「魯國之儒一人」。今之服方領、習矩步、呻呫畢，孰致身廊廟者，誰非動稱孔氏、以儒自標哉？《家語》、《大戴禮》所載《儒行》，蓋粲然詳。由今誦其書、繹其義，間若與儒行相乖剌者。夫上不事天子，下不事諸侯，是狷士也；爵祿相先，患難相死，過失可微辨而不可面數，
translation_en:
…[How is it that those in the world who speak of Confucians belittle] them! Now, reciting and modeling oneself after the former kings, and comprehensively mastering the Six Classics—this is the flower of the Confucian. Honing one's conduct and righteousness, and cultivating the Way and its virtue—this is the substance of the Confucian. Among those who were Confucians in antiquity, flower and substance matched one another; among those who were Confucians in later ages, flower and substance became separated. Once the root was uprooted, the branches and leaves grew ever more luxuriant, and scholars began to chase after the learning of exegesis and glossing. Not only did they turn it into flowery rhetoric, they went further and embroidered their ornamental belt-pouches and kerchiefs—something that men of discernment deeply lament. Yet critics do not probe into the root of the matter, and instead lump them all together when speaking of Confucians. Between flower and substance, how can one fail to distinguish?

Where did the name "Confucian" (ru) originate? In the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), the Grand Councilor (Taizai) binds the people of the states with the "nine ties," and one of its items says: "The Confucian wins the people through the Way." Running through the nine ties, the Way is great indeed! It originates in the True Ruler [Heaven] and is followed by the emperors and kings. When Yao, Shun, King Wen, and King Wu ruled the world as sovereigns, and when Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou assisted the world as chief ministers, all of this was the Way of the Confucian. Coming down to Confucius, he established his teaching by means of the Way, devoting himself attentively to it between the Zhu and Si rivers, so that later generations praised him as "the one and only Confucian of the state of Lu." Today, among those who wear square-collared robes, practice measured steps, chant over their bamboo slips, and rise to serve in the imperial court, who does not at every turn invoke Confucius and style himself a Confucian?

The "Conduct of the Confucian" (Ruxing) recorded in the Family Sayings of Confucius (Kongzi jiayu) and the Elder Dai's Record of Rites (Da Dai Liji) is brilliantly detailed. Yet when today we recite those texts and unravel their meaning, at times they seem to contradict true Confucian conduct. Now, "above, not serving the Son of Heaven; below, not serving the feudal lords"—this is an uncompromisingly aloof scholar. "Yielding to one another in ranks and emoluments, dying for one another in times of peril, and having faults that may be gently pointed out in private but not enumerated to one's face"—…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
是飾俠也攫鷙蝨不程其勇引重鼎不程
其力是用閭也儒術旣湮世常以儒相詬
病秦坑漢罵之風巳非一日所由來漸矣
戰國之士欲自附於儒以飾褒榮衆遂爲
之標榜如此而終之曰聞此言也不敢以
儒爲戲其究竟可暏也故程氏以爲非孔
子之言也安定胡氏謂游夏門人所爲其
文與孫卿相類蓋孫卿之言曰有俗儒者
有雅儒者有大儒者逢衣淺帶解果其冠
===
略法先王而足亂世術所謂俗儒也內不
以自誣外不以自欺法後王一制度尊賢
畏法而不敢怠傲所謂雅儒也以古持今
以一行萬奇變卒起擧統類而應之無所
儗怎張法而度之晻然若合符節所謂大
儒也孫卿生當戰國管商之刑名孫吳之
變詐蘇張之縱横並駕齊騖卿獨克推尊
王道崇奬儒術卽所言亦得其髣髴矣顧
語用而遺體擧一而廢百宜其不得爲醇
punctuated: 是飾俠也；攫鷙蝨不程其勇，引重鼎不程其力，是用閭也。儒術旣湮，世常以儒相詬病，秦坑漢罵之風巳非一日，所由來漸矣。戰國之士，欲自附於儒以飾褒榮，衆遂爲之標榜如此，而終之曰：「聞此言也，不敢以儒爲戲。」其究竟可暏也。故程氏以爲非孔子之言也。安定胡氏謂游、夏門人所爲，其文與孫卿相類。蓋孫卿之言曰：有俗儒者，有雅儒者，有大儒者。逢衣淺帶，解果其冠，略法先王而足亂世術，所謂俗儒也；內不以自誣，外不以自欺，法後王，一制度，尊賢畏法而不敢怠傲，所謂雅儒也；以古持今，以一行萬，奇變卒起，擧統類而應之，無所儗怎，張法而度之，晻然若合符節，所謂大儒也。孫卿生當戰國，管、商之刑名，孫、吳之變詐，蘇、張之縱横，並駕齊騖，卿獨克推尊王道，崇奬儒術，卽所言亦得其髣髴矣。顧語用而遺體，擧一而廢百，宜其不得爲醇
translation_en: …is to affect the ways of a wandering knight-errant; "seizing fierce beasts and stinging insects without measuring one's courage, lifting a heavy tripod without measuring one's strength"—this is to act like a village brawler [?]. Once the Confucian art had fallen into obscurity, the world routinely used "Confucian" as a term of reproach. The trend that culminated in the burying of scholars in Qin and the reviling of them in Han did not arise in a single day; it developed gradually. Scholars of the Warring States period wished to attach themselves to the Confucians so as to adorn themselves with praise and glory before the multitude, and so they trumpeted such claims on their behalf, concluding with the words: "Having heard this speech, he never again dared to make sport of Confucians." Their ultimate motive is plain to see. Therefore Master Cheng (Cheng Yi 程頤) held that these were not the words of Confucius. Master Hu of Anding (Hu Yuan 胡瑗) said it was composed by disciples of Ziyou (子游) and Zixia (子夏), and that its style resembles that of Sun Qing (Xunzi 荀子). Now, Sun Qing's words state: There are vulgar Confucians, there are refined Confucians, and there are great Confucians. Wearing wide-sleeved robes and narrow sashes, with caps shaped like a crab's shell, roughly imitating the Former Kings yet sufficing only to confuse the arts of the age—these are what are called vulgar Confucians. Inwardly not deceiving oneself, outwardly not deceiving others, taking the Later Kings as one's model, unifying institutional measures, honoring the worthy and standing in awe of the law without daring to be negligent or arrogant—these are what are called refined Confucians. Holding fast to the present by means of antiquity, governing ten thousand things by means of the One, when strange turns of events suddenly arise, grasping the overarching categories to respond to them without hesitation [?], and when stretching out the standard to measure them, having them match seamlessly like the halves of a tally—these are what are called great Confucians. Sun Qing lived during the Warring States period, when the doctrines of punishments and names of Guan Zhong (管仲) and Shang Yang (商鞅), the deceitful stratagems of Sun Wu (孫武) and Wu Qi (吳起), and the vertical and horizontal alliances of Su Qin (蘇秦) and Zhang Yi (張儀) were all racing abreast. Yet Sun Qing alone was able to exalt the Kingly Way and champion the Confucian art; even what he said captured a fair semblance of it. Still, he spoke of function while neglecting substance, and upheld one aspect while discarding a hundred others—so is it any wonder that he could not be considered a pure…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
儒哉今合二書論之儒行非孔子之言也
然言儒而先行則本實未泯也卿之言駁
而未醇然言儒效而證以周公孔子則大
較不爽也乃後世之言儒者則異矣班固
傳西漢儒林自丁寬迄於房鳳范曄傳東
漢儒林自劉昆迄於蔡玄大都皆講習遺
經掇摭傳註者也漢興承秦之敝六籍殘
缺孝武黜百家言延文學儒者以百數而
海內靡然向風中厄於新室更始又多懷
===
挾圖書遁伏巖藪逮於光武中興訪求遺
逸士乃抱負墳策雲集京師矣當建元建
武中上方嚮意儒術一時學子各以門
授受著錄動數千人其專相傳祖輒以號
於衆曰吾襲某氏業也而諸儒亦以此耀
之至石渠講論虎觀咨詢一言當於主聽
又輒曰此非臣之能也臣師某也世主遂
遡厥源流移之祿爵舉世翕然趨之以爲
儒道在是矣試取其行攷之則中公見幾
punctuated:
儒哉！今合二書論之，《儒行》非孔子之言也，然言儒而先行，則本實未泯也；卿之言駁而未醇，然言儒效而證以周公、孔子，則大較不爽也。

乃後世之言儒者則異矣。班固傳西漢儒林，自丁寬迄於房鳳；范曄傳東漢儒林，自劉昆迄於蔡玄，大都皆講習遺經、掇摭傳註者也。漢興，承秦之敝，六籍殘缺。孝武黜百家言，延文學儒者以百數，而海內靡然向風。中厄於新室、更始，又多懷挾圖書，遁伏巖藪。逮於光武中興，訪求遺逸，士乃抱負墳策，雲集京師矣。當建元、建武中，上方嚮意儒術，一時學子各以門授受，著錄動數千人。其專相傳祖，輒以號於衆曰：「吾襲某氏業也。」而諸儒亦以此耀之。至石渠講論、虎觀咨詢，一言當於主聽，又輒曰：「此非臣之能也，臣師某也。」世主遂遡厥源流，移之祿爵，舉世翕然趨之，以爲儒道在是矣。試取其行攷之，則中公見幾
translation_en:
… [pure] Confucian scholar! Now, if we discuss the two writings together: the "Conduct of the Scholar" (Ruxing) is not the words of Confucius, yet in speaking of the Confucian scholar it puts conduct first, so the fundamental substance is not yet lost; Xun Qing's words are mixed and not completely pure, yet in speaking of the "Teachings and Effects of the Confucian" (Ruxiao) he verifies them through the Duke of Zhou and Confucius, so in the main they do not miss the mark.

When later ages spoke of Confucian scholars, however, it was different. In Ban Gu's biographies of the "Forest of Confucians" (Rulin) of the Western Han, from Ding Kuan down to Fang Feng, and in Fan Ye's biographies of the "Forest of Confucians" of the Eastern Han, from Liu Kun down to Cai Xuan, for the most part they were all men who lectured on and practiced the surviving Classics and gathered up commentaries and annotations.
