When the Han arose, inheriting the ruin of the Qin, the Six Classics were fragmentary and incomplete. Emperor Xiaowu dismissed the words of the Hundred Schools and invited literary and Confucian scholars by the hundreds, whereupon all within the seas were swept along toward this trend. Midway through, suffering the distress of the Xin dynasty and the Gengshi reign, many again clutched their charts and books and fled into hiding among crags and marshes. Reaching the restoration under Emperor Guangwu, when he sought out surviving recluses, scholars then carried the ancient canons and records on their backs and gathered like clouds at the capital. During the Jianyuan and Jianwu eras, the emperors above turned their intentions toward Confucian arts, and the students of the time each transmitted and received teachings within their own schools [? a character such as 戶 may be missing after 門], with registered disciples easily numbering in the thousands. Those who specialized in handing down a founder's teaching would invariably proclaim to the multitude, "I inherit the tradition of Master So-and-so!" And the various scholars also used this to glorify themselves. When it came to the lectures and discussions in the Stone Canal Pavilion (Shiqu ge) and the inquiries in the White Tiger Hall (Baihu guan), whenever a single word pleased the ruler's ear, they would again invariably say, "This is not your servant's ability; it is that of your servant's teacher, So-and-so." The rulers of the age would then trace back the source and stream of their learning and bestow upon them emoluments and noble ranks, and the whole world unitedly rushed after this, supposing that the Way of the Confucian lay therein. Yet if we try to take their conduct and examine it: Shen Gong [中公, for 申公] in perceiving the subtle signs of change …

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
非哲自甘脅肩工式周旋昏主佹羅禍誅
非儒者之難進易退也孟喜謬稱師說陰
植巧慧楊政剛果任氣操刃候門非儒者
之言必忠信行必中正也京房屢陳災異
未信而諫薛漢校定圖讖阿意取容非儒
者之上答不疑不答不諂也戴憑自矜辯
難獨立爭坐何休著論古今貽書互詆非
儒者之大讓若慢弼弼若無能也甚至傳
尚書者以贓罪坐繫作易說者以風角著
===
抄距孫卿所謂推儒奚啻千里尚得冒其
名於天下後世哉宋史著儒林傳自聶崇
義而下無慮數十人而濂洛關閩諸賢則
別爲道學傳以表之夫儒者之於道也猶
農工之各持其業有司之各效其職也不
持其業而可以爲農工乎不效其職而可
以爲有司乎不學於道而可以爲儒乎顧
道學儒林判而爲兩良由儒道之不明世類
以訓詁爲儒業而高視道德非第宋人然
punctuated: 非哲，自甘脅肩；工式周旋昏主，佹羅禍誅，非儒者之難進易退也。孟喜謬稱師說，陰植巧慧；楊政剛果任氣，操刃候門，非儒者之言必忠信、行必中正也。京房屢陳災異，未信而諫；薛漢校定圖讖，阿意取容，非儒者之上答不疑、不答不諂也。戴憑自矜辯難，獨立爭坐；何休著論古今，貽書互詆，非儒者之大讓若慢、弼弼若無能也。甚至傳《尚書》者以贓罪坐繫，作《易》說者以風角著抄，距孫卿所謂推儒奚啻千里，尚得冒其名於天下後世哉？《宋史》著《儒林傳》，自聶崇義而下無慮數十人，而濂、洛、關、閩諸賢，則別爲《道學傳》以表之。夫儒者之於道也，猶農工之各持其業，有司之各效其職也。不持其業而可以爲農工乎？不效其職而可以爲有司乎？不學於道而可以爲儒乎？顧道學、儒林判而爲兩，良由儒道之不明，世類以訓詁爲儒業，而高視道德，非第宋人然
translation_en: … was not wise in foreseeing the signs, and willingly hunched his shoulders in servility; Wang Shi 王式 [transcribed as 工式] maneuvered around a benighted ruler and nearly met with disaster and execution—this is not the Confucian way of being difficult to advance and easy to withdraw. Meng Xi 孟喜 falsely claimed his master's teachings to secretly plant his own cleverness; Yang Zheng 楊政, headstrong and impulsive, held a blade while waiting at the gate—this is not the Confucian way of words always being loyal and trustworthy, and actions always being upright and balanced. Jing Fang 京房 repeatedly set forth portents and anomalies, remonstrating before gaining his ruler's trust; Xue Han 薛漢 collated and established apocryphal charts and prophecies, flattering the ruler's wishes to curry favor—this is not the Confucian way of answering without doubt when consulted by a superior, and not flattering when not consulted. Dai Ping 戴憑 boasted of his skill in disputation, standing alone to contend for seats; He Xiu 何休 wrote discourses on past and present, exchanging letters of mutual denigration—this is not the Confucian way of great yielding appearing like negligence, and modest humility appearing like incapability. It even went so far that those who transmitted the Book of Documents (Shangshu) were imprisoned for bribery, and those who composed explanations of the Book of Changes (Yi) became known for excerpts on wind-corner divination. How could this be merely a thousand li away from what Xun Qing 荀卿 [Xunzi] called a "great Confucian" [雅儒, transcribed as 推儒]? How could they still usurp that name in the empire and for posterity? When the History of the Song (Songshi) compiled the "Biographies of Confucian Scholars" (Rulin zhuan), from Nie Chongyi 聶崇義 downward there were easily several dozen men, while for the worthies of Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min it separately created the "Biographies of Masters of the Learning of the Way" (Daoxue zhuan) to distinguish them. Now, the relation of a Confucian scholar to the Way is like farmers and artisans each maintaining their trade, or officials each fulfilling their duties. Can one not maintain one's trade and yet be considered a farmer or artisan? Can one not fulfill one's duties and yet be considered an official? Can one not study the Way and yet be considered a Confucian? Yet the Learning of the Way (Daoxue) and the Forest of Confucians (Rulin) were split into two; this truly stemmed from the Way of the Confucian not being clear, so that the world generally took exegesis and glossing as the business of a Confucian while viewing morality as something lofty and remote—and it was not only the people of the Song who were thus…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
也抑如西漢之世不有董仲舒乎陳三策
而正言無諱相驕藩而汰心頓戢正誼明
道之語確乎聖門喻義之言也東漢之世
不有鄭玄乎力辭權貴之辟終老通德之
門而括囊大典網羅衆家范武子謂仲尼
之徒不能過也之二君子者即以列諸儒
林詎不卓焉增重而乃別為之傳謂其峻
立獨騁非丁寬劉昆輩所得均茵馮也豈
知周孔一儒耳而况於二氏也孰玆而論
===
是冀北之駿不以馬名崑岡之珍不以玉
名也豈理也哉葢嘗總漢宋諸儒較之漢
儒之為學也博宋儒之為學也精惟其學
之博故自墳典丘索逮於訓詁名物靡不
旁搜冥採而六籍亦因以僅存惟其學之
精故太極西銘皇極經世諸書發前人所
未發至於朱氏乃集大成而折衷之矣然
當聖學既湮之後掇殘編於煨燼採奧義
於玄渺則漢之為儒也難當斯道大明之
punctuated: 也。抑如西漢之世，不有董仲舒乎？陳三策而正言無諱，相驕藩而汰心頓戢，正誼明道之語，確乎聖門喻義之言也。東漢之世，不有鄭玄乎？力辭權貴之辟，終老通德之門，而括囊大典，網羅衆家，范武子謂仲尼之徒不能過也。之二君子者，即以列諸儒林，詎不卓焉增重？而乃別為之傳，謂其峻立獨騁，非丁寬、劉昆輩所得均茵馮也。豈知周、孔一儒耳，而况於二氏也？孰玆而論，是冀北之駿不以馬名，崑岡之珍不以玉名也，豈理也哉！葢嘗總漢、宋諸儒較之：漢儒之為學也博，宋儒之為學也精。惟其學之博，故自墳、典、丘、索逮於訓詁名物，靡不旁搜冥採，而六籍亦因以僅存；惟其學之精，故《太極》、《西銘》、《皇極經世》諸書，發前人所未發，至於朱氏，乃集大成而折衷之矣。然當聖學既湮之後，掇殘編於煨燼，採奧義於玄渺，則漢之為儒也難；當斯道大明之
translation_en:
… Moreover, in the Western Han era, was there not Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒? He presented his three policy essays and spoke uprightly without taboo; he served as Grand Mentor to arrogant feudal princes and their extravagant ambitions were immediately curbed; his words about rectifying righteousness and clarifying the Way were truly in accord with the sage's school's teachings on understanding righteousness. In the Eastern Han era, was there not Zheng Xuan 鄭玄? He firmly declined summonses from the powerful and noble, living out his old age at the Gate ofComprehending Virtue (Tongde men 通德門), encompassing the great canons and gathering together all the various schools—so that Fan Wuzi 范武子 (Fan Ning 范甯) said that even the disciples of Confucius (Zhongni 仲尼) could not surpass him. Had these two gentlemen been placed in the "Biographies of Confucian Scholars" (Rulin zhuan 儒林傳), how would that not have eminently added weight to it? Yet separate biographies were made for them instead, on the grounds that they stood toweringly apart and galloped alone, such that men of the ilk of Ding Kuan 丁寬 and Liu Kun 劉昆 could not share the same carriage mat and armrest with them. How could they fail to know that the Duke of Zhou 周公 and Confucius were themselves simply Confucians (ru 儒)—how much more so these two men? To argue on this basis [孰玆而論, taking 孰 as 執?] is as if the fine steeds of northern Ji 冀 were not called horses, and the treasures of Mount Kun 崑岡 were not called jade. How could that be reasonable!

Indeed, if we take all the Confucians of the Han and Song together and compare them: the learning of the Han Confucians was broad, whereas the learning of the Song Confucians was refined. Precisely because their learning was broad, from the Three Mounds (Sanfen 三墳), Five Canons (Wudian 五典), Eight索 (Basuo 八索), and Nine邱 (Jiuqiu 九丘) down to philological glosses and names and objects, there was nothing they did not extensively search out and deeply gather, and through this the Six Classics barely survived. Precisely because their learning was refined, books such as the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji tu 太極圖), the Western Inscription (Ximing 西銘), and the Supreme Principles Governing the World (Huangji jingshi 皇極經世) brought to light what predecessors had never expressed, until Master Zhu (Zhu Xi 朱熹) synthesized the great achievements and struck the proper balance among them. Yet, following the era when the learning of the sages had been submerged, gathering up remnant bamboo slips from the ashes and extracting profound meanings from the abstruse and distant—to be a Confucian in the Han was difficult. At a time when this Way had become brilliantly clear…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
日制故已備而可考軌轍具在而可循則
宋之爲儒也易廼論其得修踐履不詭於
正則宋儒爲優焉豈惟濂洛關閩粹然稱
最卽石介孫復諸子以砥行自植者亦未
可一二數也段謝疊山氏乃謂漢士質宋
士浮而有所軒輊於其間毋亦貴耳賤目
之論哉
今天下儒術大明矣經籍傳註著在功令學
者尺寸而守之信若蓍龜雖陳亢范升無
===
所搆其辭矣士挾策鄉闈用期於不詳所聞
上之人持衡度而較之落若累黍雖張賓
陳俠無所售其僞矣第令好脩崇實動中
準繩效職當官矜惜名節寧爲偃蹇一官
之董相不爲曲學阿世之公孫弘寧爲終
老蓬蓽之鄭玄不爲附會徼榮之賈景伯
寧使正心誠意之說爲上所厭聞不欲使
說經鏗鏘之名爲世所浮慕庶幾哉無忝
於儒行卽孫卿所謂雅儒何以加焉顧叔
punctuated:
日，制故已備而可考，軌轍具在而可循，則宋之爲儒也易。廼論其得修踐履，不詭於正，則宋儒爲優焉。豈惟濂、洛、關、閩粹然稱最，卽石介、孫復諸子以砥行自植者，亦未可一二數也。段謝疊山氏乃謂「漢士質，宋士浮」，而有所軒輊於其間，毋亦貴耳賤目之論哉？

今天下儒術大明矣。經籍傳註，著在功令，學者尺寸而守之，信若蓍龜，雖陳亢、范升無所搆其辭矣；士挾策鄉闈，用期於不詳所聞，上之人持衡度而較之，落若累黍，雖張賓、陳俠無所售其僞矣。第令好脩崇實，動中準繩，效職當官，矜惜名節：寧爲偃蹇一官之董相，不爲曲學阿世之公孫弘；寧爲終老蓬蓽之鄭玄，不爲附會徼榮之賈景伯；寧使正心誠意之說爲上所厭聞，不欲使說經鏗鏘之名爲世所浮慕。庶幾哉無忝於儒行，卽孫卿所謂「雅儒」，何以加焉！顧叔
translation_en:
… day, when institutions and precedents were already complete and verifiable, and the tracks were all in place to be followed, being a Confucian scholar in the Song was easy. Yet if we evaluate their attainment in self-cultivation and practical conduct, and their not deviating from orthodoxy, then the Song Confucians were superior. Not only were the masters of Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min [Zhou Dunyi 周敦頤, the Cheng 程 brothers, Zhang Zai 張載, and Zhu Xi 朱熹]purely the finest, even the likes of Shi Jie 石介 and Sun Fu 孫復, who established themselves by honing their conduct, are too numerous to count one by one. Yet [?] Xie Dieshan 謝疊山 [Xie Fangde 謝枋得] claimed that "Han scholars were substantial while Song scholars were superficial," elevating one over the other—is this not a judgment that values hearsay over what is before one's own eyes?

Today throughout the realm, the Confucian art has beenmade brilliantly clear. The Classics and their commentaries are enshrined in the examination regulations; scholars adhere to them to the inch and foot, trusting them like yarrow stalks and tortoise shells, so that even a Chen Kang 陳亢 or a Fan Sheng 范升 would have nowhere to fabricate their arguments. Scholars carry their texts into the provincial examination compounds, aiming not to betray [reading 不詳 as 不負?] what they have learned, while their superiors hold the balance and measure to compare them with the precision of stacked millet grains, so that even a Zhang Bin 張賓 or a Chen Xie 陳俠 would have nowhere to peddle their falsehoods. If only they love self-cultivation and revere substance, their every action hitting the mark of the plumb-line, fulfilling their duties in office and cherishing their reputation and integrity—preferring to be Chancellor Dong [Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒], frustrated in a single post, rather than Gongsun Hong 公孫弘, who twisted his learning to flatter the age; preferring to be Zheng Xuan 鄭玄, growing old to the end of his days under a thatched roof, rather than Jia Jingbo 賈景伯 [Jia Kui 賈逵], who forced interpretations to seek glory; preferring to let the doctrines of rectifying the mind and making the intentions sincere become tiresome to the ruler's ears, rather than wishing to make a reputation for sonorous expounding of the Classics an object of the world's superficial admiration—then they might almost avoid bringing shame to the conduct of a Confucian! Even what Master Xun [Xunzi 荀子] called a "refined Confucian" (yaru 雅儒), how could it surpass this? Yet as the …

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
季既趨而士風淪靡乃有高自稱許競立
門牆竊聖賢之緒餘爲一時之譚柄振徒
成黨若建鼓而招於市焉一言偶合即以
爲曾之唯閉睫高坐即以爲顏之愚乃稽
其行誼課其職業則茫乎未有以稱夫若
是而名曰儒是儒之名可以比周爭可以
夸誕有哉矧又有下於此者非愚生所敢
悉言亦無庸以口舌攻也孰事以尚志識
諸生故輒縱言之如此惟執事進而教之
===
第三問
于若瀛
同考試官訓導王　批〔士子譚時務大都勦語此作津津悉〕
中窾會有用之才也
考試官教諭郭　批〔弭盜議具見石畫至推本德意是尤〕
識其大者錄之
考試官教諭林　批〔策寄畫盜情具中機宜非可以書生目〕
之者
國家之視百姓譬之身然德意者榮衛也餘
punctuated:
季既趨，而士風淪靡，乃有高自稱許，競立門牆，竊聖賢之緒餘，爲一時之譚柄，振徒成黨，若建鼓而招於市焉。一言偶合，即以爲曾之唯；閉睫高坐，即以爲顏之愚。乃稽其行誼，課其職業，則茫乎未有以稱。夫若是而名曰「儒」，是儒之名可以比周爭、可以夸誕有哉？矧又有下於此者，非愚生所敢悉言，亦無庸以口舌攻也。孰事以尚志識諸生，故輒縱言之如此，惟執事進而教之。

第三問
于若瀛
同考試官訓導王　批：〔士子譚時務，大都勦語。此作津津悉〕中窾會，有用之才也。
考試官教諭郭　批：〔弭盜議具見石畫，至推本德意，是尤〕識其大者，錄之。
考試官教諭林　批：〔策寄畫盜情，具中機宜，非可以書生目〕之者。

國家之視百姓，譬之身然。德意者，榮衛也；餘
translation_en:
… a degenerate age has taken hold, and the ethos of scholars has sunk into decadence, there are those who loftily praise themselves, competing to set up their own sectarian gates and walls. They steal the leftover dregs of the sages and worthies to serve as conversational showpieces of the moment, rallying followers and forming cliques as if setting up a drum to summon people in the marketplace. When a single word happens to coincide, they immediately take it to be Zengzi’s "yes"; when they close their eyes and sit aloft, they immediately take it to be Yan Hui’s "apparent foolishness." Yet when one examines their conduct and righteousness or evaluates their professional duties, they are utterly at a loss and have nothing to match their claims. Now, if people like this are called "Confucian scholars" (ru), can the name of Confucian scholar be contested through partisan collusion or possessed through boastful absurdity? How much more so when there are those even lower than this, whom this foolish student dares not speak of in full, and whom there is no need to attack with mere words! Because Your Excellency [reading 執事 for 孰事] tests us students on the elevation of our aspirations and insight, I have ventured to speak freely like this, hoping only that Your Excellency will bring me forward and instruct me.

Third Question
Yu Ruoying 于若瀛
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Wang comments: [When scholars discuss current affairs, they mostly repeat plagiarized clichés. This piece speaks with absorbing interest and entirely] hits the crucial points; he is a talent of practical use.
Examiner and Instructor Guo comments: [His proposals on suppressing banditry fully demonstrate rock-solid planning; as for tracing the issue back to the sovereign's benevolent intentions, this especially] shows an understanding of what is fundamental. We record it for publication.
Examiner and Instructor Lin comments: [This policy essay's planning [?] and analysis of the bandit situation all hit the right strategic opportunities; he is not someone who can be viewed] merely as a bookish student.

The state's view of the common people may be compared to the human body. Benevolent intentions are the nutritive and defensive vital energies (rongwei); circulating [?] …

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
暢之以大吏滲調之以百執事所以使之
充益一身而無壅閼也而民起而爲盜則
手足蹶盭而不舉也設方略飭戎防剷落
其角距而披其黨醫師之按經而投劑也
盜未起也而吾有以消之則榮衛流而病
不作盜既起也而吾有以遏之則砭石中
而病不深不然未事而誨盜既事而又無
以弭盜病所爲由肢體而入于腠理腸胃
心腑之間即俞扁不顧矣
===
今天下提志搏心以奉
天子曩所憂榜鳴而虞燧舉者第一象胥道之
一田部吏勞之非有南北羽書之警尘鋒
旄之也而山東齊民婣於先民之矩其俗
習絃歌非若滇粵西南萬里而編戶獷野
好亂也饑民歲貸縣官穀歲負歲寬之有
司稍稍奉行
詔書不謹論如法又非有大璺吏魚肉之也然
而萑苻之盜往往而是隨捕隨發竟不衰
punctuated:
暢之以大吏，滲調之以百執事，所以使之充益一身而無壅閼也。而民起而爲盜，則手足蹶盭而不舉也。設方略，飭戎防，剷落其角距而披其黨，醫師之按經而投劑也。盜未起也，而吾有以消之，則榮衛流而病不作；盜既起也，而吾有以遏之，則砭石中而病不深。不然，未事而誨盜，既事而又無以弭盜，病所爲由肢體而入于腠理、腸胃、心腑之間，即俞、扁不顧矣。
今天下提志搏心以奉天子。曩所憂榜鳴而虞燧舉者，第一象胥道之，一田部吏勞之，非有南北羽書之警，尘鋒旄之也。而山東齊民婣於先民之矩，其俗習絃歌，非若滇、粵西南萬里，而編戶獷野好亂也。饑民歲貸縣官穀，歲負歲寬之；有司稍稍奉行詔書不謹，論如法，又非有大璺吏魚肉之也。然而萑苻之盜往往而是，隨捕隨發，竟不衰
translation_en:
…circulated smoothly through high officials and infused and regulated by the hundred functionaries, so as to make it fill and benefit the whole body without obstruction. When the people rise up to become bandits, however, it is as though the hands and feet are crippled and twisted and cannot be lifted. Devising strategic plans, putting military defenses in order, lopping off their horns and spurs, and breaking up their gangs is like a physician administering medicine in accordance with the medical classics. When banditry has not yet arisen and we have the means to dissolve it, then the nutritive and protective vitalities flow freely and illness does not break out; when banditry has already arisen and we have the means to check it, then the acupuncture stone hits the mark and the illness does not go deep. Otherwise, if before trouble starts one invites banditry, and once trouble has started one has no means to suppress it, that is how an illness passes from the limbs into the pores, the intestines and stomach, and the heart and viscera—at which point even Yu Fu and Bian Que would not look back at the patient.

Today the whole realm unites its will and binds its heart in service to the Son of Heaven. Where formerly we worried over the sounding of alarm boards and feared the raising of beacon fires, now it takes merely a single Interpreter (xiangxu) to guide them and a single agricultural clerk to comfort them; there are no feathered dispatches of alarm from north or south, nor the dust of blades and banners [?]. Moreover, the common people of Shandong are familiar with the standards of the ancients, and their customs are steeped in stringed instruments and song; it is not as though they were ten thousand li away in the southwest like Dian and Yue, where the registered households are fierce, rustic, and fond of rebellion. Starving people borrow grain from the government every year, and every year that they fall into arrears they are granted leniency; if the local authorities are even slightly negligent in carrying out imperial edicts, they are sentenced according to the law, so neither are there grossly abusive officials preying upon the people like fish and meat. And yet bandits in the reed marshes are to be found everywhere; no sooner are they captured than others break out, never subsiding or…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
止者則太史公所謂多劫人者大國之風
也是故怵迫於餬口之策則亡命作奸抵
扞于督租之胥則瞋目語難鼓煽于推埋
之輩則引繩批根叫囂于斥莽之陬則竭
筍鳥竄出沒于燕趙宋衛之境則疆吏不
及捕而偵卒不及詗蓋齊地多盜則自古
記之矣雖然
明天子在上鞭策四夷而獨令幺麼小醜爲山
東害不便語曰爲虺弗摧爲蛇若何今盜
===
幸不至如漢殺長吏掠城邑則勢易散也
胡不舉漢事觀之也盜起膠東而購賞捕
斬者非張敞耶多爲之間以離其黨決也
盜起平原而部衆掩擊者非趙熹耶出其
不意抵亢擣虛亦法也龔遂馴渤海賣刀
買牛盜賊輒解散彼所謂治亂民猶治亂
繩笱之熟也李固治泰山罷兵歸農盜賊
亦輒解散夫非以不治治之者耶是亦一
畫也主勦者渤海泰山疑之乎縱寇而不
punctuated: 止者，則太史公所謂「多劫人者，大國之風也」。是故怵迫於餬口之策，則亡命作奸；抵扞于督租之胥，則瞋目語難；鼓煽于推埋之輩，則引繩批根；叫囂于斥莽之陬，則竭筍鳥竄；出沒于燕、趙、宋、衛之境，則疆吏不及捕，而偵卒不及詗。蓋齊地多盜，則自古記之矣。雖然，明天子在上，鞭策四夷，而獨令幺麼小醜爲山東害，不便。語曰：「爲虺弗摧，爲蛇若何？」今盜幸不至如漢殺長吏、掠城邑，則勢易散也，胡不舉漢事觀之也？盜起膠東，而購賞捕斬者，非張敞耶？多爲之間，以離其黨，決也。盜起平原，而部衆掩擊者，非趙熹耶？出其不意，抵亢擣虛，亦法也。龔遂馴渤海，賣刀買牛，盜賊輒解散，彼所謂「治亂民猶治亂繩」，笱之熟也。李固治泰山，罷兵歸農，盜賊亦輒解散，夫非以不治治之者耶？是亦一畫也。主勦者，渤海、泰山疑之乎縱寇，而不
translation_en: … cease; this is what the Grand Historian (Sima Qian 司馬遷) meant when he said, "That there are many who rob others is the custom of a great state." Therefore, when driven by desperation in their schemes to eke out a living, they abscond and commit outrages; when clashing with the clerks who press for tax grain, they glare with rage and speak defiantly; when incited by gangs of grave-robbers and murderers, they band together and pull strings to root out rivals [?]; when shouting in tumult in corners of saline wasteland and tall grass, they exhaust their stores and scatter like birds [?]; and when appearing and disappearing along the borders of Yan, Zhao, Song, and Wei, the frontier officials cannot catch them in time, nor can the scouts spy them out in time. Indeed, that the land of Qi abounds in bandits has been recorded since antiquity. Even so, when an enlightened Son of Heaven reigns above, whipping the four barbarian tribes into submission, to allow petty, insignificant miscreants alone to plague Shandong is untoward. As the saying goes: "If you do not crush it while it is a viper, what will you do when it becomes a serpent?" Now, fortunately, the bandits have not gone so far as those in the Han dynasty who killed senior officials and plundered walled cities, so their force is easy to disperse. Why not cite the affairs of the Han and examine them? When bandits arose in Jiaodong, was it not Zhang Chang 張敞 who offered rewards to capture and behead them? Using many spies to divide their partisans was a decisive measure. When bandits arose in Pingyuan, was it not Zhao Xi 趙熹 who marshaled his troops for a surprise attack? Catching them unawares, striking at their vital points, and storming their undefended places is also a sound method. When Gong Sui 龔遂 tamed Bohai, having the people sell their swords to buy oxen, the bandits and thieves immediately dispersed; his saying that "governing a disorderly populace is like untangling a tangled cord" came from thorough deliberation [?]. When Li Gu 李固 governed Taishan, dismissing the troops and returning them to farming, the bandits and thieves likewise immediately dispersed—was this not governing them by non-interference? This too is a valid strategy. Those who advocate extermination suspect the methods of Bohai and Taishan of indulging bandits, yet do not…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
知施屠伯之威於潢池之赤子則慘矣主
撫者膠柱鼓瑟之乎皆殺而不知盧總
從之爱于冥頑之亂民則悖矣先王懼民
之有邪心而盜之不可長也于是設之以
什一而民不困于是訓之以三物而民不
怠于是教之以農者耕蠶者織而民不欲
于是禁之以司寤氏野廬氏脩閭氏而民
不敢自歉于法夫如是故精神流通協氣
和□而其或有不軌之民蘖芽其間可撫也
===
亦可勦也所謂殲厥渠魁脅從罔治者也
曷嘗屑屑焉主拘攣之見哉
朝廷威德過漢山東羣盜不加于漢文武吏
自昕何嘗敞矣與周哉顧撫與勦兩無
策也則愚所謂惑也說者曰欲弭盜必也
嚴保甲乎然保甲可行于都邑不可行于
鄉鄙蓋巖木深坳盜之逋匿甚易而廬烟
星落我之守望甚難黠盜間有以先聲喝
之者懼其螫之移于我也敢首抗乎既攫
punctuated:
知，施屠伯之威於潢池之赤子，則慘矣；主撫者，膠柱鼓瑟之乎？皆殺而不知盧總從之爱于冥頑之亂民，則悖矣。先王懼民之有邪心，而盜之不可長也，于是設之以什一而民不困，于是訓之以三物而民不怠，于是教之以農者耕、蠶者織而民不欲，于是禁之以司寤氏、野廬氏、脩閭氏而民不敢自歉于法。夫如是，故精神流通，協氣和□。而其或有不軌之民蘖芽其間，可撫也，亦可勦也，所謂「殲厥渠魁，脅從罔治」者也，曷嘗屑屑焉主拘攣之見哉！
朝廷威德過漢，山東羣盜不加于漢，文武吏自昕何嘗敞矣與周哉？顧撫與勦兩無策也，則愚所謂惑也。說者曰：「欲弭盜，必也嚴保甲乎！」然保甲可行于都邑，不可行于鄉鄙。蓋巖木深坳，盜之逋匿甚易；而廬烟星落，我之守望甚難。黠盜間有以先聲喝之者，懼其螫之移于我也，敢首抗乎？既攫
translation_en:
… know, and instead inflict the severity of a ruthless butcher upon the Emperor's own subjects dabbling in rebellion in the royal ponds, then that is cruel. Do those who advocate pacification play the zither with glued pegs [cleaving stubbornly to precedent]? To look upon them as all [deserving of] slaughter [?] and yet show the leniency of pardoning coerced followers [?] toward obstinate and unruly rebels is perverse. The former kings feared that the people might harbor wicked thoughts and that banditry must not be allowed to grow. Therefore, they established the one-tenth tax so the people would not be distressed; they instructed them in the "three things" (six virtues, six behaviors, six arts) so the people would not be idle; they taught farmers to plow and silkworm-raisers to weave so the people would not be covetous; and they restrained them through the Night-Watch Officer (Siwushi), the Country Hostel Officer (Yelushi), and the Gate-Maintaining Officer (Xiulüshi) so the people would not dare to fall short of the law. Because it was thus, spiritual energy circulated freely and harmonious ether [?]. And if perchance there were lawless people sprouting up among them, they could be pacified, or they could be suppressed by force—this is what is meant by "annihilate the chief culprits, and do not punish those coerced into following." When did they ever petty-mindedly hold to a rigid, one-sided view?

The majesty and virtue of our Imperial Court surpass those of the Han, and the bands of bandits in Shandong do not exceed those of the Han. In their own self-estimation [?], how do our civil and military officials consider themselves inferior to Zhang Chang, Zhao Xi, Gong Sui, and Li Gu [?]? Yet in both pacification and suppression they have no strategy at all—this is what I call bewildering. Some commentators say: "If you wish to quell banditry, you must strictly enforce the tithing and mutual-security system (baojia)!" However, the baojia system can be practiced in cities and towns, but cannot be practiced in rural villages. For among craggy woods and deep ravines, it is very easy for bandits to flee and hide; whereas with cottages and hearth-smoke scattered like stars, it is very difficult for our people to keep watch and aid one another. When cunning bandits occasionally intimidate them in advance with threats, people fear that their venom will be turned upon themselves—who would dare be the first to resist? Once they have seized…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
主人之金而去甚至殺人幸主人不言又
幸吏猾不問則輒相沉匿避罰敢上變乎
又其豪即保甲也敢誰何乎故曰保甲不
足恃也孔子論太叔治盜曰寬則民慢慢
則糾以猛言所以遏盜者嚴也教康子患
盜曰苟子之不欲雖賞之不竊言所以消
盜者豫也既不能消又不能遏而區區恃
保甲末也愚嘗審之而得其說凡六而所
以消盜之源有三一曰緩催科愚聞馬窮
===
則軼民窮則盜東兗濟河登萊憑海甘地
斥鹵半之民苦傜役不有望米于覆盆之
照而銜恨于向隅之悲者乎誠撫檍册問
宿負墾蕪册急催租棥疾則復之存無則
蠲之而後肺石之膆中部無之泣樗也二
曰崇敎化夫一夫善射千夫決拾故史有
閒閣之傷則民有肉袒之悔齊俗印鉏亂
夫非人情耶誠躬表率謹鄉約胥開有禁
馳騁有禁背公死黨感分遺身有禁而後
punctuated: 主人之金而去，甚至殺人；幸主人不言，又幸吏猾不問，則輒相沉匿避罰，敢上變乎？又其豪即保甲也，敢誰何乎？故曰：保甲不足恃也。孔子論太叔治盜曰：「寬則民慢，慢則糾以猛。」言所以遏盜者嚴也。教康子患盜曰：「苟子之不欲，雖賞之不竊。」言所以消盜者豫也。既不能消，又不能遏，而區區恃保甲，末也。愚嘗審之而得其說凡六，而所以消盜之源有三：一曰緩催科。愚聞馬窮則軼，民窮則盜。東、兗濟河，登、萊憑海，甘地斥鹵半之，民苦傜役，不有望米于覆盆之照，而銜恨于向隅之悲者乎？誠撫檍册問宿負，墾蕪册急催租，棥疾則復之，存無則蠲之，而後肺石之膆中部無之泣樗也。二曰崇敎化。夫一夫善射，千夫決拾；故史有閒閣之傷，則民有肉袒之悔。齊俗印鉏亂夫，非人情耶？誠躬表率、謹鄉約，胥開有禁，馳騁有禁，背公死黨、感分遺身有禁，而後…
translation_en:
…the householder's money and leave, or even go so far as to commit murder; hoping that the householder will say nothing and that cunning clerks will ask no questions, they immediately conceal the matter together to evade punishment—who would dare report the incident to higher authorities? Moreover, the local bullies are themselves the heads of the mutual security units (baojia)—who would dare challenge them? Therefore, I say that the mutual security system cannot be relied upon.

When Confucius discussed Zitaishu's suppression of bandits, he said: "When government is lenient, the people grow negligent; when they are negligent, they must be corrected with severity." This means that the way to check banditry is through strictness. When instructing Ji Kangzi on his worry over bandits, he said: "If you yourself are free from desires, they will not steal even if you reward them for it." This means that the way to eliminate banditry is through prevention beforehand. Being unable either to eliminate it beforehand or to check it, and merely relying on the mutual security system, is to attend only to the branches rather than the root.

I have carefully examined the matter and arrived at six proposals in all, of which three address the source for eliminating banditry:

The first is to relax the pressing of tax collection. I have heard that when horses are driven to exhaustion they bolt, and when the people are driven to exhaustion they turn to banditry. Dongchang and Yanzhou border the Yellow River and the Ji, while Dengzhou and Laizhou lean against the sea; half of their land [?] is barren and saline, and the people suffer bitterly from corvée labor. Are there not those who long for the light of the sun beneath an overturned basin [?], and harbor resentment in the grief of facing a corner alone? If indeed we soothe the distressed [?] and do not demand old arrears, and in opening up wasteland do not urgently press for rent—granting exemptions where there is ruin and sickness [?], and remitting taxes where nothing remains—then there will be no more grievances at the red stone of appeal or weeping in the middle territories [?].

The second is to exalt moral instruction and transformation. When one man excels at archery, a thousand men put on their thumb-rings and arm-guards; thus, when officials show the remorse of shutting themselves in their chambers to reflect on their faults, the people feel the repentance of baring their shoulders to accept punishment. That the customs of Qi are marked by quarreling over hoes [?] and disorderly men—is this not still within human nature? If officials truly lead by personal example and carefully uphold the community compacts (xiangyue), prohibiting brawling [?], prohibiting reckless galloping, and prohibiting turning against the public good to die for private factions or sacrificing one's life out of personal obligation, then afterward…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
驕悍習輩蜂蟻無乖也三曰收俠徒夫英
布鄱湖盜也劇孟俠也黃巢鹽徒也錯此
爲天下輕重而令之稿戢蓬華其誰甘之
故遺棄之則爲逋逃之藪而善撫之則爲
保障之雄者必若而人也誠藉而籠之縣
官付以捕責或擢錄不次而後鷹距無虞
颶徂詐可作使也所以遏盜之流亦有三
一曰增民兵夫胠篋探囊一夫之力耳至
于蠻結不勝其磨牙搖毒矣今轅門選牙
===
健步幾何郡邑城守驍騎幾何枹鼓一鳴
懼困吏之未能戒也卽戍卒不可掣罣額
不可增而歲解劉鎮之民兵不可減乎請
分其半鎖邪二萬太原千匹無難辦也二
曰嚴賞罰
令甲盜警三日不以報大吏卽百石之吏捽
胡而係縲之二千石以下坐不職論至嚴
也顧文網彌苛而蔽匿彌甚劫盜決背據
鄰殺越人于貨而報第曰穿竊而已尉倅
punctuated:
驕悍習輩，蜂蟻無乖也。三曰收俠徒。夫英布，鄱湖盜也；劇孟，俠也；黃巢，鹽徒也。錯此爲天下輕重，而令之稿戢蓬華，其誰甘之？故遺棄之則爲逋逃之藪，而善撫之則爲保障之雄者，必若而人也。誠藉而籠之縣官，付以捕責，或擢錄不次，而後鷹距無虞颶，徂詐可作使也。
所以遏盜之流亦有三：一曰增民兵。夫胠篋探囊，一夫之力耳；至于蠻結，不勝其磨牙搖毒矣。今轅門選牙健步幾何？郡邑城守驍騎幾何？枹鼓一鳴，懼困吏之未能戒也。卽戍卒不可掣，罣額不可增，而歲解劉鎮之民兵不可減乎？請分其半，鎖邪二萬、太原千匹，無難辦也。二曰嚴賞罰。令甲：盜警三日不以報大吏，卽百石之吏捽胡而係縲之，二千石以下坐不職論，至嚴也。顧文網彌苛而蔽匿彌甚，劫盜決背據鄰，殺越人于貨，而報第曰穿竊而已。尉倅
translation_en:
… unruly and fierce customs will be transformed [?], and swarming bandits will cause no more trouble. The third is to recruit stalwarts and adventurers. Now, Ying Bu 英布 was a bandit of Lake Po 鄱湖; Ju Meng 劇孟 was a knight-errant; Huang Chao 黃巢 was a salt smuggler. Men such as these tip the balance of the empire, yet if we force them to wither away in humble thatched huts, who among them would submit willingly? Therefore, those who become a haven for fugitives when cast aside, yet become champions of defense when well pacified, are precisely men of this sort. If we truly register and bring them into the fold of the county authorities, entrust them with the responsibility of catching thieves, or promote and employ them out of turn, then there will be no fear of hawks striking on the wind [?], and the cunning can be put to service.

As for stemming the tide of banditry, there are likewise three measures. The first is to increase the militia. Prying open chests and picking pockets require only the strength of a single man; but when bandits band together in gangs [?], there is no withstanding their sharpened fangs and deadly venom. Today, how many elite foot soldiers are selected at the commander's headquarters? How many valiant horsemen guard the prefectural and county cities? Once the alarm drum sounds, one fears that our hard-pressed officials will be unable to stand on guard. Even if garrison troops cannot be withdrawn and the fixed military quotas [?] cannot be increased, can the militia sent annually to Jizhen 薊鎮 [劉鎮?] not be reduced? I beg that half of them be retained: twenty thousand men for琅邪 [鎖邪?] and a thousand horses for Taiyuan 太原 would not be difficult to provide. The second is to strictly enforce rewards and punishments. According to the statutes, if a bandit alarm is not reported to the high officials within three days, even hundred-bushel sub-officials are seized by the throat and bound in fetters, while two-thousand-bushel officials and below are tried for dereliction of duty—this is strict indeed. Yet the harsher the net of the law becomes, the worse the concealment grows. Robbers and bandits turn their backs in defiance [?], seize neighboring areas, and murder people for their goods, yet the reports merely call it petty burglary and nothing more. District Defenders and Assistant Magistrates…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
懼罪求蒙而闗茸長吏又從而文之此沈
命所以蘇漢而謁者所以誅秦也誠嚴爲
之發獲則旌之全獲則刻之不獲則創之
匿則糾之并其追胥而處分之則激礪之
術也三曰許自首氏之爲盜率詿誤也人
知必死而不赦是堅其合也覺之則其黨
疑是假手也
制使猶于人者不惟首愿以爲殺人大劫儻自
首亦宜貰其死或量以自首不盡不實之
===
法處之盜喜于脫死而互相訐告則主名
可得也之六者皆盜之所以破也而非其
本也丘文莊曰得一良令如得勝兵三千
人得一良守如得勝兵三萬人何謂良吏
黠鮚篇之智抑投巫之奇不以爲先保
障不以鷹鸇先鸞鳳不爲凝脂不爲椎髓
如此則上下相信何法不立何恩不浹幸
而無盜策之上也不幸而有盜吾諭之如
渤海泰山可也又不幸而諭之不止吾勝
punctuated:
懼罪求蒙，而闗茸長吏又從而文之，此《沈命》所以蘇漢，而謁者所以誅秦也。誠嚴爲之發：獲則旌之，全獲則刻之，不獲則創之，匿則糾之，并其追胥而處分之，則激礪之術也。
三曰許自首。氏之爲盜，率詿誤也。人知必死而不赦，是堅其合也；覺之則其黨疑，是假手也。制使猶于人者不惟首，愿以爲殺人大劫，儻自首，亦宜貰其死，或量以自首不盡不實之法處之。盜喜于脫死而互相訐告，則主名可得也。
之六者，皆盜之所以破也，而非其本也。丘文莊曰：「得一良令，如得勝兵三千人；得一良守，如得勝兵三萬人。」何謂良吏？黠鮚篇之智，抑投巫之奇；不以爲先保障，不以鷹鸇先鸞鳳；不爲凝脂，不爲椎髓。如此，則上下相信，何法不立？何恩不浹？幸而無盜，策之上也；不幸而有盜，吾諭之如渤海、泰山，可也；又不幸而諭之不止，吾勝
translation_en:
…fearing punishment, seek to cover things up, while incompetent senior officials in turn gloss over the matter for them. This is why the "Law on Concealing Bandits" (Chenming fa) failed to revive [?] the Han, and why the Internuncio brought about the ruin of the Qin. If we truly enforce this strictly: when bandits are captured, reward the officials; when all are captured, recommend them for promotion [?]; when they are not captured, punish them; when cases are concealed, impeach them—and deal with the pursuing constables accordingly—this will be the way to spur them on.

Third: permit voluntary confession. When the common people [?] become bandits, it is mostly through being misled and entangled. If men know that they will certainly die and never be pardoned, this only hardens their solidarity; if we open a way for them [?], their comrades will grow suspicious of one another, which is a way of borrowing their own hands to destroy them. Imperial regulations already allow confession for ordinary offenses [?], but I would humbly suggest that even in cases of homicide and major robbery, if a bandit voluntarily surrenders, his life should also be spared, or he should be dealt with proportionately under the law for incomplete or untruthful confession. When bandits rejoice at escaping death and inform against one another, the ringleaders' names can be obtained.

These six measures are all means by which bandits may be defeated, yet they do not address the root of the matter. Qiu Wenzhuang (Qiu Jun 丘濬) said: "To obtain one good Magistrate is like obtaining three thousand victorious soldiers; to obtain one good Prefect is like obtaining thirty thousand victorious soldiers." What is meant by a good official? He checks the cleverness of the bamboo receptacle for secret denunciations [?], and restrains the theatricality of throwing shamans into the river; he does not put taxation [?] ahead of protective barriers, nor does he put hawks and falcons ahead of simurghs and phoenixes; he does not act like congealed fat in his harshness, nor does he beat the marrow out of the people. When it is like this, superiors and inferiors trust one another—what law will not stand, and what grace will not penetrate? If by good fortune there are no bandits, that is the best outcome; if by misfortune there are bandits, we may admonish them into submission as was done in Bohai and Taishan; and if by further misfortune admonishing them does not stop them, we may overcome…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
之如膠東平原亦可也
明興山以東號良吏如許逵尹樂陵而寇不
爲害張慶知章丘而道不拾遺繇是道也
之所謂善弭盜者也雖然吏者奉德意而
致之民者也而其機則在
上而不在下
朝廷屢下
明旨切責郡邑吏吏廪廪救過不暇此乃手持
足行而非精神榮衛所流貫也以故治愈
===
鍥急而効愈虚而
輦轂之下且有闕遏而不流者秦浙名藩惡
少得以侮大吏江淮内地緇徒得以煽人
心而何獨一山東多盜哉
主上觀化理之原廣諮諏之路資啓沃則延公
卿而坐籌陳便宜則引郡縣而陛見不下
衽帶而明燭窮簷不越俎豆而慮周纖微
務使天下之勢如身使臂如臂使指脉然
而溢溢然而通四體百骸不言而喻而無
punctuated: 之如膠東、平原亦可也。明興，山以東號良吏，如許逵尹樂陵而寇不爲害，張慶知章丘而道不拾遺，繇是道也。之所謂善弭盜者也。雖然，吏者，奉德意而致之民者也，而其機則在上而不在下。朝廷屢下明旨，切責郡邑吏，吏廪廪救過不暇，此乃手持足行，而非精神榮衛所流貫也。以故治愈鍥急而効愈虚，而輦轂之下，且有闕遏而不流者。秦、浙名藩，惡少得以侮大吏；江、淮内地，緇徒得以煽人心，而何獨一山東多盜哉？主上觀化理之原，廣諮諏之路，資啓沃則延公卿而坐籌，陳便宜則引郡縣而陛見，不下衽帶而明燭窮簷，不越俎豆而慮周纖微，務使天下之勢，如身使臂，如臂使指，脉然而溢，溢然而通，四體百骸不言而喻，而無
translation_en:
… over them as in Jiaodong and Pingyuan is also acceptable.

Since the rise of the Ming, among those east of the Mountains acclaimed as upright officials—such as Xu Kui 許逵, who governed Laoling so that bandits did no harm, and Zhang Qing 張慶, who administered Zhangqiu so that lost items were not picked up on the roads—all followed this way. This is what is meant by being skilled at quelling banditry. Even so, officials are those who uphold the Sovereign's benevolent intentions and deliver them to the people, yet the pivotal mechanism lies above and not below. The Court repeatedly issues clear decrees sternly reproaching prefectural and county officials, and the officials, trembling with fear, have no leisure save to rescue themselves from fault. This is merely the hands grasping and the feet walking, not the vital spirit and nutritive and defensive qi coursing through them. For this reason, the more harshly and urgently governance is pressed, the more hollow its effects become, and even beneath the imperial chariot wheels there are blockages that fail to flow. In renowned provincial seats such as Shaanxi and Zhejiang, unruly youths are able to insult high officials; in the interior regions of the Yangtze and Huai, Buddhist monks are able to incite people's minds—so why would Shandong alone have many bandits?

If His Majesty observes the source of transformative governance and broadens the avenues of consultation—receiving enlightening counsel by inviting dukes and ministers to sit and plan, and hearing proposals of what is expedient by summoning prefectural and county officials for audience at the steps of the throne; illuminating the poorest huts without leaving his mat and sash, and extending his concern to the finest details without overstepping the sacrificial vessels—he will surely cause the momentum of the realm to be like the body moving the arm and the arm moving the fingers, surging like the pulse and flowing unimpeded, the four limbs and hundred bones responding without a word being spoken, so that there is no…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
復有疥癬之疾痿痺之患此則所謂通天
下爲一身而在乎君心加之意者敢以爲
芹曝獻
第四問
張四聰
同考試官教諭彭　批〔譚道術時政不作墓語而議論正大　不可辯折足稱作矣〕
考試官教諭郭　批〔援古證今卓有定見亟錄〕
考試官教諭林　批〔其文粹雅其論正大是通方之士也〕
===
國家之取士明其道以標準之闢其途以招
徠之而已矣經術神化之奥區其道不可
易也科目登籲之矩矱其途不可廢也繇
是道以折衷乎六藝則杜多岐之惑而摶
心揖志粹然同軌于下廣是途以蒐羅乎
羣材則破拘攣之法而旁搜遠取翕然輻
輳于上古聖王所以朝多蒸髦而野無遺
賢者不可坐而致之哉
今天下亦極治矣道化翔洽弦誦萬里士通
punctuated:
復有疥癬之疾、痿痺之患，此則所謂通天下爲一身，而在乎君心加之意者，敢以爲芹曝獻。

第四問
張四聰
同考試官教諭彭　批〔譚道術、時政不作墓語，而議論正大，　不可辯折，足稱作矣。〕
考試官教諭郭　批〔援古證今，卓有定見，亟錄。〕
考試官教諭林　批〔其文粹雅，其論正大，是通方之士也。〕

國家之取士，明其道以標準之，闢其途以招徠之而已矣。經術，神化之奥區，其道不可易也；科目，登籲之矩矱，其途不可廢也。繇是道以折衷乎六藝，則杜多岐之惑，而摶心揖志，粹然同軌于下；廣是途以蒐羅乎羣材，則破拘攣之法，而旁搜遠取，翕然輻輳于上。古聖王所以朝多蒸髦而野無遺賢者，不可坐而致之哉？今天下亦極治矣，道化翔洽，弦誦萬里，士通
translation_en:
…longer be any afflictions like scabies and ringworm or ailments of paralysis and numbness. This is what is meant by uniting the whole realm into a single body, which depends on the ruler's mind giving special attention to it; I venture to offer this as my humble gift of wild celery and warm sunlight.

Question Four
Zhang Sicong 張四聰
Associate Examiner and Instructor Peng 彭 comments: 〔In discussing philosophical learning and current governance, he does not use stale expressions [? 墓語, perhaps for 套語], and his arguments are upright and grand, irrefutable; it truly deserves to be called a fine piece of work.〕
Examiner and Instructor Guo 郭 comments: 〔Citing antiquity to verify the present, he possesses outstanding and firm views; record this urgently.〕
Examiner and Instructor Lin 林 comments: 〔His writing is pure and elegant, and his arguments are upright and grand; he is a scholar of comprehensive understanding.〕

In selecting scholars, the state simply clarifies its Way to set a standard for them, and opens up its paths to attract and summon them. Classical scholarship is the profound realm of spiritual transformation—its Way cannot be altered; the examination categories are the established standard for advancing and calling forth talent—their path cannot be abolished. By following this Way to take the Six Arts as the criterion, the confusion of multiple diverging paths is blocked off, and minds are united and wills gathered, purely following the same track below. By broadening this path to gather in the multitude of talents, restrictive and rigid laws are broken through, and by searching widely and selecting from afar, talents harmoniously converge like spokes at a hub above. That whereby the ancient sage-kings had courts filled with outstanding men and left no worthy neglected in the wilderness—could it not be achieved without effort? Today the realm is also in a state of utmost order: moral transformation spreads far and wide, the sound of stringed instruments and recitation is heard for ten thousand li, and when a scholar masters…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
一藝輙續食上公車稱
主上任使故天下非乏才也而執事猶咨咨焉
過計也無亦以按圖而求或遺驪黃之外
而緩急推擇致廑掛髀之思邪則上世之
理可鏡也疇咨訪岳虞治以光顓俊敷求
商道用茂逮乎成周而取士之制益備矣
是故閭胥書敬敏任恤者于族族師書孝
弟睦婣者於黨黨正州長書德行道藝者
於鄉然猶未登之朝也而鄉老師衆寡而
===
以禮禮賓之獻賢能之書而王拜受之其
慎重有如此者鄉論秀士升之司徒司徒
論選士升之學大樂正論造士之秀升之
司馬然猶未命之官也而司馬辨其材而
論賢以進之告于王而論定以官之其詳
審有如此者茲所以廣薪槱之道闢網羅
之途棫樸歌興而菁莪化治也裔是而降
科目繁興漢列而爲四茂才明經孝廉賢
良也茂才復疏而爲三明經明律治劇也
punctuated: 一藝，輙續食上公車，稱主上任使，故天下非乏才也。而執事猶咨咨焉，過計也。無亦以按圖而求，或遺驪黃之外；而緩急推擇，致廑掛髀之思邪？則上世之理可鏡也。疇咨訪岳，虞治以光；顓俊敷求，商道用茂。逮乎成周，而取士之制益備矣。是故閭胥書敬敏任恤者于族，族師書孝弟睦婣者於黨，黨正、州長書德行道藝者於鄉，然猶未登之朝也；而鄉老師衆寡而以禮禮賓之，獻賢能之書，而王拜受之，其慎重有如此者。鄉論秀士，升之司徒；司徒論選士，升之學；大樂正論造士之秀，升之司馬，然猶未命之官也；而司馬辨其材而論賢以進之，告于王而論定以官之，其詳審有如此者。茲所以廣薪槱之道、闢網羅之途，棫樸歌興而菁莪化治也。裔是而降，科目繁興。漢列而爲四：茂才、明經、孝廉、賢良也。茂才復疏而爲三：明經、明律、治劇也。
translation_en:
… a single art are promptly supplied with provisions along the way to ride the public carriages to the capital, proving worthy of the Sovereign's employment and commissions. Thus the empire does not lack talent. Yet Your Excellency still sighs over this in anxious deliberation—an excess of caution! Is it not because you fear that searching strictly according to a diagram might overlook great steeds beyond mere black or yellow coat colors, and that when selecting men in times of urgency, we might be left lamenting with our hands slapping our thighs over the lack of generals? If so, the principles of high antiquity can serve as a mirror. Through inquiring of the crowd and consulting the Four Peaks, the governance of Yu [Shun] shone forth; by esteeming the eminent and searching broadly for them, the Way of Shang flourished. Coming down to the perfected Zhou dynasty, the system for selecting scholars became even more complete.

Therefore, the Neighborhood Head (lüxu) recorded those who were respectful, diligent, trustworthy, and compassionate for the Clan Master; the Clan Master (zushi) recorded those who were filial, fraternal, harmonious, and friendly to in-laws for the Community; and the Community Head (dangzheng) and District Magistrate (zhouzhang) recorded those possessing moral conduct and mastery of the Way and arts for the Region (xiang). Yet they were still not presented to the court. Only when the Regional Elder (xianglao) led the multitude, large and small, to feast them as guests in accordance with ritual, and presented the registers of the worthy and capable, did the King bow and receive them—such was the gravity and caution shown! The regions evaluated the Cultivated Scholars (xiushi) and promoted them to the Minister of Education (situ); the Minister of Education evaluated the Selected Scholars (xuanshi) and promoted them to the Grand Academy (xue); and the Grand Director of Music (da yuezheng) evaluated the finest of the Accomplished Scholars (zaoshi) and promoted them to the Minister of War (sima). Yet they were still not appointed to office. Only when the Minister of War distinguished their capabilities, evaluated the worthy to advance them, reported to the King, and finalized the assessment did he appoint them to office—such was the thoroughness and deliberation shown! This was how they broadened the way of gathering firewood for sacrifice and opened wide the avenues of their nets, so that the ode "Oak Thickets" (Yupu) arose and the transformative nurturing celebrated in "Luxuriant Tarragon" (Jing'e) prevailed.

From this era downward [? 裔是而降], recruitment categories proliferated. The Han dynasty arranged them into four: Flourishing Talent (maocai), Classicist (mingjing), Filial and Incorrupt (xiaolian), and Worthy and良 [Good] (xianliang). Flourishing Talent was further subdivided into three: familiarity with the classics (mingjing), familiarity with the statutes (minglü), and capability of governing complex jurisdictions (zhiju). …

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
明經復疏而爲三甲乙丙也碎召復疏而
爲四德行經術法律才藝也唐析而爲六
秀才明經進士明法明字明筭也宋約而
爲三賢良方正直言極諫經義優深可爲
師法詳閑政理達于教化也世有升降制
由益損故宋不沿唐唐不沿漢漢不沿周
勢也要之乎蒐羅才儁弘熙帝載爾誠得
真才而用之即制與周異奚論哉惟夫孝
廉有冒年之譏明經有曲學之誚劉蕡以
切直見棄葉祖洽以阿諛見收而漢唐宋
之選舉視成周賓典之義始邈邈矣
===
熙朝以經術取士辨黑白而定一諸不在六
籍語孟之科不列學官士不操本業龍不
用脫有姫孔詎越是起家哉而二百年來
鴻士碩卿比肩接轂吾試舉往牒譚之也
論思密勿則有若楊文定商文毅即夔龍
不過也樹績安攘則有若于肅愍馬端肅
即方召不過也捐軀赴難則孫忠烈許忠
punctuated:
明經復疏而爲三：甲、乙、丙也；碎召復疏而爲四：德行、經術、法律、才藝也。唐析而爲六：秀才、明經、進士、明法、明字、明筭也。宋約而爲三：賢良方正直言極諫、經義優深可爲師法、詳閑政理達于教化也。世有升降，制由益損，故宋不沿唐，唐不沿漢，漢不沿周，勢也。要之乎蒐羅才儁，弘熙帝載爾。誠得真才而用之，即制與周異，奚論哉？惟夫孝廉有冒年之譏，明經有曲學之誚，劉蕡以切直見棄，葉祖洽以阿諛見收，而漢、唐、宋之選舉，視成周賓典之義始邈邈矣。
熙朝以經術取士，辨黑白而定一。諸不在《六籍》、《語》、《孟》之科，不列學官；士不操本業，龍不用。脫有姫、孔，詎越是起家哉？而二百年來，鴻士碩卿，比肩接轂，吾試舉往牒譚之也。論思密勿，則有若楊文定、商文毅，即夔、龍不過也；樹績安攘，則有若于肅愍、馬端肅，即方、召不過也；捐軀赴難，則孫忠烈、許忠
translation_en:
Those Proficient in the Classics (mingjing) were further subdivided into three grades: A, B, and C; and those summoned directly to office [?; 碎召 for 辟召] were further subdivided into four categories: moral conduct, classical scholarship, legal statutes, and talent and artistry. The Tang divided them into six categories: Cultivated Talent (xiucai), Proficient in the Classics (mingjing), Metropolitan Graduate (jinshi), Proficient in Law (mingfa), Proficient in Calligraphy (mingzi), and Proficient in Mathematics (mingsuan). The Song reduced them to three categories: Worthy, Upright, and Outspoken in Remonstrance; Profound in Classical Meaning and Fit to Serve as a Model Teacher; and Thoroughly Versed in Administrative Principles and Accomplished in Moral Transformation. As ages rise and fall, institutions are augmented or abridged accordingly; thus the Song did not follow the Tang, the Tang did not follow the Han, and the Han did not follow the Zhou—this is the natural course of events. In essence, all aimed at gathering talented and outstanding men to broaden and brighten the imperial undertakings. If one truly obtains genuine talent and employs it, even if the institution differs from that of the Zhou, what need is there to debate it? Only when the Filially Pious and Incorrupt (xiaolian) incurred criticism for falsifying their ages, when those Proficient in the Classics drew ridicule for distorted learning, when Liu Fen 劉蕡 was rejected for his incisive frankness, and when Ye Zuqia 葉祖洽 was accepted for his sycophancy, did the selection systems of the Han, Tang, and Song begin to drift far indeed from the meaning of the guest-selection canons [?; 賓典 for 賓興] of the成周 (Cheng Zhou) era.

Our illustrious dynasty selects scholars on the basis of classical scholarship, distinguishing black from white and uniting all under a single standard. Any subject not grounded in the Six Classics, the Analects, and the Mencius is not established in the official schools; if scholars do not cultivate these fundamental studies, they are never employed [?; 龍不用 for 終不用]. Even if the Duke of Zhou or Confucius were to appear, how could they rise to prominence by going beyond this? Over the past two hundred years, great scholars and eminent ministers have stood shoulder to shoulder and wheel hub to wheel hub; let me cite past records to discuss them. In deliberating and advising in the privy council, there were men such as Yang Wending 楊文定 (Yang溥) and Shang Wenyi 商文毅 (Shang Lu 商輅),whom even Kui 夔 and Long 龍 could not surpass; in establishing achievements that pacified the realm within and repelled threats without, there were men such as Yu Sumin 于肅愍 (Yu Qian 于謙) and Ma Duansu 馬端肅 (Ma Wensheng 馬文升), whom even Fang Shu 方叔 and Shao Hu 召虎 could not surpass; in sacrificing their lives to confront national crises, the righteous spirit of Sun Zhonglie 孫忠烈 (Sun Sui 孫燧) and Xu Zhong…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
節之正氣非所謂耀日星者與此鱗敢諫
則李文襄黃少卿之抗疏非所謂泣鬼神
者與栖意道德之囿則薛文清王新建爲
之冠游心著作之林則丘文莊鄭端簡爲
之伯之數君子者語德行則閱先民之堂
語文章則漱羣言之潤語事功則鴻名勒
於旂常而駿烈標於青汗蓋下陋漢唐而
上媲周代矣說者顧謂科目不足以得眞
才而必欲舉成周舉選之制而復之愚以
爲說者過也天下之日趨于僞也譬則江
河之流而不返也虞夏而上天下噩噩故
疇咨可行也至周而文明開矣然而淳龐
之氣未漓也故書升可行也至漢而唐而
宋而
===
今日而人之智慧已極糊名易書猶究弊也
若之何其以書升滋弊端也謂書升可以
羅眞才乎則四岳舉鯀何以以圯族誅華
士少正卯世稱聞人而聖人何以以爲戮謂
punctuated: 節之正氣，非所謂耀日星者與？此鱗敢諫，則李文襄、黃少卿之抗疏，非所謂泣鬼神者與？栖意道德之囿，則薛文清、王新建爲之冠；游心著作之林，則丘文莊、鄭端簡爲之伯。之數君子者，語德行，則閱先民之堂；語文章，則漱羣言之潤；語事功，則鴻名勒於旂常，而駿烈標於青汗，蓋下陋漢、唐而上媲周代矣。說者顧謂科目不足以得眞才，而必欲舉成周舉選之制而復之，愚以爲說者過也。天下之日趨于僞也，譬則江河之流而不返也。虞、夏而上，天下噩噩，故疇咨可行也；至周而文明開矣，然而淳龐之氣未漓也，故書升可行也；至漢、而唐、而宋、而今日，而人之智慧已極，糊名易書猶究弊也，若之何其以書升滋弊端也？謂書升可以羅眞才乎？則四岳舉鯀，何以以圯族誅？華士、少正卯，世稱聞人，而聖人何以以爲戮？謂
translation_en:
… Jie [Xu Da 許達]; is their righteous spirit not what is said to outshine the sun and stars? In braving the dragon's scales to remonstrate boldly [reading 此鱗 as 批鱗], there were the defiant memorials of Li Wenxiang [Li Xian 李賢] and Vice Minister Huang [Huang Wan 黃綰 or Huang Gong 黃鞏]; are they not what is said to make ghosts and spirits weep? In dwelling within the garden of morality and virtue, Xue Wenqing [Xue Xuan 薛瑄] and Wang Xinjian [Wang Shouren 王守仁, Earl of Xinjian] stood at the forefront; in letting the mind roam through the forest of literary scholarship, Qiu Wenzhuang [Qiu Jun 丘濬] and Zheng Duanjian [Zheng Xiao 鄭曉] were the foremost leaders. As for these several gentlemen: if we speak of their moral conduct, they entered the hall of the ancients [reading 閱 as 入]; if we speak of their literary writings, they rinsed their mouths in the richness of the myriad words; if we speak of their practical achievements, their great names are inscribed on banners and ritual vessels and theirillustrious deeds are recorded in the bamboo annals of history—looking down upon the Han and Tang dynasties below while matching the Zhou dynasty above!

Yet commentators nonetheless claim that the examination system is insufficient to obtain true talent, and insist on reviving the recommendation and selection system of the flourishing Zhou. In my humble opinion, such commentators are mistaken. The world's daily slide toward falsehood is like the flow of the Yangzi and Yellow Rivers, never to return. From the Yu and Xia eras upward, the world was simple and unadorned, so inquiry and consultation among the court could be practiced. By the Zhou, civilization had blossomed, yet the pure and generous ethos had not yet thinned out, so recording merits and promoting the worthy from the local schools could be practiced. Coming down to the Han, the Tang, the Song, and to the present day, human cleverness and cunning have reached an extreme. Even with sealing candidates' names and transcribing their papers, abuses are still endlessly scrutinized; how then could one use local recommendation and promotion to breed even more avenues for abuse? Do they claim that local recommendation and promotion can net true talent? Then when the Four Peaks recommended Gun, why was he executed for ruining his clan? Huashi and Shaozheng Mao were praised by the world as men of renown, yet why did the sages put them to death? Do they claim that…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
科目果不足以羅眞才乎曩之翊賛休明
而竊奕彝䌌者非異人率是選也故碔砆
似玉文鷄似鷟上以孝求則廬墓者售矣
上以獨行求則割股者售矣上以廉求則
敝衣羸馬者售矣夫制科試士固聖經也
士所習者聖人之經學聖人之學也誠由聖人之經學
聖人之學行聖人之行則不必書升而所
謂德行道藝者自在然則鄉舉里選不必
善科目不必不善古今人不相及而可拘
===
拘同哉顧科目之法行之旣久而士習漸
㢘道術日裂往往致嘆于才難則又何以
故也愚以爲學術貴端也墨子見素絲而
泣曰入乎黃而黃也入乎蒼而蒼也故物
緜染士緜習今士飾銀黃工擘帨剽二氏
而託之乎名高甚至稱引魑魅不經之說
朝廷三令五申習竟不止孟軻氏謂君子反
經而已矣其要在尊經而復古而使周公
孔子之道如揭日月而行天故竽吹則聲
punctuated: 科目果不足以羅眞才乎？曩之翊賛休明，而竊奕彝䌌者，非異人，率是選也。故碔砆似玉，文鷄似鷟。上以孝求，則廬墓者售矣；上以獨行求，則割股者售矣；上以廉求，則敝衣羸馬者售矣。夫制科試士，固聖經也。士所習者聖人之經，學聖人之學也。誠由聖人之經，學聖人之學，行聖人之行，則不必書升，而所謂德行道藝者自在。然則鄉舉里選不必善，科目不必不善，古今人不相及，而可拘拘同哉？顧科目之法，行之旣久，而士習漸㢘，道術日裂，往往致嘆于才難，則又何以故也？愚以爲學術貴端也。墨子見素絲而泣曰：「入乎黃而黃也，入乎蒼而蒼也。」故物緜染，士緜習。今士飾銀黃，工擘帨，剽二氏而託之乎名高，甚至稱引魑魅不經之說，朝廷三令五申，習竟不止。孟軻氏謂：「君子反經而已矣。」其要在尊經而復古，而使周公、孔子之道，如揭日月而行天。故竽吹則聲…
translation_en: …that the examination system is truly insufficient for gathering genuine talent? Those in the past who assisted in a glorious and enlightened reign, and whose achievements were gloriously inscribed on sacrificial vessels and banners [? 竊奕彝䌌], were not men of a different sort—they all came from this selection process. Thus, the wufu stone resembles jade, and a patterned pheasant resembles the zhuo phoenix. When superiors seek filial piety, those who build huts by graves succeed in advancing; when superiors seek extraordinary conduct, those who slice flesh from their thighs succeed in advancing; when superiors seek incorruptibility, those who wear tattered clothes and ride lean horses succeed in advancing. Now, testing scholars through the regular examinations is based on the sacred Classics. What scholars practice are the Classics of the sages, and they study the learning of the sages. If indeed they follow the Classics of the sages, study the learning of the sages, and practice the conduct of the sages, then there is no need for the ancient system of recording and promoting from local schools, for what are called moral conduct, the Way, and the arts are naturally present therein. This being so, local recommendation and village selection are not necessarily good, and the examination system is not necessarily bad. People of ancient and modern times are not the same; how can one rigidly insist on making their institutions identical? Yet, as the system of examinations has been practiced for a long time, the habits of scholars have gradually grown decadent [? 㢘], and the Way and its arts are daily torn apart, often leading to sighs over the scarcity of talent—why is this so? I humbly believe that in scholarly learning, what is valued is orthodoxy. Master Mo (Mozi 墨子) sawundyed silk and wept, saying: "Put into yellow dye, it becomes yellow; put into blue dye, it becomes blue." Thus, things depend on what dyes them, and scholars depend on what they habituate themselves to. Nowadays, scholars embellish their diction like silver and gold and labor over carving and embroidering petty rhetoric [? 飾銀黃工擘帨]; they plagiarize from the two sects of Buddhism and Daoism and use them to lay claim to lofty reputations, going so far as to cite absurd and uncanonical talk of demons and sprites. Though the court issues repeated orders and injunctions, the habit ultimately does not cease. Mencius (Meng Ke 孟軻) said: "The gentleman simply returns to the standard (Classics)." The essential point lies in venerating the Classics and restoring antiquity, causing the Way of the Duke of Zhou (Zhougong 周公) and Confucius (Kongzi 孔子) to be like holding up the sun and moon to travel across the heavens. Thus, when theリード pipe (yu) is blown, the voices…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
和鵠立則射趍而後道德一風俗同也愚
又以爲廉恥貴勵也齊人伐魯取饞鼎魯
以贋鼎往齊人曰必柳下惠之言爲信魯
人語柳下惠柳下惠曰奚不以眞者與之
魯人曰愛吾鼎柳下惠辭曰吾亦愛吾鼎
故士各有鼎也今士貴進取而賤廉潔重
儇通而輕椎魯尚洪恣而鄙孤高上以是
求下以是應是使士喪鼎也上誠毋令士
喪鼎士亦自愛其鼎則才別才別則厝注
===
別所裨于國家非淺鮮也愚又以爲師儒
之選貴擇也雲門咸池非伶倫不調純鉤
湛盧非歐冶不鑄黌校固士之工與冶也
而令遲暮蒙闒者充之士曷型焉誠得人
如胡瑗端模範肅條秩甄陶其德性而銷
鑠其私而後恂飭之士可得也愚又以爲
貢舉之途貴慎也冀北之群非伯樂不識
鄧林之材非班倕不採今貢舉固士之冀
北鄧林也雅不錄浮不黜士何觀焉誠得
punctuated: 和，鵠立則射趍，而後道德一、風俗同也。愚又以爲廉恥貴勵也。齊人伐魯，取饞鼎，魯以贋鼎往。齊人曰：「必柳下惠之言爲信。」魯人語柳下惠，柳下惠曰：「奚不以眞者與之？」魯人曰：「愛吾鼎。」柳下惠辭曰：「吾亦愛吾鼎。」故士各有鼎也。今士貴進取而賤廉潔，重儇通而輕椎魯，尚洪恣而鄙孤高，上以是求，下以是應，是使士喪鼎也。上誠毋令士喪鼎，士亦自愛其鼎，則才別，才別則厝注別，所裨于國家非淺鮮也。愚又以爲師儒之選貴擇也。雲門、咸池，非伶倫不調；純鉤、湛盧，非歐冶不鑄。黌校固士之工與冶也，而令遲暮蒙闒者充之，士曷型焉？誠得人如胡瑗，端模範，肅條秩，甄陶其德性而銷鑠其私，而後恂飭之士可得也。愚又以爲貢舉之途貴慎也。冀北之群，非伯樂不識；鄧林之材，非班倕不採。今貢舉固士之冀北、鄧林也，雅不錄、浮不黜，士何觀焉？誠得
translation_en:
… harmonize, and when the target is set up the archers hasten toward it; only then will morality be unified and customs made uniform.

I also believe that a sense of honor and shame ought to be encouraged. When the men of Qi attacked Lu and demanded the Chan tripod, Lu sent a counterfeit tripod instead. The men of Qi said, "We will only believe it if Liuxia Hui 柳下惠 says it is genuine." When the men of Lu spoke to Liuxia Hui, Liuxia Hui said, "Why not give them the real one?" The men of Lu replied, "We cherish our tripod." Liuxia Hui declined, saying, "I too cherish my tripod [of integrity]." Thus every scholar has his own tripod. Nowadays, scholars value career advancement and despise integrity and purity, prize slick adaptability and look down on simple honesty, esteem unrestrained license and scorn solitary loftiness. Those above seek them on this basis, and those below respond accordingly—this causes scholars to lose their tripods. If those above truly do not cause scholars to lose their tripods, and scholars also cherish their own tripods, then talents will be differentiated; when talents are differentiated, their practical deployment will be differentiated, and the benefit to the state will not be slight.

I also believe that in the appointment of Confucian teachers, careful selection is essential. The Yunmen and Xianchi music could not be tuned without Ling Lun 伶倫; the Chungou and Zhanlu swords could not be cast without Ou Ye 歐冶. Schools are indeed the musicians and smiths that shape scholars, yet if we allow senile, ignorant, and mediocre men to fill these posts, what model will scholars have to pattern themselves after? If we truly obtain men like Hu Yuan 胡瑗 to rectify the model, enforce orderly rules, mold their moral nature, and melt away their selfishness, then sincere and disciplined scholars may be obtained.

I also believe that the avenue of recommendation and examination ought to be managed with caution. The herds of northern Ji could not be recognized without Bo Le 伯樂; the timber of Deng Forest could not be harvested without Ban 班 and Chui 倕. Today, the recommendation and examination system is indeed the northern Ji and Deng Forest of scholars. If the refined are not selected and the superficial are not dismissed, what standard will scholars have to look to? If we truly obtain …

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
人如歐陽脩抑奇袞黜踏駁以通經學古
爲高以繢章繪句爲戒而後大雅之風可
挽也之門者皆所以維科目之弊也而猶
未也愚尤竊有說焉科目不可廢矣書升
不可復矣然
祖宗朝不有孝弟力田賢良方正令有司各舉
所知者乎又不有大臣薦舉遣行人聘召
者乎鼓之皮丹砂之屑良醫不棄今制三
途止矣貢于膠庠者以日暮躑起于任子
===
者以膏梁沮入粟賜爵者以商賈棄法律
起家者以刀筆摧而世所與羅豪傑者一
制科耳提衡量而程槩之累黍儀毫十不
得一是以踈𨁝俶儻之夫或齟齬于尺幅
丘巖高蹈之士多跼伏于蓬蒿而
國家何從而得其一臂力也茲欲廣羅人才
莫若考
令甲倣故事以科目爲主而其他間一行之
如是而野有白駒之嘆朝無宅俊之臣者
punctuated: 人如歐陽脩，抑奇袞、黜踏駁，以通經學古爲高，以繢章繪句爲戒，而後大雅之風可挽也。之門者，皆所以維科目之弊也，而猶未也，愚尤竊有說焉。科目不可廢矣，書升不可復矣，然祖宗朝不有「孝弟力田」、「賢良方正」，令有司各舉所知者乎？又不有大臣薦舉、遣行人聘召者乎？鼓之皮、丹砂之屑，良醫不棄。今制三途止矣：貢于膠庠者以日暮躑，起于任子者以膏梁沮，入粟賜爵者以商賈棄，法律起家者以刀筆摧；而世所與羅豪傑者，一制科耳。提衡量而程槩之，累黍儀毫，十不得一。是以踈𨁝俶儻之夫，或齟齬于尺幅；丘巖高蹈之士，多跼伏于蓬蒿，而國家何從而得其一臂力也？茲欲廣羅人才，莫若考令甲、倣故事，以科目爲主，而其他間一行之。如是，而野有《白駒》之嘆、朝無宅俊之臣者，
translation_en: … someone like Ouyang Xiu 歐陽脩, who suppressed the eccentric and strange [奇袤?] and rejected the mixed and impure [踏駁 -> 駮駁], valuing thorough mastery of the Classics and study of antiquity while warning against ornate phrasing and embellished sentences—only then can the ethos of high elegance be restored. These four [之門 -> 四?] measures are all means of remedying the abuses of the examination system; and yet this is still not all, for I humbly have a further proposal. The examination system cannot be abolished, nor can the ancient practice of recording and promoting talent from the local schools be revived. Yet during the reigns of our Imperial Ancestors, were there not the special categories of "Filial, Fraternal, and Diligent in Farming" (xiaodi litian 孝弟力田) and "Worthy, Good, Square, and Upright" (xianliang fangzheng 賢良方正), under which the authorities were ordered each to recommend those whom they knew? And were there not also recommendations by Grand Ministers and invitations issued by dispatching Messengers (xingren 行人)? A skilled physician does not discard the skin of an old drum or the crumbs of cinnabar. Under the present system, the three avenues of entry have effectively been reduced to a standstill: Tribute Students from the state schools are held back by their advancing years; those who enter through the protection privilege (renzi 任子) are thwarted as pampered scions of wealth; those granted rank for contributing grain are spurned as merchants; and those who rise through legal studies are disparaged as mere petty scribes. Thus, the sole means by which the world nets heroic talent is the regular civil service examination alone. When candidates are weighed on the balance and measured with the strike-stick down to the smallest grain and hair's breadth, not one in ten succeeds. Consequently, men of bold, untrammeled, and extraordinary mettle often find themselves at odds with the narrow confines of the examination paper, while lofty-minded scholars among the hills and cliffs mostly remain crouched in obscurity amid thebrushwood—how, then, is the State to gain the help of their strength? If we now wish to cast a wide net for men of talent, nothing would be better than to examine the statutory ordinances and follow historical precedents, keeping the examination system as the main avenue while occasionally putting those other methods into practice. If this is done, then that there should still be the lament of the ode "White Colt" (Baiju 白駒) in the wilderness, or a lack of worthy and eminent ministers serving at court, …

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
愚不信也雖然有取士者有所以取士者
試問上之化下如鈞與壚璧之孟圜則水
圜孟方則水方轉移化導之機惟在人主
加之意而已漢高大度故其時多瑰傑不
羈之士漢武喜功名故其時多瓌詭立名
之士漢宣精吏治故其時多循良綜核之
吏是以聖上邇穆清之上握甄陶之紀中
心無爲以守至正已雕已琢復反其樸如
此則八埏之外夫孰不祓濯其心志而宅
於醇賢哲景從庶明勵翼卽軼成周而駕
===
唐虞可也奚科目之足云
第五問
趙任
同考試官訓導陳 批〔條陳□□利害明如觀火而末復規之以實心實政請之渥然〕
考試官教諭郭 批〔□□議甚核而□□後事理尤見肯綮儒者明體經國之華也〕
考試官教諭林 批〔□□乃東省最務子能籌畫無遺足〕
punctuated:
愚不信也。雖然，有取士者，有所以取士者。試問上之化下，如鈞與壚，璧之孟圜則水圜，孟方則水方。轉移化導之機，惟在人主加之意而已。漢高大度，故其時多瑰傑不羈之士；漢武喜功名，故其時多瓌詭立名之士；漢宣精吏治，故其時多循良綜核之吏。是以聖上邇穆清之上，握甄陶之紀，中心無爲，以守至正，已雕已琢，復反其樸。如此，則八埏之外，夫孰不祓濯其心志而宅於醇？賢哲景從，庶明勵翼，卽軼成周而駕唐、虞可也，奚科目之足云！

第五問
趙任
同考試官訓導陳 批〔條陳□□利害，明如觀火，而末復規之以實心實政，請之渥然。〕
考試官教諭郭 批〔□□議甚核，而□□後事理尤見肯綮，儒者明體經國之華也。〕
考試官教諭林 批〔□□乃東省最務，子能籌畫無遺，足〕
translation_en:
…I do not believe it. Even so, there are the methods for selecting scholars, and there is that which lies behind the selection of scholars. Consider how those above transform those below: it is like the potter's wheel and the kiln; or to draw an analogy [?], if the bowl is round then the water is round, and if the bowl is square then the water is square. The pivot for shifting and guiding customs lies solely in the ruler directing his intentions toward it. Emperor Gao of Han (漢高) was magnanimous, and therefore in his time there were many extraordinary and unrestrained scholars; Emperor Wu of Han (漢武) delighted in merit and fame, and therefore in his time there were many marvellous, eccentric scholars bent on establishing a name; Emperor Xuan of Han (漢宣) was meticulous in administrative governance, and therefore in his time there were many upright, benign, and rigorously verifying officials. Thus, if His Sacred Majesty, dwelling aloft in solemn purity [?], holds the guiding threads of molding and fashioning, abides in non-action within his heart so as to preserve the utmost rectitude, and after carving and polishing returns again to uncarved simplicity—if it is like this, then even beyond the eight reaches of the world, who would not cleanse their hearts and minds and dwell in pure sincerity? Worthies and sages will follow like shadows, and the host of enlightened officials will exert themselves to assist; even to surpass the accomplished Zhou (周) and override Tang (唐) and Yu (虞) would be possible—what need is there even to speak of examination categories!

Fifth Question
Zhao Ren (趙任)
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Chen (陳), comments: 〔He sets forth step by step the advantages and disadvantages of […], as clear as looking at fire, and at the end further admonishes with sincere heart and substantive governance; reading [?] it, one finds it richly substantial.〕
Examiner, Instructor Guo (郭), comments: 〔The discussion of […] is very rigorous, and after […], the principles of the matters especially hit the crucial points; it is the splendid flower of a Confucian scholar who understands fundamental substance and orders the state.〕
Examiner, Instructor Lin (林), comments: 〔[…] is the most urgent affair of the eastern province (Shandong); you are able to plan it out without omission, which suffices…〕

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
夫民之待利于上不甚亟哉利一而害倍
民必齟齬而不從利一害一而從之者半
矣害一而利倍而從之者十之九矣利而
亡害而民不從十無一矣善爲政者知民
避害而趍利故予之以利而去其害予之
以利則爲之治其常生之業而勿使有流
離之憂去其害則爲之盡其經久之圖而
勿使有侵剝之患挈是而譚而山東墾荒
之議無難策也且夫先王所以足國賦而
===
阜民生者孰有急於土田哉粤稽田之
制肇于軒轅則壤之賦陳于禹貢而所從
來遠矣周禮遂師遂大夫掌敎民稼穡之
務而先王巡狩覜田之關蕪爲慶讓焉誠
重之也吾試舉山東譚之也夫土黑墳田
中下賦貞作十有三載乃同者非兗州邪
土白墳海濵廣斥田上下賦中上者非靑
州邪周公封魯太公封齊大都用助貢法
punctuated: 夫民之待利于上，不甚亟哉？利一而害倍，民必齟齬而不從；利一害一，而從之者半矣；害一而利倍，而從之者十之九矣；利而亡害，而民不從，十無一矣。善爲政者，知民避害而趍利，故予之以利而去其害。予之以利，則爲之治其常生之業，而勿使有流離之憂；去其害，則爲之盡其經久之圖，而勿使有侵剝之患。挈是而譚，而山東墾荒之議，無難策也。且夫先王所以足國賦而阜民生者，孰有急於土田哉？粤稽田之制，肇于軒轅，則壤之賦，陳于《禹貢》，而所從來遠矣。《周禮》遂師、遂大夫掌敎民稼穡之務，而先王巡狩，覜田之闢蕪爲慶讓焉，誠重之也。吾試舉山東譚之也。夫「土黑墳，田中下，賦貞，作十有三載乃同」者，非兗州邪？「土白墳，海濵廣斥，田上下，賦中上」者，非靑州邪？周公封魯，太公封齊，大都用助、貢法，
translation_en: How urgent indeed is the people's expectation of benefit from those above! If there is one part benefit and twice the harm, the people will certainly resist and refuse to follow; if there is one part benefit and one part harm, half will follow; if there is one part harm and twice the benefit, nine out of ten will follow; if there is benefit and no harm, not one in ten of the people will fail to follow. Those who excel at governance know that the people avoid harm and pursue benefit; therefore, they grant them benefit and remove their harm. To grant them benefit is to establish for them livelihoods for their constant sustenance, so that they do not suffer the sorrow of displacement; to remove their harm is to exhaustively devise for them long-lasting plans, so that they do not suffer the affliction of encroachment and exploitation. Taking this as our guiding principle in discussion, the deliberations on reclaiming wasteland in Shandong present no difficulty in formulating a policy. Moreover, in the former kings' means of sufficing state revenues and enriching the people's livelihood, what was more urgent than land and fields? Examining antiquity, the system of fields began with Xuanyuan [the Yellow Emperor], and taxation graded by soil quality was set forth in the "Tribute of Yu" (Yugong); thus its origins are remote indeed. In the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), the Master of the Outlying Districts (suishi) and the Grand Master of the Outlying Districts (suidafu) were in charge of instructing the people in the tasks of sowing and reaping, and when the former kings went on tours of inspection, they observed whether the fields were opened up or left overgrown in order to dispense rewards and reprimands—truly because they attached great importance to it. Let me try to discuss this by citing Shandong. Now, "its soil is black and rich, its fields are of the lower-middle grade, its revenue is of the lowest grade, and after thirteen years of labor it was brought into parity"—is this not Yanzhou? "Its soil is white and rich, the sea-shores are wide expanses of salt-marsh, its fields are of the lower-upper grade, and its revenue is of the upper-middle grade"—is this not Qingzhou? When the Duke of Zhou was enfeoffed in Lu and Duke Tai was enfeoffed in Qi, for the most part they used the mutual-aid (zhu) and tribute (gong) methods of taxation, …

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
田固未甞不墾也齊世中衰管仲相桓公
創霸仲之書曰積於不涸之倉藏於不竭
之府府與倉即五穀桑麻六畜田亦未甞
不墾也逮夫近世而地有遺利民庶不耕
者何也說者曰東兗瀕河沮洳斥鹵之患
往往而是而青萊三郡濱大海瀉鹵儲之
田卒汙萊天之荒也非人之咎也雖然人
力之至山可塹谷可塞龍門可鑿造化可
奪而矧墾荒乎蓋甞考鏡前代而得石晝
===
之吏也鎮襄陽而墾田八百餘頃則有若
羊祜祜始至軍無百日之儲迨其季年食
可支十歲竟以平吳皆祜力也修召信臣
故迹而公私利之則有若杜預預乘羊祜
後激用滍淯諸水以漫原田萬餘頃分疆
刻石使有定分厥績懋焉為營田使而起
代北墾田三百頃非韓重華乎給耒耜耕
牛假種已而開營田三千八百餘里歲收
粟二十萬石省度支錢二千萬緡則重華
punctuated: 田固未甞不墾也。齊世中衰，管仲相桓公創霸，仲之書曰：「積於不涸之倉，藏於不竭之府。」府與倉，即五穀、桑麻、六畜，田亦未甞不墾也。逮夫近世，而地有遺利，民庶不耕者，何也？說者曰：「東、兗瀕河，沮洳斥鹵之患往往而是；而青、萊三郡濱大海，瀉鹵儲之，田卒汙萊。天之荒也，非人之咎也。」雖然，人力之至，山可塹，谷可塞，龍門可鑿，造化可奪，而矧墾荒乎？蓋甞考鏡前代，而得石晝之吏也。鎮襄陽而墾田八百餘頃，則有若羊祜。祜始至，軍無百日之儲，迨其季年，食可支十歲，竟以平吳，皆祜力也。修召信臣故迹，而公私利之，則有若杜預。預乘羊祜後，激用滍、淯諸水，以漫原田萬餘頃，分疆刻石，使有定分，厥績懋焉。為營田使而起代北，墾田三百頃，非韓重華乎？給耒耜、耕牛，假種，已而開營田三千八百餘里，歲收粟二十萬石，省度支錢二千萬緡，則重華
translation_en: …the fields were certainly never left uncultivated. When the ruling house of Qi fell into decline, Guan Zhong 管仲 served as minister to Duke Huan 桓公 and established his hegemony. In Guan Zhong's book [Guanzi], it is said: "Store in granaries that do not run dry; hoard in treasuries that are never exhausted." Those treasuries and granaries consisted of none other than the five grains, mulberry and hemp, and the six domestic animals; thus the fields were also never left uncultivated. Yet when we come down to recent times, why is it that the land has unexploited resources and the common people do not plow? Commentators say: "Dongchang 東昌 and Yanzhou 兗州 border the Yellow River, where the afflictions of waterlogged marshes and saline soil are found everywhere; meanwhile, the three prefectures around Qingzhou 青州 and Laizhou 萊州 border the great sea, where salty and alkaline waters accumulate [?], so that the fields end up flooded or overgrown with weeds. This is wasteland made by Heaven, not the fault of men." Even so, when human effort reaches its utmost, mountains can be trenched through, valleys can be filled in, the Longmen 龍門 gorge can be chiseled open, and the work of nature itself can be wrested away—how much more so the reclamation of wasteland! Indeed, I have examined the mirror of former dynasties and found officials who formulated rock-solid plans [?]. For garrisoning Xiangyang 襄陽 and reclaiming over eight hundred qing of land, there was the example of Yang Hu 羊祜. When Hu first arrived, the army did not have provisions for a hundred days; by his final years, food supplies could last for ten years, and in the end Wu 吳 was pacified—all through Hu's strength. For restoring the former waterworks of Shao Xinchen 召信臣 to the benefit of both public and private interests, there was the example of Du Yu 杜預. Succeeding Yang Hu, Yu dammed and channeled the waters of the Zhi 滍 and Yu 淯 rivers to irrigate over ten thousand qing of plateau fields, dividing the boundaries and engraving stone markers so that everyone had a fixed allotment, whereby his achievements were grand indeed. Was it not Han Chonghua 韓重華 who served as Agricultural Colony Commissioner (yingtianshi 營田使) and began in northern Dai 代北 by reclaiming three hundred qing of fields? He supplied plows and draft oxen and lent out seed, and before long opened up agricultural colonies stretching over three thousand eight hundred li, harvesting two hundred thousand shi of grain each year and saving the Finance Commission (duzhi 度支) twenty million strings of cash; thus Chonghua's…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
之衛與周也兗河北判官而興堰六百里
非黃懋乎置斗門引水灌溉已而荒蕪皆
蛤之饒民賴其利則懋之爲計得也之四
子者夫非善墾荒者邪懷無疆之圖而建
必然之畫一舉而民生國計胥裨焉則安
可謂人力不足恃而荒終不可墾也
國朝
令甲凡山東空閑地聽民開種永不起科其
便民計至熟也嘉靖間當事之臣嘗一議
===
世廟俞允特令使者行部核其事歲報若干殿
最諸長吏其立法至嚴也民投墾者官給
牛種復二年越三年始稅其拊循意至厚
也然而二十餘年汶萊如故歲終覈報竟
屬虛文者則有故焉夫沃田必不荒而荒
者必瘠也沃則事半而功倍瘠則事倍而
功半以事之倍企功之半費甚鉅也即寬
其二年之賦寧足償乎勞費未償徵斂遄
墾矣
punctuated:
之衛與周也。兗河北判官而興堰六百里，非黃懋乎？置斗門引水灌溉，已而荒蕪皆蛤之饒，民賴其利，則懋之爲計得也。之四子者，夫非善墾荒者邪？懷無疆之圖，而建必然之畫，一舉而民生國計胥裨焉，則安可謂人力不足恃，而荒終不可墾也？
國朝令甲：凡山東空閑地，聽民開種，永不起科。其便民計至熟也。嘉靖間，當事之臣嘗一議墾矣。世廟俞允，特令使者行部核其事，歲報若干，殿最諸長吏，其立法至嚴也。民投墾者，官給牛種，復二年，越三年始稅，其拊循意至厚也。然而二十餘年，汶萊如故，歲終覈報竟屬虛文者，則有故焉。夫沃田必不荒，而荒者必瘠也。沃則事半而功倍，瘠則事倍而功半。以事之倍，企功之半，費甚鉅也。即寬其二年之賦，寧足償乎？勞費未償，徵斂遄
translation_en:
… safeguarded and comprehensively provided for things. As for filling the post of Administrative Assistant of Hebei and building six hundred li of embankments, was that not Huang Mao 黃懋? He installed sluice gates to channel water for irrigation, and before long the uncultivated wastes all yielded the abundance of wild rice and shellfish [蛤 for 菰蛤], on whose benefits the people relied—thus Mao's planning succeeded. Were these four men not skilled at reclaiming wasteland? Harboring boundless vision and establishing unfailing plans, at a single stroke they benefited both the people's livelihood and the state's finances. How then can it be said that human effort cannot be relied upon and that wasteland can never be reclaimed?

In the statutes of our dynasty, any vacant and idle land in Shandong was permitted to be opened and cultivated by the people, forever exempt from taxation. This plan for the convenience of the people was most thoroughly considered. During the Jiajing 嘉靖 reign (1522–1566), the officials in charge once proposed a plan for land reclamation. The Shizong Emperor (世廟) gave his approval and specially ordered an envoy to tour the region and verify the matter, reporting the amount reclaimed each year to rank the various local magistrates by merit and demerit; the law established was most strict. For commoners who registered to reclaim land, the authorities supplied oxen and seed, exempted them from obligations for two years, and only began taxing them in the third year; the intention to comfort and nurture them was most generous. And yet for more than twenty years, the lands along the Wen River have remained overgrown with weeds as before, and the year-end verification reports have turned out to be mere empty words—for which there is a reason. Fertile fields are surely never left uncultivated, and what is left uncultivated is surely barren. On fertile land, half the effort yields double the result; on barren land, double the effort yields half the result. Expending double the effort in hopes of half the result entails immense cost. Even if taxes are remitted for two years, how could that suffice to compensate for it? Before the labor and expense have been recouped, tax collection swiftly…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
至里胥索逋而富室責券誶無已時矣語
曰天下攘攘皆爲利往天下熙熙皆爲利
來今未覩墾荒之利而輒罹其害民甘之
乎䖍兕䖍虎寧率彼曠野耳有司避譴輒
僞增以報而使者亦日夜跂徙而釋負去
也田不加尺寸之籍租不加升合之入而
嗷嗷然號于人曰墾荒刻脂鏤冰徒有其
文塵飯塗羹可爲戲耳或者謂荒之不墾
則地額未清所致抲荒爲沃隱沃爲荒民
===
之所以告病也是一說也邇者
皇上軫念民嵒特
令丈地乃魚鱗踏丈首以清額報者非東省
邪乘丈地之後而行墾荒之政其勢甚易
顧百姓懼於輸租如嘉靖故事則召募流
移占種鮮有應者近當事諮得其故又即
一二已試之效而建爲之議凡額外荒地
聽民開墾每畝歲輸穀三升永不科賦疏
入得
punctuated: 至，里胥索逋而富室責券，誶無已時矣。語曰：「天下攘攘，皆爲利往；天下熙熙，皆爲利來。」今未覩墾荒之利，而輒罹其害，民甘之乎？䖍兕䖍虎，寧率彼曠野耳。有司避譴，輒僞增以報，而使者亦日夜跂徙而釋負去也。田不加尺寸之籍，租不加升合之入，而嗷嗷然號于人曰「墾荒」，刻脂鏤冰，徒有其文，塵飯塗羹，可爲戲耳。或者謂荒之不墾，則地額未清所致，抲荒爲沃，隱沃爲荒，民之所以告病也，是一說也。邇者皇上軫念民嵒，特令丈地，乃魚鱗踏丈，首以清額報者，非東省邪？乘丈地之後而行墾荒之政，其勢甚易。顧百姓懼於輸租，如嘉靖故事，則召募流移占種，鮮有應者。近當事諮得其故，又即一二已試之效，而建爲之議：凡額外荒地，聽民開墾，每畝歲輸穀三升，永不科賦。疏入，得
translation_en:
… arrive; village clerks demand arrears while wealthy households press for repayment on loan deeds, with endless berating and harassment. As the saying goes: "All the world bustles about, rushing after profit; all the world hustles along, coming for profit." Now, before seeing any profit from reclaiming wasteland, the people immediately suffer its harms—would they willingly endure this? Though neither rhinoceroses nor tigers [?], they would rather roam those desolate wilds! To avoid reprimand, the local authorities routinely fabricate increases in their reports, while the commissioners likewise stand on tiptoe day and night waiting to be transferred and lay down their burden. Not an inch or foot of land is added to the registers, nor a pint or gill of grain added to the tax revenues, yet they clamorously proclaim to everyone, "Reclaiming wasteland!" This is like carving grease or engraving ice—possessing mere outward form; or like rice made of dust and soup made of mud—good only for child's play.

Some say that the failure to reclaim wasteland is caused by land quotas not being cleared up: misrepresenting [?] wasteland as fertile land, and concealing fertile land as wasteland, which is why the people complain of hardship. This is one explanation. Recently, His Majesty, in his compassionate concern for the hardships [?] of the people, specially ordered a land survey. And in conducting the step-by-step fish-scale survey, was not the Eastern Province (Shandong) the very first to report cleared quotas? Taking advantage of the completed land survey to carry out the policy of wasteland reclamation makes the task very easy in circumstance. Yet if the common people fear paying land taxes as happened under the precedent of the Jiajing era (1522–1566), then when vagrants and migrants are recruited to occupy and cultivate the land, few will respond. Recently, the authorities in charge inquired into and discovered the reason for this, and drawing upon one or two already proven successes, established a proposal: for all wasteland outside the quota, allow the people to open and cultivate it, paying three pints (sheng) of grain per mu annually, and never levying regular land taxes upon it. When the memorial was submitted, it received …

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
俞旨
上若曰誠令無流亡吾何愛錙銖入不以便百
姓哉揭榜刻石檄郡邑長吏總其事丞倅
分領之歲計幾何上之計部毀成〔冊給執〕
照示信也定盈亏之式塡地形之圖令晝
一也一時人心景從響應不數月闢而土
著流寓之衆咸請有司投牒受田爭摩而
衽接矣夫嘉靖間寬賦于二年之後而地
荒如故今額輸穀于初墾之年而民樂從
===
則民情可想也復民二年三年則稅之是
紓死于昏而遲之旦也所謂利一害倍而
民齟齬而不從也輸穀三升賦永蠲矣挈
千金與人而不責其直民不懽乎所謂利
而亡害而不從者十無一也率是著爲
令愚竊以爲計之便雖然墾荒之議冇三而
其害有二藉令曆注一不當則不有廢格
明旨而壅閼澀澤者乎夫十室之邑人人提耳
猶懼弗逮今令長吏巡行阡陌顧萑葦蕭
punctuated: 俞旨。上若曰：「誠令無流亡，吾何愛錙銖入，不以便百姓哉！」揭榜刻石，檄郡邑長吏總其事，丞倅分領之。歲計幾何，上之計部，毀成〔冊給執〕照，示信也；定盈亏之式，塡地形之圖，令晝一也。一時人心景從響應，不數月闢，而土著流寓之衆，咸請有司投牒受田，爭摩而衽接矣。夫嘉靖間寬賦于二年之後，而地荒如故；今額輸穀于初墾之年，而民樂從，則民情可想也。復民二年，三年則稅之，是紓死于昏而遲之旦也，所謂利一害倍，而民齟齬而不從也；輸穀三升，賦永蠲矣，挈千金與人而不責其直，民不懽乎？所謂利而亡害，而不從者十無一也。率是著爲令，愚竊以爲計之便。雖然，墾荒之議冇三，而其害有二，藉令曆注一不當，則不有廢格明旨而壅閼澀澤者乎？夫十室之邑，人人提耳，猶懼弗逮，今令長吏巡行阡陌，顧萑葦蕭
translation_en:
…an approving rescript. It was as if the Emperor said: "If only we can truly prevent people from fleeing and becoming vagrants, why would I begrudge a tiny fraction of revenue and not use it to benefit the common people!" Placards were posted and stone steles engraved. Directives were sent to the chief magistrates of prefectures and counties to take overall charge of the matter, while their assistants and deputies were assigned specific responsibilities. Each year, the amount reclaimed is calculated and reported to the Ministry of Revenue. The completed registers [?] are used to issue certificates of ownership [?], demonstrating good faith; formats for recording surpluses and deficits are established and maps of the terrain are filled in, ensuring uniformity. All at once, people's hearts followed like shadows and responded like echoes. Within a few months of opening the land, both native residents and migrant settlers all petitioned the authorities, submitting applications to receive fields, rubbing shoulders and crowding together in their eagerness.

Now, during the Jiajing reign (1522–1566), taxes were remitted for two years, yet the land remained as desolate as before; today, a fixed quota of grain is paid from the very first year of reclamation, yet the people gladly comply. From this, the sentiments of the people can easily be imagined. To exempt the people for two years and then tax them in the third year is like postponing death in the evening only to execute it at dawn—this is what is meant by one benefit bringing double the harm, causing the people to balk and refuse to comply. By paying three sheng of grain, regular land taxes are permanently remitted; it is like handing a thousand pieces of gold to someone without demanding its price—how could the people not rejoice? This is what is meant by having benefit without harm, where not one in ten will fail to comply. To follow this and establish it as an ordinance is what I humbly consider an advantageous plan.

Nevertheless, there are three proposals regarding the reclamation of wasteland, and two harms. Suppose the implementation and execution [?] are in any way improper; would this not amount to obstructing the Emperor's clear decree and blocking up the flow of imperial grace? Even in a hamlet of ten households, if one instructs every person face to face, one still fears not reaching everyone. Now, if we order the chief magistrates to tour the field paths, looking out over reeds, rushes, and wormwood…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
艾窮鄉僻陬足跡莫遍也莫若擇其名豪
無論胥監胥吏之屬令宣
朝廷德意以一教十家喻户曉耳漸目濡而
有司者又時時勞來之故鴻鴈有中澤之
咏而碩鼠無樂土之謠也所當議者一也
頃有司議支帑金給牛種愚以爲投籍之
衆泉湧雲集取之帑非盡也宜敕曩時嘗
牛影占者亟行追奪以予貧民而官庾有
新穀可爲種者輒借給之民有小貿量輸
===
特一穀若干貫不治奇贏之家轉貸佐縣
官緩急官爲復其身以酬勞焉可也所當
議者二也于茅索綯乘屋播穀詩人咏焉
百姓箄絡藍縷以處草莽而棲無廬是鳥
去林魚去壑也閔閔焉病矣宜令郡邑各
𠜂官莊數十所募民僦居之寛其直越三
年而後償焉什伍繹絡而田可卒治也所
當議者三也三者皆便民大計而其或有
沮格而不行則愚以爲侵占貴懲也夫豪
punctuated:
艾，窮鄉僻陬，足跡莫遍也。莫若擇其名豪，無論胥監、胥吏之屬，令宣朝廷德意，以一教十，家喻户曉，耳漸目濡，而有司者又時時勞來之，故《鴻鴈》有「中澤」之咏，而《碩鼠》無「樂土」之謠也。所當議者一也。
頃有司議支帑金給牛種，愚以爲投籍之衆，泉湧雲集，取之帑非盡也。宜敕曩時嘗牛影占者，亟行追奪以予貧民；而官庾有新穀可爲種者，輒借給之；民有小貿，量輸特一穀若干貫；不治奇贏之家，轉貸佐縣官緩急，官爲復其身以酬勞焉，可也。所當議者二也。
「于茅索綯，乘屋播穀」，詩人咏焉。百姓箄絡藍縷以處草莽，而棲無廬，是鳥去林、魚去壑也，閔閔焉病矣。宜令郡邑各𠜂官莊數十所，募民僦居之，寛其直，越三年而後償焉，什伍繹絡，而田可卒治也。所當議者三也。
三者皆便民大計，而其或有沮格而不行，則愚以爲侵占貴懲也。夫豪
translation_en:
…and mugwort; in remote villages and isolated corners, their footsteps cannot reach everywhere. It would be best to select prominent local figures, regardless of whether they are subofficial functionaries, Imperial Academy students [?], or lesser clerks, and have them proclaim the benevolent intentions of the Court. With one instructing ten, every family and household will understand; their ears and eyes will gradually be steeped in it, while the authorities also from time to time comfort and encourage them. Thus there will be the song of "the middle of the marsh" from the "Wild Geese" (Hongyan) ode, and no ballad of "the happy land" from "Big Rat" (Shuoshu). This is the first matter that ought to be deliberated.

Recently the authorities proposed disbursing treasury silver to supply oxen and seed. In my humble opinion, with people coming to register surging like springs and gathering like clouds, drawing from the treasury cannot supply them all. Orders should be issued that those who in the past fraudulently occupied [official] oxen [?] be urgently pursued and stripped of them so they may be given to poor commoners; and where official granaries have new grain suitable for seed, it should promptly be loaned out to them. Where commoners engage in small trade, let them contribute according to measure a single beast or a certain number of strings of grain [?]; and as for families that do not pursue speculative profits [or: wealthy families with surplus] who lend to assist the county magistrate in emergencies, it would be permissible for the authorities to grant them exemption from service in reward for their labor. This is the second matter that ought to be deliberated.
