"Gathering thatch and twisting ropes, climbing onto roofs and sowing grain"—thus sang the poet [of the Book of Odes]. When the common people, in wicker frames and ragged clothes, dwell among the wild grasses without huts to shelter in, they are like birds that have left the forest or fish that have left the deep pool, pitifully distressed. Each prefecture and county should be ordered to establish several dozen official estates (guanzhuang), recruiting people to rent and dwell in them, relaxing their price and requiring repayment only after three years have passed. Grouped in fives and tens in continuous succession, the fields can eventually be brought under cultivation. This is the third matter that ought to be deliberated.

These three are all grand plans for the convenience of the people; yet if perhaps they are obstructed and not carried out, in my humble opinion it is crucial to punish encroachment and usurpation. Now the powerful…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
在非所謂素封者耶俛有拾仰有取陂池
畝鍾之入不啻足也而又強據滌瀁之區
爲牧生牸所即有司清覈而有力人輒脫
籍是邇何德哉夫民富千則役萬則僕固
不足怪然不可令弱之肉强之食也誠嚴
爲之核一切影射論如法大蠹其有弭乎
愚又以爲追呼貴杜也頃令郡縣民投匭
者宿逋置不問而各社巨猾巧辦百計或
唆業主之告訐或索逃戶之糧徭朝夕叫
===
囂而民愀然歌黃鳥矣誠檄示諸長吏遍
諭吏民一切不得爲怨府而流徙可怗枕
也三議定二害除毅然必行而不沮于盈
廷築舍之說故斥鹵變爲蕃衍磽确易爲
沃野人物歸之繦至而輻輳則
國計可充也遷民如歸失業忘亡則民生可
阜也驅呰窳偷生之民而歸之農勞其筋
骨於鋤犂畚鍤之間而馴習其氣則悍俗
可革也耕作力食毋爲椎剽則萑苻可息
punctuated: 在，非所謂「素封」者耶？俛有拾、仰有取，陂池畝鍾之入，不啻足也，而又強據滌瀁之區，爲牧生牸所；即有司清覈，而有力人輒脫籍，是邇何德哉？夫民富千則役、萬則僕，固不足怪，然不可令弱之肉、强之食也。誠嚴爲之核，一切影射論如法，大蠹其有弭乎？愚又以爲追呼貴杜也。頃令郡縣民投匭者，宿逋置不問；而各社巨猾巧辦百計，或唆業主之告訐，或索逃戶之糧徭，朝夕叫囂，而民愀然歌《黃鳥》矣。誠檄示諸長吏，遍諭吏民，一切不得爲怨府，而流徙可怗枕也。三議定，二害除，毅然必行，而不沮于盈廷築舍之說；故斥鹵變爲蕃衍，磽确易爲沃野，人物歸之，繦至而輻輳，則國計可充也；遷民如歸，失業忘亡，則民生可阜也；驅呰窳偷生之民而歸之農，勞其筋骨於鋤犂畚鍤之間，而馴習其氣，則悍俗可革也；耕作力食，毋爲椎剽，則萑苻可息
translation_en:
…[powerful families (?)] are they not what are called “untitled lords”? Bending down they have things to pick up, looking up they have things to take; the income from their ponds and fields yielding a zhong per mu is more than enough. Yet they also forcibly seize vast open lands as pastures for breeding cattle. Even when the authorities conduct a thorough audit, powerful individuals always manage to evade registration—what virtue is there in being near them? Indeed, that people with a fortune of a thousand command others’ labor, and those with ten thousand command servants, is hardly surprising; yet we must not allow the weak to become the meat that the strong devour. If we truly conduct a strict audit and punish all fraudulent concealment according to the law, will this great blight not be eradicated?

I also believe that the harassment of tax dunning must be stopped. Recently, an order was given that for prefectural and county commoners who submit appeals [or return to register (?)], their past tax arrears should be set aside and not pursued. Yet the great rascals of each rural community devise a hundred clever schemes: some incite original landowners to lodge accusations, while others extort grain taxes and labor services owed by fled households. They clamor morning and night, until the people mournfully sing the “Yellow Bird” ode [of longing to flee]. If we truly issue dispatches to all the senior officials to instruct the sub-officials and commoners everywhere that they must refrain entirely from becoming sources of resentment, then the displaced migrants will be able to rest securely on their pillows.

When these three proposals are settled and these two harms eliminated, if we carry them out with resolute determination and are not deterred by the talk of a full court building a house by the roadside [endlessly debating without result], then saline marshes will turn into lush growth, and barren, stony ground will be transformed into fertile fields. People and goods will return to them, arriving in continuous streams and converging like spokes at a hub; thus the state finances can be replenished. When resettled people feel as though they have come home, and those who lost their livelihoods forget their displacement, the people’s livelihood can be made abundant. When lazy, shiftless people who merely scrape by are driven back to agriculture, working their sinews and bones among hoes, plows, baskets, and spades so as to tame and accustom their temperaments, violent customs can be reformed. And when they till the soil and eat by their own strength rather than engaging in robbery and pillage, banditry in the marshes can be brought to rest…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
也抑余尤有說焉魯君以東野畢之善御
問顏回回對曰善則善矣而馬將佚也君
問何以知之顏回曰臣聞造父不窮馬力
是以無佚馬東野畢之御馬力盡矣而求
馬不已臣以是知之嗟乎
今天下之民之力猶馬也
皇上屢下
德音有司視爲文具利未及興害愈甚惠未及
溥擾愈甚有子曰百姓足君孰與不足是
===
以聖王尚可以便民山林川澤與民共之
而後世王者往往與民爭利至于與民爭
利而民力窮矣誠推廣
德意而行之以實心實政天下無難理也
punctuated: 也。抑余尤有說焉。魯君以東野畢之善御問顏回，回對曰：「善則善矣，而馬將佚也。」君問：「何以知之？」顏回曰：「臣聞造父不窮馬力，是以無佚馬。東野畢之御，馬力盡矣，而求馬不已，臣以是知之。」嗟乎！今天下之民之力，猶馬也。皇上屢下德音，有司視爲文具，利未及興，害愈甚；惠未及溥，擾愈甚。有子曰：「百姓足，君孰與不足？」是以聖王尚可以便民，山林川澤與民共之。而後世王者往往與民爭利，至于與民爭利，而民力窮矣。誠推廣德意，而行之以實心實政，天下無難理也。
translation_en:
… [may be] stilled.

Yet I have something further to say. The ruler of Lu asked Yan Hui 顏回 about Dongye Bi's 東野畢 skill in driving horses. Hui replied: "Skillful he is indeed, yet his horses are about to bolt." The ruler asked: "How do you know this?" Yan Hui said: "Your servant has heard that Zaofu 造父 did not exhaust his horses' strength, and therefore had no bolting horses. In Dongye Bi's driving, the horses' strength is exhausted, yet he demands of the horses without cease. By this your servant knows it." Alas! Today the strength of the people of the realm is just like that of horses. His Majesty repeatedly issues benevolent decrees, yet the authorities treat them as mere formalities. Before benefits have been promoted, harms grow ever worse; before favors have been broadly extended, disturbances grow ever worse. Master You 有子 said: "If the common people have enough, with whom could the ruler lack enough?" Therefore, as long as something can convenience the people, sage kings share the mountains, forests, streams, and marshes with the people. Yet the rulers of later ages often compete with the people for profit, and when it comes to competing with the people for profit, the people's strength is exhausted. If we truly broaden and extend His Majesty's benevolent intentions and carry them out with sincere hearts and substantive governance, there will be no difficulty in bringing order to the realm.

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
山東鄉試錄後序
萬曆壬午東省大比士於鄉
延輸叨校文之役從使者諸
大夫士吏日夜悉勅以克有
成事既載賢書當屬一言其
後延輸聞徵物於府徵士於
儔物聚則良士博則儁其數
===
使之然也自孔子以文行立
教孟軻氏遵而修之由是齊
魯之間於文學若出天性而
史稱諸儒質行謂其治官民
皆有廉節稱其好學豈非先
賢聖之遺迹而人士之儔與
國家以明經修行網羅天下才
punctuated:
山東鄉試錄後序

萬曆壬午，東省大比士於鄉。延輸叨校文之役，從使者、諸大夫、士吏日夜悉勅，以克有成事。既載賢書，當屬一言其後。

延輸聞：徵物於府，徵士於儔。物聚則良，士博則儁，其數使之然也。自孔子以文行立教，孟軻氏遵而修之，由是齊、魯之間於文學若出天性；而史稱諸儒質行，謂其治官民皆有廉節，稱其好學。豈非先賢聖之遺迹，而人士之儔與？國家以明經、修行網羅天下才
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shandong Provincial Examination

In the renwu year of the Wanli era (1582), the eastern province of Shandong held the triennial Provincial Examination to select scholars. I, Yanshu, was undeservedly assigned the task of examining the essays, and following the imperial emissaries, grandees, scholars, and functionaries, worked diligently day and night to bring the matter to successful completion. Now that the roster of worthy candidates has been compiled for publication, it falls to me to compose a postface at its end.

I have heard that one seeks goods in storehouses and seeks scholars among their peers. Where goods are gathered in abundance, the finest are found; where scholars are numerous, the most outstanding emerge—such is the natural principle of things. Ever since Confucius established his teachings on letters and conduct, and Meng Ke (Mencius) followed and cultivated them, the people of the Qi and Lu regions have taken to literature and learning as if by innate nature. Furthermore, the histories praise the upright conduct of their Confucian scholars, noting that in governing officials and commoners alike they possessed integrity and restraint, worthy of their reputation for loving learning. Is this not the enduring legacy of the former sages and worthies, and the fellowship of scholars from which talent is drawn? The Dynasty nets the talented and wise of the realm through their mastery of the Classics and cultivation of conduct…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
哲
聲教翔洽湛浸八區僻陬裔土
稱說孔孟之指六藝之科晻
然若合符節矧齊魯經術所
由興於古昔豈異焉嚮者觀
子多士所論著咸各綜述訓
典原本性命類道德之統而
===
晢王伯之塗于文則斌斌矣
質行何如哉夫市函於燕非
不精也而弗服不知其堅市
鏄於粵非不瑩也而弗御不
知其利齊魯信士之燕粵然
售而弗試亦安敢知其良楛
顧士有豫辨者耳蓋孔子論
punctuated: 哲。聲教翔洽，湛浸八區。僻陬裔土，稱說孔孟之指、六藝之科，晻然若合符節。矧齊魯經術所由興，於古昔豈異焉？嚮者觀子多士所論著，咸各綜述訓典，原本性命，類道德之統而晢王伯之塗，于文則斌斌矣，質行何如哉？夫市函於燕，非不精也，而弗服不知其堅；市鏄於粵，非不瑩也，而弗御不知其利。齊魯信士之燕粵，然售而弗試，亦安敢知其良楛？顧士有豫辨者耳。蓋孔子論
translation_en: …wise. Moral prestige and transformative instruction soar and spread, deeply steeping the eight regions of the realm. Even in remote corners and borderlands, when people expound the teachings of Confucius and Mencius and the disciplines of the Six Arts, they agree uniformly as if matching the halves of a tally. How much more so in Qi and Lu, where classical learning originated—how could it differ today from antiquity? Just now, upon examining the essays composed by you gentlemen, I saw that all of you comprehensively expounded the canonical precepts, traced things back to human nature and destiny, categorized the lineage of the Way and virtue, and clearly distinguished the paths of the True King and the Hegemon. In terms of literary culture, they are resplendent indeed; yet how do things stand with your substantive conduct? Now, when one buys armor in Yan, it is not that it lacks fine craftsmanship, yet without wearing it one cannot know its sturdiness; when one buys a blade in Yue, it is not that it lacks a bright sheen, yet without wielding it one cannot know its sharpness. Qi and Lu are truly the Yan and Yue of scholars; yet if they are selected without being tested in practice, how can one dare claim to know whether they are of sound or inferior quality? Still, there is that which scholars must discern in advance. For when Confucius discussed…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
學先志而別白君子小人之
分決諸義利孟軻氏干說世
主首以仁義與利洮汰其惑
而論士亦曰尚志子多士所
熟數也今
主上備藉太平右文嗜士有司羣
吏執鈞綳而求之如恐不及
===
得則籍之賢書函采聲詩推
轂勸駕榮燿道路雲煜閈閎
此先賢聖所不逢於世也士
即塵芥聲榮亦安有不灑然
自適者哉顧此其時意念何
居耳於乎此志隆汙所由辨
矣曰士之所不朽者名居則
punctuated: 學先志，而別白君子、小人之分，決諸義、利；孟軻氏干說世主，首以仁義與利洮汰其惑，而論士亦曰「尚志」，子多士所熟數也。今主上備藉太平，右文嗜士，有司羣吏執鈞綳而求之，如恐不及；得則籍之賢書，函采聲詩，推轂勸駕，榮燿道路，雲煜閈閎，此先賢聖所不逢於世也。士即塵芥聲榮，亦安有不灑然自適者哉？顧此其時意念何居耳。於乎！此志隆汙所由辨矣。曰：「士之所不朽者名。」居則
translation_en:
…learning prioritized aspiration, and in clearly distinguishing between the noble man and the petty man, he decided the matter upon rightness versus profit. When Meng Ke [Mencius] sought audiences to persuade the rulers of his age, he began by using benevolence and rightness versus profit to wash away their delusions, and in discussing scholars he likewise said, "Exalt your aspiration." All of this is something with which you many scholars are thoroughly familiar.

Today our Sovereign fully enjoys the inheritance of Great Peace, esteems civil culture, and cherishes scholars. The authorities and assembled officials hold out the standard and measure [?] to seek them, as if fearing they might fall short. Once found, their names are inscribed in the Roster of the Worthy; they are feasted with the recitation of the Odes; their carriage wheels are pushed forward as they are urged to set out for the capital; glory illuminates the roads, and brilliance shines upon the gates of their home villages. Such treatment is what the former worthies and sages never encountered in their own times! Even if a scholar regards reputation and glory as mere dust and chaff, how could he not feel briskly gratified and at ease? Yet the question is simply where his thoughts and intentions abide at such a moment. Alas! Herein lies the distinction between whether one's aspiration is lofty or base.

Someone may say, "That by which a scholar achieves immortality is his reputation." When dwelling in retirement, he…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
好修强學蚤夜不解幸而遭
際
明盛載軍質服官效尺寸之功於世
聲流鍾鼎而烈烈著乎春秋以
是爲愉快固亦有之其伏在
蓬藋居約處阨一日俠然名
列
===
天府即且緤組彯纓都華彌寵顯
施先世慶流支屬爲之滿志
固亦有之嗟夫此所謂義與
利之間也而效可前睹矣蓋
使志規於義則其出也進不
敢比周以事主退不敢營私
以自殖奉官守法不飾短長
punctuated: 好修强學，蚤夜不解，幸而遭際明盛，載軍質服官，效尺寸之功於世，聲流鍾鼎而烈烈著乎春秋，以是爲愉快，固亦有之；其伏在蓬藋，居約處阨，一日俠然名列天府，即且緤組彯纓，都華彌寵，顯施先世，慶流支屬，爲之滿志，固亦有之。嗟夫！此所謂義與利之間也，而效可前睹矣。蓋使志規於義，則其出也，進不敢比周以事主，退不敢營私以自殖，奉官守法，不飾短長，
translation_en: …cherish moral cultivation and strive in study, never slacking from morning to night, and when by good fortune they encounter an enlightened and flourishing age, they present their pledge of allegiance [?] and take up office, rendering some small measure of meritorious service to the world, so that their fame is inscribed on bells and tripods and their illustrious deeds are recorded in the annals—those who take delight in this certainly exist. On the other hand, there are those who lie hidden among the brambles and weeds, living in poverty and distress, and when one day their names are suddenly [?] placed on the register of the Imperial Treasury, they thereupon bind on official sashes and flutter their cap-strings, basking in splendor and brimming with favor, extending glory to their ancestors and letting blessings flow to their kin—those who feel fully satisfied with this certainly also exist. Alas! This is what is meant by the distinction between righteousness and profit, and its effects can be foreseen. For if a man's ambition is guided by righteousness, then when he goes forth into service, in advancing at court he will not dare form partisan cliques to serve his ruler, and in retiring he will not dare pursue private gain to enrich himself; he will uphold his office and abide by the law, without disguising his shortcomings or exaggerating his strengths, …

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
國事揆策不慮夷險恥實不
懋不恥不工恥職不修不恥
不捷若此者卽未必盡非凡
絕世之材然專志一節修實
而效之上循將有得士之益
焉何也則其所志者義也假
令希世階寵追趣逐嗜曲學
===
以偶時飾褒以熒衆巧文以
規便漂說以養交矯性以博
名鑿空以合變睆然在經繼
之中波流茅靡而不知所止
若此者卽雖有瓌奇可喜之
迹而積習所生使天下陰受
其敝元氣損而不知何也則
punctuated: 國事揆策，不慮夷險；恥實不懋，不恥不工；恥職不修，不恥不捷。若此者，卽未必盡非凡絕世之材，然專志一節，修實而效之，上循將有得士之益焉。何也？則其所志者義也。假令希世階寵，追趣逐嗜，曲學以偶時，飾褒以熒衆，巧文以規便，漂說以養交，矯性以博名，鑿空以合變，睆然在經繼之中，波流茅靡而不知所止。若此者，卽雖有瓌奇可喜之迹，而積習所生，使天下陰受其敝，元氣損而不知。何也？則
translation_en:
…in devising policies for state affairs, they do not calculate whether the path is smooth or perilous; they are ashamed when their substance is not diligent, not when their craft is unpolished; they are ashamed when their duties are neglected, not when they fail to be nimble. Men such as these, even if they are not necessarily all talents of extraordinary, peerless caliber, nevertheless focus their resolve and maintain single-minded integrity, cultivating substance and offering it in service, so that the ruler will accordingly reap the benefit of having obtained true scholars. Why is this? It is because what they set their minds upon is righteousness.

Suppose instead that they flatter the world to climb to favor, chasing trends and pursuing cravings: twisting their learning to suit the times, adorning praise to dazzle the multitude, crafting artful words to angle for advantage, peddling floating talk to cultivate connections, forcing their nature to win renown, and fabricating empty theories to match changing circumstances—gazing about complacently amidst their toils and entanglements [?], swept along like waves and flattened like reeds without knowing where to stop. Men such as these, even though they may show traces of striking and pleasing brilliance, through the habits they accumulate cause the empire to secretly suffer their harm, its vital energy impaired without anyone realizing it. Why is this? It is because…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
志規於利而純白渝也然則
路岐於咫尺而跡懸於秦楚
故志不可不蚤辨矣
主上念士習日靡傷平中之化
詔有司校文剖覈胥用淳和爲質
返之素樸乃士所由趣舍起
於一念藉使義利之辨不審
===
即隨時雅化猶之逃兩無之
而不濡故在辨其志而已語
有之素之質白染之以涅則
黑縑之質黃染之以丹則赤
性非好漸也其所豫者鮮也
乃若玉生而堅蘭生而芳素
有其質久而愈彰物惡能渝
punctuated: 志規於利，而純白渝也。然則路岐於咫尺，而跡懸於秦楚，故志不可不蚤辨矣。主上念士習日靡，傷平中之化，詔有司校文剖覈，胥用淳和爲質，返之素樸。乃士所由趣舍，起於一念；藉使義利之辨不審，即隨時雅化，猶之逃兩，無之而不濡，故在辨其志而已。語有之：「素之質白，染之以涅則黑；縑之質黃，染之以丹則赤。」性非好漸也，其所豫者鮮也。乃若玉生而堅，蘭生而芳，素有其質，久而愈彰，物惡能渝
translation_en: … their aims are fixed upon profit, and their pure whiteness is sullied. Thus, though the paths diverge by a mere foot, their tracks end up as far apart as Qin and Chu; therefore, one's aims cannot but be discerned early on. His Majesty, mindful that the habits of scholars grow daily more decadent to the detriment of balanced and moderate transformation, has decreed that the authorities, in evaluating essays and making rigorous assessments, should all take pure harmony as the substance and return things to unadorned simplicity. Yet the direction a scholar chooses to pursue or reject arises from a single thought; even if they adapt to the refined transformation of the times, should their discernment between righteousness and profit remain unexamined, it would be like fleeing the rain [?]—nowhere can one go without getting drenched. Therefore, it lies simply in discerning their aims. As the saying goes: "The substance of plain silk is white, yet dyed with alum-mud it turns black; the substance of fine silk is yellow, yet dyed with cinnabar it turns red." It is not that their nature loves to be steeped, but that what they have prepared in advance is slight. By contrast, jade is born hard and the orchid is born fragrant; possessing their substance inherently, they become all the more manifest with time—how could external things ever sully…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text:
之故志誠蚤辨卽日溷於聲
利而無所紛華涉世之态态
而不汲溺此孔孟之要眇而
上所欲與士更始也聞之一夫挽
强百夫決拾一人持器千人
臨淵貴其倡也爲天下倡宜
莫如東人士其相與蚤辨之
===
俾聲實相中而言行毋相踰
使人謂齊魯經儒信能有其
文質修先賢聖之業不攺于
以風厲四方則天下之函皆
燕而鎛皆粤也尚安所試而
知士勉之矣
浙江杭州府昌化縣儒學敎
punctuated:
之？故志誠蚤辨，卽日溷於聲利而無所紛華，涉世之态态而不汲溺。此孔、孟之要眇，而上所欲與士更始也。聞之：一夫挽强，百夫決拾；一人持器，千人臨淵。貴其倡也。爲天下倡，宜莫如東人。士其相與蚤辨之，俾聲實相中而言行毋相踰，使人謂齊、魯經儒信能有其文質，修先賢聖之業不攺，于以風厲四方，則天下之函皆燕而鎛皆粤也。尚安所試而知？士勉之矣！
浙江杭州府昌化縣儒學敎
translation_en:
… it? Therefore, if one's aspiration is truly discerned early on, even if one is daily immersed in fame and profit, one will not be dazzled by ostentation; though bustling through the affairs of the world, one will not be drowned in them. This is the profound essence of Confucius and Mencius, and it is how His Majesty wishes to make a fresh start with the scholars. I have heard it said: when one man draws a strong bow, a hundred men put on their thumb-rings and arm-guards; when one man holds the fishing gear, a thousand men approach the deep pool. What is valued is taking the lead. In taking the lead for the realm, none are more suited than the men of the East [Shandong]. May you scholars join together in discerning this early on, so that reputation and reality correspond to each other and words and deeds do not transgress one another. Cause people to say that the classical scholars of Qi and Lu truly possess both cultural refinement and substantial quality, cultivating the legacy of the former worthies and sages without alteration, thereby inspiring the four quarters. Then all the armor in the realm will be as fine as that of Yan, and all the hoes as fine as those of Yue. What further need would there be to test in order to know them? Scholars, strive at this!

Instructor of the Confucian School of Changhua County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang…

title: 萬曆十年山東鄉試錄
text: 謝郭兆□謹序
punctuated: 謝郭兆□謹序。
translation_en: … Instructor (謝 [for 諭?]), Guo Zhao[?] (郭兆□), respectfully writes this postface.
